title: Price the CH4 and N2O the radiation cannot carry
description:
Price the CH4 and N2O the radiation cannot carry, at THIS star's mixing ratios rather than Earth's, and report whether `derive_design_flux.py` is absorbing the difference

Source: `config/planet.yaml` atmosphere block, `notes/audits/absent-and-inherited-physics.md` finding 5
notes:
From archive/tasks.md closing note:
done 2026-08-20, and it is the LARGEST item in the error budget by a wide margin: +2.25 to +5.26 W/m2, against mineral dust's +0.34 to +0.61 which stood second, and against 2.02 W/m2 for Earth's own CH4 and N2O by the same calculation. Etminan et al. (2016) could only bound it, being valid to 3500 ppb of CH4 and 525 ppb of N2O with this world above both ceilings; Byrne and Goldblatt (2014) cover 100 ppbv to 100 ppmv and settle it, and the two agree to 3.5% where both are valid. THE REMAINING WIDTH IS NOT THE RADIATIVE CALCULATION, which two independent methods fix to a few percent: it is a disagreement about whether tropospheric N2O is enhanced at all, and that is CLIM-43. THE MIXING RATIOS ARE THE FINDING. Segura et al. (2003) was already on disk and read, already supplying `star.surface_uv_relative_to_earth` and `model.ozone_scale`, and its p. 701 says CH4 and N2O are "systematically higher for the K2V planet ... because of the difference in stellar UV fluxes", at the same modern-Earth surface fluxes: same biology, less near-UV, slower photolysis, longer lifetimes. Read off Fig. 12a at 1 PAL against Fig. 4 as calibration, a factor of 2 to 5 on both gases, with two independent checks that the figure reading is sound -- Fig. 4's Sun values reproduce modern Earth, and the text's "of the order of 20 ppm" at 0.1 PAL matches where Fig. 12a's peak reads. Gravity is applied and cuts the other way: 1 bar at 12.81 m/s2 makes a mixing ratio 0.756 of Earth's column, the same 23% the other absorbers already carry correctly. Two caveats pull opposite ways and are recorded rather than resolved: Segura's K2V is 4620 K against this host's 4965 K, and this star is DECLARED active where Segura's is a quiet modelled one, which puts near-UV back -- so `surface_uv_relative_to_earth` and this both rest on one assumption about the star's UV, and the activity declaration is in tension with it. AND THE DESIGN FLUX IS ABSORBING IT, by construction: `derive_design_flux.py` searches flux to meet thresholds on the modelled climate, so a missing greenhouse term is met with more starlight. The climate is not wrong; the ATTRIBUTION is, and the residual moves to everything keyed on insolation rather than temperature -- photosynthetically active flux, the shortwave band split, the aerosol forcings, the reported surface UV -- all with one sign. `exoplasim/notes/trace-gas-absorbers.md` carries it; adding the band is CLIM-42
close_reason: done 2026-08-20, and it is the LARGEST item in the error budget by a wide margin: +2.25 to +5.26 W/m2, against mineral dust's +0.34 to +0.61 which stood second, and against 2.02 W/m2 for Earth's own CH4 and N2O by the same calculation.

title: Add a CH4 and N2O band to the longwave. config/planet.yaml says the shape
description:
Add a CH4 and N2O band to the longwave. `config/planet.yaml` says the shape of it -- "adding either means adding a band, not a key" -- and CLIM-41 measured that the term outranks every other item in the budget

Source: `exoplasim/notes/trace-gas-band.md`, `exoplasim/analysis/trace_gas_band_model.json`, `exoplasim/analysis/co2_overlap_589.json`
notes:
From archive/tasks.md closing note:
done 2026-08-20. Three bands on Donner and Ramanathan (1980) in `radmod.f90`: CH4 1306 and N2O 1285 overlapped by water vapour through the `zth2o` the routine already computes, N2O 589 overlapped by CO2 through a correlated-k fit cross-checked against Ramanathan (1976) Appendix A. Band intensities are a MATCHED TRIPLE with `A0` and `beta0`, so CH4's is recovered from the paper's own Table 2 and N2O's two from McClatchey, the compilation it cites. All four declared tests pass: the zero-abundance reduction identity is bit-identical on restart, output and snapshot over a segment crossing two writes; sign and monotonicity hold; 100 ppmv produces no NaN; and the term lowers global mean OLR by **0.799 W/m2**, which is 40% of the offline pricing and exactly what this scheme returns for CO2 against a line-by-line answer -- its whole CO2 greenhouse is 12.28 W/m2. **That comparison was later withdrawn**: the Earth figures it was held against were quoted from general knowledge, never sourced, and are an ATTRIBUTION with band overlap shared out rather than the REMOVAL measured here. Checked properly instead, every step of the chain is verified against a line list -- CH4's band absorptance within 7% of HITRAN 2020, the narrow-band Planck conversion to 1.004, and Sasamori's own CO2 absorptivity 0.175 against a line-list 0.165 -- so no defect is identified anywhere and what remains is two estimates of one quantity differing by 2.5x, priced as a disagreement in `analysis/error_budget.json`. **THE LAST DAY OF IT WAS ONE MISSING `mpbcr`.** `ch4` and `n2o` went into `radmod_nl` and not into `radini`'s broadcast block, so they kept their default of zero on every rank but the root and the band ran on eight polar latitude rows and nowhere else -- measuring 0.0175 instead of 0.799. Invisible: no warning, the run completes, `plasim_diag` echoes the values because that prints on NROOT too, and the symptom looks like weak physics. It was chased as physics through a Doppler-broadening hypothesis (Cess 1973 fetched, read, and it does not apply -- its branch is below Lorentz at every level here), a shortwave hypothesis, and a supposed 40x contradiction between two perturbations that were identical. What found it was dumping the flux PER RANK: exact zeros on seven of eight. Two things the false trails left standing: the band model is validated against HITRAN 2020 to better than 7% at every level, and the scheme's own CO2 calibration is measured. Failure-modes has the class; `config/planet.yaml` now declares the mixing ratios

title: Settle whether TROPOSPHERIC N2O is enhanced at this star
description:
Settle whether TROPOSPHERIC N2O is enhanced at this star, which is the whole width of the CH4/N2O budget item: read Rugheimer et al. (2013) Fig. 7's per-grid-star surface mixing ratios at its 5000 K point, which is this host to within 35 K

Source: `exoplasim/notes/trace-gas-absorbers.md` section 3
notes:
From archive/tasks.md closing note:
done 2026-08-20, and it settles CH4 as well as N2O. The paper is a vector PDF, so Fig. 7 was extracted as PATH COORDINATES rather than read off a log axis: `analysis/trace_gas_forcing.py` parses the content stream, matches each curve to its legend colour and converts through the panel's own tick calibration. **The 5000 K grid point reads 1.600 ppmv of CH4 and 0.300 ppmv of N2O -- the Sun case's values on both gases.** Neither is enhanced. THE TWO SOURCES NEVER DISAGREED: the enhancement is real and turns on between 4750 K (1.600 ppmv CH4) and 4500 K (37.27), and Segura's K2V is 4620 K, INSIDE that transition, while this host at 4965 K is above it. The apparent conflict was a comparison between stars 345 K apart. It also closes the quiet-star caveat the estimate carried, because epsilon Eridani is Rugheimer's own 5000 K grid star and is what this world's activity is modelled on -- though `star.surface_uv_relative_to_earth` still rests on the quiet-star calculation and now does so alone. Budget item goes from (2.25, 5.26) to (1.56, 1.98) W/m2 against 2.02 for Earth's own; it stays the largest single term, and is below Earth's only because 1 bar at 12.81 m/s2 is 0.756 of Earth's column. What outranks everything is now the TERM rather than the uncertainty in it, which is CLIM-42. Byrne and Goldblatt's fits are checked four ways and the script raises on each: branch continuity at 2.5 ppmv, the paper's 100 ppmv maxima, Earth's known industrial-era forcings, and the extracted Sun curve against Rugheimer's separately stated Sun-case numbers (1% on N2O, 8% on CH4)
close_reason: done 2026-08-20, and it settles CH4 as well as N2O.

title: The model is not run-to-run reproducible, and nothing owns
description:
The model is not run-to-run reproducible, and nothing owns it: the SAME binary on identical inputs gives bit-identical output at 1 timestep and differs by 16, and `plasim_status` differs between two runs even at 1 timestep, so a bitwise restart diff reports nothing

Source: `notes/audits/model-reproducibility.md`, `exoplasim/analysis/reproducibility_matrix.json`
notes:
From archive/tasks.md closing note:
done 2026-08-20, and the premise is REFUTED. A declared factorial -- 8 and 16 ranks, output off and at the production setting, segments crossing no write and two, three repeats each -- comes out bit-identical in `plasim_status`, `plasim_output`, `plasim_snapshot` and the model half of `plasim_diag` in every measurable cell. **The rank count is what is not free**: 8 against 16 ranks differ in 83 of 199 restart records, at round-off and growing, so an A/B must hold it fixed and a bracket at one rank count is not comparable to a control at another. The comfortable explanation was refuted by accident: the first pass ran on the binaries a run directory had frozen, which still carry the `zsolars` overread, and it reproduces THERE TOO -- so the overread is deterministic under `-finit-real=zero` and is a source of rank-dependence, not of run-to-run difference. What is left of the original observation is that its control could not have shown it: a gridpoint record is written on `mod(nstep, nafter) == 0` over the ABSOLUTE step count, and on the production restart neither a 1-step nor a 16-step segment reaches one. Two traps are now closed in code rather than in prose -- `plasim_diag`'s resource block is filtered from the source that writes it rather than from a diff, since every line of it is conditional on a non-zero counter; and the harness hashes a bed's executables against `binary_manifest.json`, because `--verify` answers whether the INSTALLED binaries are current and cannot answer whether the bed is running them. Consequence: bit-identity is available again, at a fixed rank count, and CLIM-39's reduction identity needs re-taking as CLIM-45
close_reason: done 2026-08-20, and the premise is REFUTED.

title: Re-take CLIM-39's REDUCTION IDENTITY, which CLIM-44 showed was stated at a horizon that writes
description:
Re-take CLIM-39's REDUCTION IDENTITY, which CLIM-44 showed was stated at a horizon that writes no gridpoint output: same configuration through a base-built binary and the multi-species one, at a segment length chosen against the write cadence and at a fixed rank count

Source: `notes/audits/model-reproducibility.md`, `aeolian/notes/multi-species-aerosol.md` section 8
notes:
From archive/tasks.md closing note:
done 2026-08-20, **and the identity FAILS** -- not in a way that invalidates the change, but the recorded claim of bit-identity is wrong. Re-taken with the three things the original lacked: 56 timesteps so `plasim_output` holds 13.4 MB rather than nothing, a fixed rank count, and the aerosol ACTUALLY ACTIVE at `ndustrad = 1`, since at zero both code paths skip it and would agree for no reason. Against a binary built from `66dbcf0` in a throwaway worktree. The two differ FROM THE FIRST TIMESTEP at a few ulps -- 1.3e-14 on `dust3`, 6.2e-12 on cloud cover -- amplifying to 4.4e-10 by 56 steps, the same magnitude CLIM-44 measured between 8 and 16 ranks. The order-1 differences in `plasim_output` are all 460-485 diagnostic codes and one of them, 482, is identically zero in the old build: a per-species diagnostic the old code does not populate. So the change is answer-preserving to ROUND-OFF and not to the bit, and an A/B crossing this commit must be read at the round-off bound. Where the ulp comes from is NOT what the patch header predicted: the `knz == 1` fast path is present and correct, and the optical-depth and band-2 lines are operand-for-operand identical to the old ones. The two-stream restructure is the remaining candidate and is not pinned, which is not worth doing at 1e-14. Bed caveats stated in the note: the prescribed field is synthetic and `DUSTQLW` is a test input, neither of which the identity depends on
close_reason: done 2026-08-20, **and the identity FAILS** -- not in a way that invalidates the change, but the recorded claim of bit-identity is wrong.

title: Store the Legendre weights as P and Q alone. legini builds EIGHT NCSP x NLPP matrices
description:
Store the Legendre weights as P and Q alone. `legini` builds EIGHT `NCSP x NLPP` matrices and every one is touched every timestep, which is 48.4 MB a die at T127 and 114.9 MB at T170 against CCD0's 96 MB of L3 and CCD1's 32 MB -- and that footprint is the measured cause of a 10.5 point load imbalance that makes CCD1 the critical path at both resolutions. All eight are P or Q times a per-MODE factor and a per-LATITUDE factor, both separable and neither needing an `NCSP x NLPP` array, so storing two matrices instead of eight leaves 12.1 MB and 28.7 MB a die and both fit CCD1. It is the exact inverse of the filter fold, which moved a per-mode scalar INTO the matrices to save one multiply in three and returned 1.6% because those loops are bound by streaming the matrices rather than by the multiplier; the same sentence read backwards is the argument for this

Source: `exoplasim/notes/rank-imbalance-and-weight-traffic.md`, `exoplasim/notes/legendre-filter-fold.md`
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
open. It is a reassociation, so restart shas move and it needs `compare_restarts.py` at a declared tolerance with a control, as the symmetry work did. Two things to establish before believing the prize: whether the extra per-mode vector read costs the inner loops their vectorisation, and whether anything survives at T21 and T42 where the matrices already fit [step: rebuild_binaries, baseline_run] IN THE OPTIMISATION WORKTREE'S SCOPE, on CLIM-61's precedent: this is the same problem space that worktree is working in, so the reassociation may already be done or made moot there. The merging session owns reconciling this row.
close_reason:
Built, measured and refused, and the roadmap already carried the verdict this row did not. exoplasim/notes/non-mpi-performance-roadmap.md section 1: implemented in full, correct, four times smaller (114.9 MB a die to about 36 at T170, 15.1 MB a thread to 4.5, under the 32 MB target) and 1.56% SLOWER on the threaded build at T170 -- 80.57 s against 81.66 s, paired and interleaved, faster in 0 of 4 rounds, [-2.17, -0.74]. The code is reverted; verify_weight_factorisation_model.sh is kept and agreed with the eight-matrix build to 4.8e-13 at one step and 1.06e-11 at twenty against a 1e-10 bar declared before the arms ran.

THE PREMISE WAS BACKWARDS. The route was ranked first because the filter fold returned 1.6%, read as evidence these loops are bound by streaming the weight matrices. Undoing the fold costs the same 1.6% back, and the reading that fits both numbers is that they are bound by the MULTIPLY. A second measurement agrees: at NPRO=1 one thread streams 30 MB of pmat and 30 MB of qmat per transform against 1.88 MB at NPRO=16, and the two time the same, 1.45 ms against 1.48.

SHTns has since removed the matrices altogether, computing the Legendre functions on the fly and storing no NCSP x NLPP array, which takes pmat and qmat out of cache_budget.py entirely. The cache-boundary finding in rank-imbalance-and-weight-traffic.md still stands; what no longer stands is that this is the way to act on it.

Closed WONTFIX. Reopen only if a resolution above T170 makes the memory headroom worth a small speed loss. The row stayed open because a71cc1bc pointed it at the merging worktree and the merge (85de8f85) never reconciled it.

title: Read the 103 implicitly SAVEd procedure-body declarations in plasim/src and classify each
description:
Read the 103 implicitly SAVEd procedure-body declarations in `plasim/src` and classify each as intended persistent state, harmless write-before-read, or a defect. The thread port tripped exactly one of them and the other 102 have never been examined. Under `-fopenmp` a SAVEd local is SHARED by every thread, demonstrated at seven of eight threads reading a value another thread wrote, while under MPI each rank is a process and its SAVEd locals are private by construction. So this class is reachable under threads and unreachable under ranks, and source that has only ever run under ranks has never exercised it. gfortran reports nothing at any warning level tried, so there is no flag that shortens this and it is reading

Source: `notes/audits/uninitialised-reads-and-implicit-save.md` finding 2
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
open. 103 is a POPULATION and not a defect count; the row closes on every site being classified, not on every site being changed. `plasim_dummy.f90` at 18, `icemod.f90` and `icemod_template.f90` at 14 each and `hurricanemod.f90` at 13 are over half of it [step: rebuild_binaries]

title: Settle the offline glacier accelerator: newsnow.x and buildice.x are built by ExoPlaSim's own
description:
Settle the offline glacier accelerator: `newsnow.x` and `buildice.x` are built by ExoPlaSim's own `configure.sh` and consume `newdsnow`, `newxsnow`, `lsm` and `persist`, which `glaciermod.f90:610-619` writes at the end of every model call and which every glacier-enabled run this project has made has produced and nobody has ever read. `newsnow` extrapolates a five-year snow tendency forward by a declared interval where snow is shrinking or has persisted a full year, which makes it the only device in the tree for reaching an equilibrium ice sheet inside an affordable run -- the land-ice counterpart of `NCVEG`. Both programs hardcode `NLAT = 32, NLON = 64`, so they are T21 and would silently misread a T42 field, and `buildice`'s uniform 400 m over land is an initialiser for a planet whose ice sheets are already known

Source: `notes/audits/dormant-exoplasim-modules.md` finding 5, `notes/glacier-rough-pass.md`
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
open, and it is a verdict rather than an implementation: generalise the extrapolator to the resolution ladder and declare what the acceleration is valid for, adopt it as a step in `config/pipeline.yaml` with the model calls it sits between, or state that the four fields are deliberately unconsumed and why. Deleting the loop is a legitimate close. Read with DUST-14, which puts a deposition term on the same ice the accelerator would grow [step: bootstrap_run, baseline_run]. AMENDED 2026-08-22: PALADYN's equilibrium spinup mode is the WORKED EXAMPLE of the verdict this row asks for. It runs vegetation and carbon at an artificial 1000-year internal step, possible only because those components are fully implicit, reaches near equilibrium in about 100 simulated years instead of 10,000, and then states what it is NOT valid for -- processes intrinsically out of equilibrium, naming peatlands and inert permafrost carbon, which need a transient run instead. That is the shape of the answer: not whether the accelerator is correct, but what it is valid for and what has to be integrated honestly. Three devices of this class now sit in reach and one is unrun. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 3c. THIS ROW IS UPSTREAM OF ANY FLOW QUESTION and that ordering is deliberate. `newsnow` grows ice without moving it, which is the cheaper test of whether ice persists for a year at all, and flow is not needed until it does. A shallow-ice model run before PHYS-13's mask exists would be fed a surface mass balance built on orography that evaluates high ground about 7.8 K too warm on average, so it would return zero ice confidently and for the wrong reason. Sequence: PHYS-13, then this row, then whether flow is wanted. A FOURTH DEVICE AND A THIRD IDIOM, 2026-08-22, which bears on what this row's verdict should SAY. cGENIE's GEMlite accelerates by CYCLING -- `gem_notyr` ordinary years, then an accelerated stretch, repeat -- rather than by a single long jump. That is more conservative than PALADYN's 1000-year internal timestep or `newsnow`'s forward extrapolation of a five-year tendency, because the full model periodically re-establishes the state the accelerated component was drifting from, so it is valid under weaker assumptions. Worth knowing before choosing a shape for `newsnow`. AND ALL FOUR STATE THEIR INVALIDITY, which is the property this row is really asking to reproduce: PALADYN's mode excludes processes intrinsically out of equilibrium, GEMlite's cannot handle a transient CO2 pulse because it needs surface-to-atmosphere disequilibrium, and `newsnow` extrapolates only where snow already exists and is shrinking or has persisted. The device is never the deliverable; the statement of what it is valid for is. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 26a. THE GUARD PATTERN FOR AN ACCELERATOR, 2026-08-22, if this one is kept. cGENIE controls its geochemical accelerator by two thresholds and a counter -- engage only when a drift RATE is below `gem_adapt_dpCO2dt`, extend only while an accumulated ERROR stays below `gem_adapt_DpCO2`, and refuse to run unbounded by default with the reason written beside the switch. It also STATES ITS OWN DOMAIN OF VALIDITY in the module header rather than leaving it to be found: GEMlite works on slow equilibration and explicitly fails on a CO2 pulse. Whatever this row settles, an accelerator that ships here should carry both -- a declared validity domain and, if a scalar drift measure exists, the two-sided guard. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 35

title: Decide whether the baseline carries the cyclogenesis index diagnostics, NSTORMDIAG = 1
description:
Decide whether the baseline carries the cyclogenesis index diagnostics, `NSTORMDIAG = 1`, and if so read what this climate's environments say. Potential intensity, the ventilation index, the tropospheric entropy deficit, lower-atmosphere absolute vorticity and the genesis potential index are ENVIRONMENTAL indices, built to be evaluated on coarse fields because no model of this class resolves a storm, so T42 is their intended support rather than a compromise; `hurricaneini` takes `RD` from `gascon` and `absvorticity` uses the model's own `omega`, so the module is already planet-aware where most inherited physics is not. Enabling is more than the switch: codes 322 to 329 have to join `REGULAR_CODES` in `run_exoplasim.py`, pyburn already naming them, and `stormclim` has to be reapplied per segment for the CLIM-17 reason. The thresholds are Komacek et al. (2020)'s Earth calibration and are namelist keys, so a Vesper verdict means what it means only once they are re-derived or explicitly declared

Source: `notes/audits/dormant-exoplasim-modules.md` finding 3
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
open. It feeds nothing back, so it rides a segment declared `diagnostic` and costs one namelist key and a postprocessor list rather than a run of its own. The durable half is a finding about whether this world's tropical environments admit cyclogenesis at all, which survives a regeneration; a storm COUNT is not on offer at this resolution and CLIM-55 is why [step: baseline_run]

title: Keep the storm-capture half of hurricanemod recorded as a declared gap rather than an option.
description:
Keep the storm-capture half of `hurricanemod` recorded as a declared gap rather than an option. `HC_CAPTURE` hunts a RESOLVED vortex -- 33 m/s in the lower atmosphere with 20.5 m/s at the surface, over at least 30 gridcells, sustained at least 256 timesteps -- and the bar is higher here than on Earth by two compounding factors. A given truncation buys 20% coarser spacing in kilometres because the planet is 1.2 radii (375 km at T42, 188 at T85, 125 at T127, 94 at T170), and the storms are not correspondingly larger: rotation at 0.800 of Earth's raises the deformation radius while 12.81 m/s2 lowers the scale height to 0.766, for a net 0.957. Earth GCMs want roughly 50 km before cyclone-like vortices reach realistic intensity, which is about T320 on this planet

Source: `notes/audits/dormant-exoplasim-modules.md` finding 3
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
open as a DECLARED gap on DUST-16's precedent: the process is real, it is not representable at any resolution in the plan, and a storm statistic produced by turning the capture thresholds on anyway would be a property of the grid rather than of the world. It is conditional rather than wrong, which is why it is not wontfix -- the revisit condition is a target support finer than about T320, which neither loop D nor CLIM-52's converter contemplates. Until then this row is why no storm count exists, and why that absence is not a null result [step: baseline_run]

title: Write the spectral partials straight into shared storage and let mpsumsc reduce them in place
description:
Write the spectral partials straight into shared storage and let `mpsumsc` reduce them in place, which is Stage B of the plan `exoplasim/notes/shared-spectral-state.md` describes. Stage A shared the spectral STATE and took the threaded build from -18.9% to -11.22% at T127 and from -25.7% to -20.66% at T170, sixteen threads against sixteen ranks. A profile by shared object, converted to seconds against the measured medians, accounts for the remainder to within 5%: at T127 the model's own code is identical to 0.04 s, dropping the MPI stack SAVES 4.03 s, and the staging copy in libc COSTS 8.28 s; at T170 the same three terms are +6.57 s, -12.97 s and +21.58 s. So the diagnosis holds and libc is still the largest term. `mpsumsc` stages 68 GB of the 82 GB left after Stage A, and `sdf` and its four siblings are locals of two routines in `plasim.f90`, so they become sections of one shared `zpart(NESP,NLEV,0:NPRO-1)` that is contiguous at a fixed third index and passes to `mktend` without a temporary This row was issued as CLIM-49 on the shared-state branch and renumbered when it met main, which had already issued CLIM-49 for different work; commit messages from before the merge still say CLIM-49.

Source: `exoplasim/notes/shared-spectral-state.md`, `exoplasim/notes/threads-instead-of-ranks.md`
notes:
From archive/tasks.md closing note:
done 2026-08-22. Built as planned: `sdf` and its four siblings became sections of one shared `zpart`, and `mpsumscp` reduces them where they are written. THE SIGN HELD AND THE MAGNITUDE DID NOT -- Stage B is worth about **-11.6%** at T170 against ranks, chained from the two clean paired ratios rather than from its own contaminated run, where the projection was threads AHEAD by 4%. So it moved the deficit further than Stage A did, which is what the decision rule asked, and it did not cross zero: the plan's stopping condition -- Stage 2 only if threads reach parity -- was NOT met by Stage B, and what met it was CLIM-57's mkdheat and then SHTns. Both checks held: `verify_shared_determinism.sh` gives one hash, and the T21 restart is bit identical, this change reassociating nothing. The staging copy is gone from `mpsumsc`, and what now stands in libc is memset rather than memcpy -- `__memset_avx512_unaligned_erms` at 31% of T170 -- which is CLIM-75's attribution and CLIM-80's prize

title: Give mkdheat the treatment Stages A and B gave the rest of the dynamical core.
description:
Give `mkdheat` the treatment Stages A and B gave the rest of the dynamical core. It is the frictional heating term, `spectrald` calls it at `plasim.f90:3974` under `ndheat > 0`, and `ndheat` is 1 by default, so it runs every timestep -- a frame-pointer profile puts it at 12.29% of all samples, second only to `radstep`. It carries both halves of the threaded build's remaining deficit at once. TRAFFIC: eight `mpgallsp` calls staging about 2.5 MB a thread each at T170, and three `mpsumsc` calls still copying partials into a buffer, which is roughly 320 MB a timestep across sixteen threads and the same order as the 105 GB Stage A removed. FOOTPRINT: 18.7 MB of stack locals a thread, 299 MB across sixteen, of which six are `(NESP,NLEV)` FULL spectral arrays -- `zsd`, `zsz`, `zsq`, `zsdef`, `zstf1`, `zstf2` -- one complete copy of the global field per thread, which is exactly the pattern Stages A and B removed everywhere else. One thread's 18.7 MB does not fit CCD1's 32 MB of L3 beside weight matrices that are already 114.9 MB a die This row was issued as CLIM-50 on the shared-state branch and renumbered when it met main, which had already issued CLIM-50 for different work; commit messages from before the merge still say CLIM-50.

Source: `exoplasim/notes/shared-spectral-state.md`, `exoplasim/notes/rank-imbalance-and-weight-traffic.md`
notes:
From archive/tasks.md closing note:
done 2026-08-21. The six full `(NESP,NLEV)` spectral locals became four shared arrays and three partial slots in `pumamod`; what stays on the stack is what is genuinely per-process. Two collectives carry it, both build-agnostic: `mpgallspp` is `mpgallsp` with the staging removed, the destination being one array the team can see, so a thread writing its own slice IS the gather; `mpzerosp` clears a replicated spectral array from a given mode upward. NUMERICALLY INERT, which is the bar it earns by reassociating nothing -- the T21 two-thread restart hash is Stage B's own `53b3316c9fa35f59`, and at T170 on sixteen both arms wrote `4e5ac384ad34f5d1`, which is the stronger statement and came free with the measurement. Worth **+4.59%** [+3.82, +7.25] threaded against threaded, 4 of 4 rounds, taking the deficit against ranks to -5.48%. An earlier attempt is void and is quoted nowhere: unrelated work was running and the ranks arm scattered 10.3% against the 5% floor. Two places the shared-array discipline bit, both caught by reading the code rather than by the detector: a whole-array scaling in the `nenergy` block that every thread would have written, and a clear-from-mode-2 that could not stay a whole-array statement. mkdheat's TRANSFORMS were out of scope here and became CLIM-76

title: Establish whether a single-precision spin-up is sound
description:
Establish whether a single-precision spin-up is sound, and belongs with the restart converter because the handoff is the converter's job. MEASURED already: `compile.sh -p 4` builds FP32 -- upstream's default, which this project overrides to eight -- and it runs T170 on sixteen threads 39.69% faster [+39.63, +39.82], 4 of 4 rounds, 0.6% and 0.4% scatter. That is the largest single gain in this line of work and it needs no port and no device. The per-die working set halves from 260 MB to 130, so it pulls the same way as the 32 MB target. WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED is the whole risk: stability was shown over 300 steps, which is 6.2 model days and 0.043% of a 691,200-step spin-up, and single precision fails exactly where accumulation is long. Where the FP32 state LANDS is also unknown, because four-byte restart records against eight are different files to `compare_restarts.py` rather than different answers

Source: `exoplasim/notes/shtns-viability.md`, `exoplasim/notes/restart-resolution-precision-converter.md`
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
open. FP32 is a SPIN-UP accelerator and never a production mode: planet.yaml declares eight-byte precision, and the converter's own contract treats a converted state as a new initial condition that must settle at the target, never as proof of equilibrium -- so FP32 has only to land near equilibrium and FP64 does the final approach and the judging, which is what dissolves the objection that FP32 cannot resolve a 0.05 W/m2 per orbit criterion. The decisive test is a full FP32 spin-up, which costs hours and is exactly what the technique claims to make cheap. Pairs with main's CLIM-52, which already has four-to-eight byte conversion in its contract [step: rebuild_binaries, baseline_run]

title: Put SHTns behind every spectral transform call site
description:
Put SHTns behind every spectral transform call site, not just the inverse ones. `nshtns=1` now runs `gridpointa` and `gridpointd` through `sh_sp2gp`, `sh_dv2uv` and `sh_sp2grad`, which is the whole INVERSE direction, and the model agrees with legmod at rounding scale on four threads and is bit identical run to run. The FORWARD direction is untouched and is the other half: `gp2fc` plus `fc2sp` becomes `spat_to_SH`, `uv2dv` becomes `spat_to_SHsphtor`, and `mktend` -- which fuses six Fourier fields into three spectral tendencies with derivative weights -- has no single SHTns call and needs the fusion re-expressed. The forward direction also changes the SHAPE of the parallelism, because legmod integrates over a thread's own latitudes and produces a PARTIAL that `mpsumscp` reduces, while SHTns needs the whole globe in one call and produces the finished field, so the reduction goes away rather than getting faster. That requires the tendency grid arrays to be full-globe as the eleven prognostic ones already are

Source: `exoplasim/notes/shtns-viability.md`, `exoplasim/notes/shared-spectral-state.md`
notes:
From archive/tasks.md closing note:
done 2026-08-22, and the forward direction is what made it pay. Every per-timestep spectral transform call site runs through SHTns: both gridpoint paths in both directions, `spectrald`'s forward, `mkdheat` entire (CLIM-76), `mkdqtgp` in rainmod which the sweep found, and `zqout` (CLIM-78). `mktend`'s fusion was re-expressed and gridpointa's four `mpsumscp` reductions are gone, SHTns integrating the globe and returning the finished field. T127, sixteen threads, 300 steps, paired and interleaved with NSHTNS flipped inside one binary: **+16.81%** [+7.22, +23.00], 4 of 4 rounds, against -28.50% for the inverse half alone. HALF A TRANSFORM IS WORSE THAN NONE, by 41.7 points, because the model then pays for both implementations and still runs every reduction -- the inverse-only number was never evidence about SHTns and reading it as one would have killed the work a step before it paid. The 12.2% self-scatter on the third arm overlaps the +13.17% measured a commit earlier, so the honest figure is mid-teens percent and the two are not distinguished. NSHTNS=1 is now the default and the paired latitude decomposition is deleted, 515 lines. What is left on legmod is stated rather than forgotten: `span` is periodic, the `nenergy`/`nentropy` blocks are off by default, `glaciermod` and `surfmod` filter the orography at startup, and the alternative rain schemes are not compiled; legmod itself stays compiled because NSHTNS=0 is the reference `verify_shtns_model.sh` compares against, and deleting it would delete the comparison
close_reason: done 2026-08-22, and the forward direction is what made it pay.

title: Price a band-resolved shortwave and longwave against the broadband scheme, on this host
description:
Price a band-resolved shortwave and longwave against the broadband scheme, on this host, before deciding anything. WHAT THE ROW IS ABOUT, and it is not only accuracy: this scheme carries seven derived per-star corrections onto Lacis-Hansen and Sasamori -- `ozone_scale`, `ozone_uv_weight`, `ozone_visible_weight`, `h2o_sw_weight`, `h2o_sw_level`, `co2_sw_weight`, `cloud_absorption_scale` -- plus a longwave band added for CH4 and N2O. Each is separately derived and citable and none is a knob. The COUNT is the tell, and what it points at is measured: the broadband scheme returns about 40 percent of a line-by-line answer for CO2 and the same for the trace-gas band. Every one of those seven exists because a FITTED broadband absorptance cannot be re-weighted structurally and has to be re-derived, so they are seven manual instances of one operation that a band-resolved scheme performs as configuration. Price the maintenance retired beside the slowdown incurred

Source: `notes/external-model-survey.md` sections 8 and 9, `exoplasim/notes/corrk-cross-check.md`, `exoplasim/notes/trace-gas-band.md`
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
open and ORDERED after the SHTns forward direction lands, since both touch the same worktree. EXPLORATION: the deliverable is a cost per timestep and a verdict, not a replacement. NOT a defect row -- the shortwave water vapour deficit is one-signed, bracketed and carried under PHYS-9. CANDIDATES, all local. SOCRATES, `references/socrates/`, BSD 3-Clause: `ga7` is 6 shortwave bands with at most 12 k-terms and 9 longwave bands against 2 and 1 here, so about an order of magnitude of radiative work and, with `radstep` over 12 percent of the profile, roughly a twofold whole-model slowdown TO MEASURE. `sbin/Ccorr_k` makes that tunable by dropping absorbers and k-terms this world has no use for. ExoRT, `references/exort/`, is REJECTED on reading rather than second: `n68equiv` covers CO2, H2O and CH4 plus a collision-induced set and carries NO OZONE TABLE AND NO N2O, which discards `ozone_scale`, both derived ozone band weights and CLIM-42's trace-gas band outright, and it costs 68 intervals at 8 Gauss points, about three times `ga7`. Worse on both axes. THE REASON GENERALISES and should be applied to any candidate: ExoRT is built for Archean and hydrogen-rich atmospheres around M dwarfs, and this world's atmosphere is 1 bar of N2, O2 and Ar with 450 ppm CO2 and an ozone layer -- close to modern Earth in COMPOSITION and unlike it only in its STAR. So an Earth-built code with a substitutable stellar spectrum fits this project better than an exoplanet-built code aimed at exotic compositions. RTE+RRTMGP is the remaining alternative. CLIMBER-X was checked and REJECTED under REF-10: two shortwave bands like PlaSim's and a longwave that is a tuned parameterisation over concentrations rather than bands. A CHEAPER RUNG EXISTS AND IS HALF WHAT IT LOOKED LIKE. SPEEDY's shortwave is two bands with fitted absorptivities, the same class as Lacis-Hansen and no gain. Its four longwave bands are worth having because they divide the PLANET's emission and so need no per-star reweighting at all -- but `fband(100:400,4)` is fitted quadratics CLAMPED FLAT below 200 K and above 320 K, which stratospheric temperatures reach in normal operation, so re-deriving them from a Planck integral is part of taking it. THE INTERFACE IS BOUNDED, NOT GUESSED. Isca has already wired SOCRATES into a spectral GCM in 3,452 lines at `references/isca/src/atmos_param/socrates`, with spectral files as namelist strings. It is FMS-based so nothing drops into ExoPlaSim; what transfers is the SPECIFICATION, its call signature naming what a host must supply -- temperature, humidity, ozone, CO2, surface temperature, pressure and height at full and half levels, albedo, zenith cosine, distance factor, cloud fraction, effective radius, cloud water -- and returning heating rates, fluxes, clear-sky counterparts and optionally a spectral outgoing longwave, which would be a new diagnostic here. Its albedo argument is ONE broadband value per column, so a band-resolved atmosphere does not resolve the surface and PHYS-14 stays a separate decision. THE STELLAR INPUT NEEDS NOTHING NEW. `references/socrates/data/solar/trappist1` and ExoRT's spectra are both BT-Settl, the same library and the same three parameters `build_stellar_spectrum.py` already uses, and `examples/trappist1/mk_ga_trappist` is 46 lines that re-weight an existing spectral file against a stellar spectrum WITHOUT regenerating the k-distributions, copying the longwave file unchanged [step: rebuild_binaries]. A FIFTH AXIS, and the candidate is now well-supported without a run. SOCRATES exposes the PLANET as well as the star: `src/modules_core/rad_ccf.F90` declares `planet_radius`, `grav_acc`, `mol_weight_air`, `r_gas_dry`, `cp_air_dry` and `repsilon` as `PROTECTED` rather than `PARAMETER`, and `set_socrates_constants(iu_nml)` reads the first five from a `socrates_constants` namelist under its own comment "Read planet-specific constants from namelist", then DERIVES `repsilon` from `mol_weight_air` so the two cannot drift apart -- the same discipline `config/planet.yaml` uses where mass follows from gravity. It is the only external code read in this survey that gets that structurally right: CLIMBER-X puts Earth's radius, gravity and the Sun's visible share in a compile-time `parameter` block, GOLDSTEIN hardcodes `rsc` and `gsc` inside a subroutine, and Isca uses a namelist for most of it and still let `RADCON` through. For this planet only two of the five move -- radius and gravity -- since 78 percent N2, 21 percent O2 and 0.93 percent Ar is Earth's composition to three figures. WHAT REMAINS GENUINELY OPEN is only the cost per timestep in this model, which is the measurement this row is ordered after the SHTns work to take. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 21 EVIDENCE POINTERS, filed 2026-08-22 during a survey consolidation: the SPEEDY and SOCRATES readings this row rests on are `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 8, and the ExoRT rejection is `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 15.. THE COST IS FAR LOWER THAN THE TOOLING'S SIZE SUGGESTS, 2026-08-22. THE CRUX: the Met Office's own non-solar example, `examples/trappist1/mk_ga_trappist:5-15`, takes the standard Earth `ga9` shortwave file, rewrites BLOCK 2 ONLY with a TRAPPIST-1 spectrum, and runs NO `corr_k` at all -- blocks 3, 5, 10-12 and 17 carried over from Earth verbatim. TRAPPIST-1 is a 2600 K M8 dwarf, a far larger spectral shift than 4965 K, so if the cheap path is accepted there it is accepted here. TWO TIERS: cheap is one `prep_spec` run, seconds; expensive is re-running the correlated-k fit with `+S`, which the tooling's own README puts at "probably several days if not done in parallel" needing about 20 GB, then roughly an hour on re-runs. AND THE LONGWAVE FILE IS ENTIRELY STAR-INDEPENDENT -- its k-fits use Planckian weighting, not stellar -- so an Earth longwave spectral file transfers untouched and half the problem disappears. IF TAKING THE CHEAP TIER, know that THREE star-weighted quantities go stale and not one: block 3's Rayleigh coefficients, block 5's k-term weights, and every cloud and aerosol band average built by `Cscatter_average -S`. The TRAPPIST-1 example regenerates none of them; block 3 and the scatter averages are cheap to redo, block 5 is the expensive tier. THE ATMOSPHERE IS THE EASY PART: the foreign broadener is hard-coded to HITRAN air-broadened half-widths with no substitution mechanism, which is exactly right for a 1 bar N2/O2/Ar column, and the standard p-T grids span 1 Pa to 10 bar and 100 to 400 K. ONE TRAP: refractive-index validity ranges are declared and NEVER ENFORCED -- argon's is 0.140 to 0.568 um and the Sellmeier forms are silently extrapolated, with more K-dwarf flux redward of that bound than solar; the resulting error size is not determined from source. Ozone is fully separable, its own gas index and block entries, standard cross-sections covering 195 to 1100 nm. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 44

title: Cost the two routes to a shallow-ice solver on this project's grids. The claim that a native
description:
Cost the two routes to a shallow-ice solver on this project's grids. The claim that a native implementation beats a port is a JUDGEMENT with no measurement behind it, and it should not be inherited. Scope the comparison to the FLOW SOLVER ALONE: neither route supplies the surface mass balance, which is most of the work and is refused on separate grounds, so a comparison that includes it measures the wrong thing. ROUTE A, native on the region mesh: the operator is the doubly nonlinear diffusion `div(D grad H)`, with `D` depending on both `H^(n+2)` and `abs(grad z_S)^(n-1)`. This project already owns an elliptic operator on that mesh with exact closure and a certified uniqueness identity, and it owns an ACTIVE SET, which is what an advancing and retreating margin needs since `H >= 0` is a free boundary. ROUTE B, port MITgcmIS: establish whether the solver is separable from the cubed-sphere geometry and from MITgcm at all, what licence the Zenodo archive carries, and what the grid crossing costs under rule 3. EXPLORATION: the deliverable is a cost for each route and a verdict, not a solver

Source: `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 4
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
open, and INDEPENDENT of PHYS-13 and CLIM-53 -- whether this world wants ice is a different question from what a solver costs, and only the second is answerable today. DECLARE THE RULE BEFORE COSTING: the native route wins unless the port is cheaper by a wide margin, because it carries no grid crossing and no external dependency; and if the nonlinear diffusion will not converge on this mesh then route A is unavailable at any cost and the comparison is over. THAT CONVERGENCE IS THE FIRST THING TO TEST AND THE CHEAPEST. GW-9's exponential transmissivity failed on this same mesh under both Picard and Kirchhoff, so a doubly nonlinear diffusion has direct local precedent for failing, and GW-8 measured the discrete operator's own noise floor at about 12 percent relative RMS above l = 1, which bounds what any answer here can mean. Test it against the closed-form similarity solution for shallow ice at zero mass balance, which is an identity with a right answer, rather than against an ice sheet that merely looks plausible [step: any]. Route B is PARTLY ANSWERED already, from the tree now under `references/big-mitgcm/`: `MITgcmIS.py` is 557 lines, imports numpy, scipy, numba and joblib and NOTHING from MITgcm, reading its inputs as binary files instead -- so it is separable from that model. It is NOT separable from the cubed sphere: `read_cs_bin`, `cs_to_vec`, `vec_to_cs` and a `crossmap` face-crossing routine are structural rather than incidental, which is the part rule 3 makes expensive. What remains for this row is the cost, not the separability. A THIRD ROUTE EXISTS AND IS ALREADY ON DISK, AND THE SEPARABILITY QUESTION HAS A PEER ANSWER, 2026-08-22. `references/climber-x/src/ice_sico/` is SICOPOLIS, 27,000 lines, vendored inside CLIMBER-X, and `references/climber-x/src/ice/` is the 1,169-line layer it sits behind -- `ice_init`, `ice_update`, `ice_end`, plus a per-model translation pair. THAT LAYER SERVES TWO DIFFERENT ICE MODELS: it carries `yelmo_to_ice` and `ice_to_yelmo` beside the SICOPOLIS path, and `nml/ice_yelmo_par.nml` configures the second, so the interface is demonstrably model-agnostic rather than fitted to one solver. THIS DOES NOT SHOW MITgcmIS IS SEPARABLE, but it removes the possibility that nothing in this class separates, and it gives the interface a measured size to cost ROUTE B against: roughly 1.2k lines of adapter around a 27k-line solver, twice. It also adds a ROUTE C this row does not consider -- SICOPOLIS or Yelmo behind that same interface -- which should be costed or refused explicitly rather than left unnamed. Route A's argument from the existing elliptic operator and active set is untouched by this. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 4. ROUTE C COSTED, AND IT IS A DOWNGRADE FROM ROUTE A ON THE FREE BOUNDARY, 2026-08-22. SICOPOLIS does NOT solve the `H >= 0` constraint: `calc_thk_m.f90:1306` and `:1376` CLIP, the implicit variants solve the same unconstrained system and clip afterwards, and there is no active set, variational inequality or complementarity condition in the module. The mass the clip destroys or invents is then REBOOKED AS A SURFACE MASS BALANCE CORRECTION at `:1437-1443`, redefining accumulation and runoff after the fact so the diagnostics balance. Route A gets the margin right by construction; Route C gets it approximately and repairs the books. The margin is a per-cell binary against a single-precision epsilon with no sub-grid position. THE GRAVITY EDIT IS SMALL -- 17 lines mention `G`, one parameter defines it, two literals hide it -- SO THE COST IS ELSEWHERE: Earth-tuned dimensional limiters `hd_max = 500` m2/s and `vh_max = 3000` m/a sitting directly on g^3 and g^4 quantities and binding about 2.2x more often here while silently truncating the effect being studied; seven welded Earth region ids with a Greenland exclusion switch and a 604-line discharge scheme documented as Greenland-specific; and no material constant being namelist-configurable, so any change is a whole-model recompile. `hydro_m.f90` is 2,041 lines of DEAD code with a second inconsistent constant set -- do not port it. The coupling surface is NOT the expensive part: 13 fields in, 7 out, about 90 lines of translation, with a 1-based/0-based transpose that is rule 3's class of defect on indices. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 45c-d

title: Establish SEMI as the surface mass balance candidate
description:
Establish SEMI as the surface mass balance candidate, which is the half CLIM-62 scopes out and is most of the work. MITgcmIS's Positive Degree Day scheme is refused for driving ablation from 2 m air temperature alone, blind to absorbed shortwave over ice, which is the term a K2.5V host changes most. `references/climber-x/src/smb/semi.f90` is the opposite kind of object: it takes surface albedo and downward shortwave in FOUR components each, visible and near-infrared by direct and diffuse, with the derivatives of downward shortwave with respect to albedo, plus cloud, downward longwave, a lapse rate, a zenith cosine and dust. THAT BAND STRUCTURE IS ALREADY THIS PROJECT'S -- the visible and near-infrared split is the decomposition `lib/stellar.py` computes at 0.75 um -- so the per-star reweighting that exists maps onto its inputs instead of being reinvented. It also consumes sub-grid elevation, an elevation standard deviation, slopes and elevation classes and calls `downscaling_mod`, so it runs the balance on a downscaled field rather than a cell mean, and `snow_par` carries `lsnow_dust`, `w_snow_dust` and `dust_con_scale`

Source: `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 3f
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
open. EXPLORATION: the deliverable is what SEMI requires that this project cannot currently supply, and a verdict on whether the scheme or only its structure is worth taking. ITS INPUTS ARE THE QUESTION and most of the row: a four-component surface albedo and a four-component downward shortwave are more than `radmod.f90` exposes today, and costing that exposure is the work. `smb_bias_corr.f90` is a bias correction against Earth observations and has no meaning here; every constant in the module is a PHYS-class inheritance. ORDERED after PHYS-13 on CLIM-53's argument: a mass balance scheme fed cell-mean orography answers the wrong question however good the scheme is [step: rebuild_binaries]. THE ENTHALPY CHOICE AND ITS COST HERE, 2026-08-22. SICOPOLIS defaults to ENTM, the melting-CTS enthalpy method of Greve and Blatter: the conventional enthalpy solve plus a corrector that re-solves the column from the cold-temperate transition upward so the transition condition holds exactly. THE CORRECTOR MAKES PER-COLUMN COST DEPEND ON HOW MUCH OF THE COLUMN IS TEMPERATE, and with strain heating at g^4 and the pressure-melting gradient 1.31x steeper here, a simulated ice sheet on this world is temperate over more of its volume -- so a run is SLOWER PER TIMESTEP than an Earth run of the same size. Expect that rather than discover it. Sub-shelf melt itself is a two-parameter thermal-forcing law with no gravity; its freezing-point line needs both the gravity rescale above and a salinity decision, and its Earth-hydrography bias corrector should be deleted rather than ported. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 45e

title: Price the aerosol indirect effect, which is ABSENT rather than wrong and which no row has ever
description:
Price the aerosol indirect effect, which is ABSENT rather than wrong and which no row has ever named. Aerosol here is offline dust, sea salt and volcanic sulfate, each with an optics product, and the clouds are diagnostic: NOTHING connects condensation nuclei to droplet number to cloud albedo. WHAT AN OFFLINE AEROSOL PRODUCT WOULD HAVE TO CARRY IS FOUR NUMBERS PER MODE -- number concentration, median dry radius, geometric standard deviation, and HYGROSCOPICITY KAPPA, which is the only compositional information a condensation solver ever sees; densities, molar masses and dissociation numbers collapse into it before the run starts. That is a far smaller demand than the framing suggests and the existing products could carry it. THE BLOCKER IS THE UPDRAFT: PySDM prescribes vertical velocity and never derives it, there is no buoyancy closure, and an ExoPlaSim gridcell has no resolved updraft, so nothing generates the supersaturation that drives activation. AND THE CHEAP DOOR IS SHUT IN THAT TREE: it implements no Twomey and no Abdul-Razzak-Ghan -- the ARG directory is a reproduction TARGET of digitised figure data. The Koehler algebra is trivial; the missing piece is PEAK SUPERSATURATION, which is exactly what ARG parameterises

Source: `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 50
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
open. SCOPE THIS AS AN ACQUISITION FIRST, NOT AN IMPLEMENTATION: price an ARG-class parameterisation that maps aerosol and updraft to droplet number in closed form, and separately decide where an updraft proxy could come from, because without one the chain does not start. NOTE ALSO WHERE THE CHAIN ENDS: PySDM does reach albedo through effective radius, liquid water path, Stephens (1978) optical depth and Bohren (1987) two-stream -- but with NO spectral dependence and NO solar zenith angle, which for a host putting 0.382 of its flux below 0.75 um, and after section 37 priced snow's missing zenith term at 0.30, is one step short of usable rather than the end [step: none]. THE CLOSED FORM EXISTS TWICE OVER, 2026-08-22, and one of them already treats gravity correctly. `pyrcel/legacy/activation.py` is BSD-3, pure numpy plus `scipy.special.erfc`, and carries FOUR schemes side by side -- Abdul-Razzak-Ghan 2000, Morales Barahona and Nenes 2014, Shipway-Abel 2010 and Ming 2006 -- on one set of thermodynamics, which gives this row a second opinion for free. Its inputs are updraft speed, temperature, pressure and per-mode lognormal aerosol with kappa, which is exactly the four-numbers-per-mode set section 50a established and which this project's offline products could carry. Gravity appears once, in the alpha coefficient. SEPARATELY READ `CloudMicrophysics.jl`'s `AerosolActivation.jl`, which is the source of the ARG values PySDM's own test data cites, and WHICH ALREADY CARRIES GRAVITY AS A NAMED PARAMETER rather than a constant -- so it is the reference for where `g` belongs in the derivation, and it additionally corrects peak supersaturation for pre-existing liquid and ice after Korolev and Mazin (2003). Neither needs Earth observations: the ARG fit coefficients are fits to a parcel-model solution, not to data. THE UPDRAFT REMAINS THE BLOCKER and neither source solves it. `notes/external-source-inventory.md`

title: Convert the no-q-flux structural term from declared to measured
description:
Convert the no-q-flux structural term from declared to measured, using the procedure CLIMBER-X demonstrates. `references/climber-x/src/main/coupler.f90:4142-4146` and `:4189-4191` show how a q-flux is actually made: run with PRESCRIBED SSTs, write the diagnosed net surface heat flux to a restart as `qflux`, then read it back and apply it as `(flx_ocn - qflux)/cslab` against a 30 m slab. This row carries no-q-flux as a STRUCTURAL term and offers a constant diffusivity as the cheapest bound on it; this is a different and complementary instrument, bounding the term with a measurement at the cost of one prescribed-SST run. IT DOES NOT MAKE THE TRANSPORT PHYSICAL -- the field is a residual, and calling it transport would be the tuning this project forbids -- but a residual measured is better than a term declared. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 43e

Source: `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 43e
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
open, and DELIBERATELY SEPARATE FROM CLIM-16, which is closed: that row settled that horizontal diffusion stays off and that a constant diffusivity is a BOUND on the missing transport rather than the transport. This row is the other instrument -- a residual measured rather than a term declared -- and it does not reopen that decision. IT COSTS ONE PRESCRIBED-SST RUN, so it is not a desk calculation. Physics is not a knob: the diagnosed field is a residual and calling it transport would be the tuning this project forbids [step: baseline_run]

title: Repair two mirror-image averaging errors in the surface modules
description:
Repair two mirror-image averaging errors in the surface modules, found by sweeping the code this project RUNS rather than a peer. SEA ICE TAKES AN ARITHMETIC MEAN WHERE SERIES CONDUCTION REQUIRES A HARMONIC ONE: `icemod.f90:1427` sets `zckap = (CKAPSN*h_snow + CKAPI*h_ice)/(h_snow + h_ice)` and uses it at `:1439`, where snow over ice is two conductors in series and the effective conductivity is `(h_s+h_i)/(h_s/k_s + h_i/k_i)`. With 0.31 against 2.03 W/m/K the forms diverge fast: +21 percent at 0.05 m of snow on 1 m of ice, +39 at 0.10, +83 at 0.30, +104 at 0.50. **`landmod.f90:751-752` solves the identical series problem with the correct harmonic form**, so two modules of one model disagree. AND LAND TAKES A HARMONIC MEAN WHERE AN EXTENSIVE BLEND REQUIRES AN ARITHMETIC ONE: `landmod.f90:743-744` blends snow and soil heat capacity in the top layer harmonically, and heat capacity is extensive, so the blend is `(C_sn*z_sn + C_so*z_so)/z_top`. The coded form is exact at both endpoints, which is why it survived, and 25 to 31 percent low across partial snow cover. Repeated at `:753`, `:793` and `:803`

Source: `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 56a
notes:
From archive/tasks.md closing note:
done 2026-08-22. Rule 4's gate is discharged: all 12 binaries rebuilt from `vendor/exoplasim` at b7854949, `--verify` reports all 12 current against the sha of the source they were built from, and `check_consistency.py` passes `binaries carry current patches` at 29 checks 0 failed. A COMPILE PROVES THE CODE BUILDS AND NOT THAT THE NUMBERS ARE RIGHT; confirming the effect on this world's sea ice and land thermal inertia needs a run and is CLIM-71's cold start. Three instances fixed, not the two this row named: the sweep found `icemod.f90:1780` repeating the identical arithmetic mean in the skin-temperature routine, where `ntskin` defaults to 1 so it runs.

title: Cap the surface wetness factor on the restart path
description:
Cap the surface wetness factor on the restart path, where it is uncapped and both siblings cap. `landmod.f90:487-488` computes `drhs = dwatc/(drhsfull*dwmax)` bare, while `:418` and `:576` each wrap the same expression in `AMIN1(1., ...)`. Since `dwatc` is capped at `dwmax` and `drhsfull = 0.4`, **`drhs` reaches 2.5** -- an evaporation efficiency above the potential rate. `plasim.f90` calls `fluxstep` before `surfstep`, so the atmosphere consumes the bad value for one timestep before `landstep` recomputes it correctly, AND IT RECURS AT EVERY RESTART, which means every segment boundary

Source: `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 56c
notes:
From archive/tasks.md closing note:
done 2026-08-22. Rule 4's gate is discharged: all 12 binaries rebuilt from `vendor/exoplasim` at b7854949, `--verify` reports all 12 current against the sha of the source they were built from, and `check_consistency.py` passes `binaries carry current patches` at 29 checks 0 failed. A COMPILE PROVES THE CODE BUILDS AND NOT THAT THE NUMBERS ARE RIGHT; the substitution it removes is CLIM-70's check, which now guards the resume path, and CLIM-71 is the only route to exercising the fixed path at all. Not a cap in the end: the whole `limitwater` block is deleted, because `drhs` is already in the restart, the block's `dsnow` guard was inert, and `newsurf=2` already serves the case its comment described.

title: HALF OF THE CLOUD-ABSORPTION CORRECTION IS DEAD CODE
description:
HALF OF THE CLOUD-ABSORPTION CORRECTION IS DEAD CODE, and it is the half this project computed. `config/planet.yaml` carries `cloud_absorption_scale: 1.192`, derived through Mie from liquid water's refractive index and documented there as worth about +2.0 K, and `exoplasim/scripts/run_exoplasim.py:171-175` applies it to `TSWR3` and `ACL2`. **`ACL2` NEVER ACTS**: its only computational uses are `radmod.f90:2393-2396`, inside a block opening `if (nswrcl == 0)` at `:2387` and closing at `:2461`, and `nswrcl` defaults to 1 at `:182`, which is what every run records. The values are read, broadcast and never consumed. `TSWR3` is live -- but only at `:2382`, four lines ABOVE the branch; its second use at `:2445` is inside it and equally dead. SO THE CORRECTION IS APPLIED AT HALF STRENGTH AND NOTHING SAYS SO

Source: `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 58a
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
open, and it SUPERSEDES PART OF ARCHIVED PHYS-11, whose measurement assumed both keys acted -- that row is closed and stays closed, but any number quoted from it for the cloud pair needs re-reading against this. THE FIX IS A DECISION, NOT AN EDIT: either set `NSWRCL=0` to reach the prescribed-cloud branch, which changes the whole shortwave cloud treatment and is not a small change, or move the absorptivity into the computed-cloud path, or declare the correction as TSWR3-only and restate what it is worth. Rule 4 applies to any source change [step: baseline_run]

title: The calendar's seconds-per-day is eight times too large, from an argument-count mismatch
description:
The calendar's seconds-per-day is eight times too large, from an argument-count mismatch, and the run log prints the wrong number. `calmod.f90:44-45` declares `calini` with EIGHT dummy arguments; both call sites, `plasim.f90:428` and `:1521`, pass SEVEN -- so `kmpstep` receives `mcal_days_per_year` and `calmod.f90:67` puts 360 into the minutes-per-timestep, while the eighth dummy gets nothing and its only assignment sits after a `return` and is unreachable. No compile error, because `calini` is an external procedure with no explicit interface. THE PROOF IS IN THE OUTPUT: a T42 run's own diagnostics print `Sec per calendar day: 345600`, which is 16 x 360 x 60, where the correct figure at a 45-minute timestep is 16 x 45 x 60 = 43200

Source: `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 58b
notes:
From archive/tasks.md closing note:
done 2026-08-22. Rule 4's gate is discharged: all 12 binaries rebuilt from `vendor/exoplasim` at b7854949, `--verify` reports all 12 current against the sha of the source they were built from, and `check_consistency.py` passes `binaries carry current patches` at 29 checks 0 failed. A COMPILE PROVES THE CODE BUILDS AND NOT THAT THE NUMBERS ARE RIGHT; here the compile IS close to a real test, which is why this row is the one to trust most: the defect was a REAL passed through an implicit interface into an implicitly-INTEGER dummy, and a clean build with `kmpstep` declared at `calmod.f90:50` is exactly what catches that class.

title: Make a per-cell staged surface field detectably per-cell AFTER a restart
description:
Make a per-cell staged surface field detectably per-cell AFTER a restart, which is the check that would have caught CLIM-67 and does not exist. `surface_field_report` verifies only that the `.sra` files are PRESENT in the run directory, and presence is not the property that failed: the model read surface code 229, `landmod.f90`'s restart branch read the same `dwmax` back out of the restart with `mpgetgp`, and then a namelist scalar overwrote the array in memory. Nothing on the resume path compares CONTENT -- the per-code sha comparison runs only on the `--restart-from` prepare path -- so a segment could silently substitute a uniform field for a staged one and every downstream product would look well-formed. Compare the restart's own copy of each per-cell field against the staged field it was built from, on every resume, and refuse on a mismatch

Source: CLIM-67, `exoplasim/scripts/continue_exoplasim.py:550`, `vendor/exoplasim/exoplasim/plasim/src/landmod.f90` restart branch
notes:
From archive/tasks.md closing note:
done 2026-08-22. `exoplasim/scripts/restart_surface.py` compares the restart's own copy of every surface code this project stages against the field it was built from, scoped by `intended_surface_codes` so a new staged code is covered without editing the module, and it runs on the resume path from `continue_exoplasim.py` immediately after `surface_field_report`. The code-to-record mapping is verified at runtime against `surfmod.f90`'s own `surfcode` table, so an upstream renumbering fails loudly instead of silently comparing the wrong record, and the comparison is positional on flat NUGP arrays with no coordinate reconstructed on either side, per rule 3. TOLERANCE DECLARED BEFORE ANY RESTART WAS READ, and it is exact bit equality: the model's only operations between the `.sra` and the restart record are a list-directed ASCII read into real*8, an MPI scatter and the matching gather, none of them arithmetic, so no round-off is available on the path and a tolerance could only widen the target. IT FIRES AND IT PASSES, which is what makes it a test: `dz0clim` and `dls` match bit for bit and are the control that says the reader, the index mapping, the `dls` binarisation and the 14-month expansion are all right, while `dwmax` is refused on every run on disk. THE ATTRIBUTION WAS REFUSED RATHER THAN ASSUMED: no cold-started run exists, so these artifacts cannot show CLIM-67's substitution and the override chain accounts for the flattening independently. A synthetic fixture was built instead, `--self-test`, which requires three named outcomes and gets them -- a cold-start restart passes on 7 of 7 codes, `dwmax` flattened to `wsmax` is refused naming `dwmax`, and `dalbcl` flattened to `albland` is refused naming `dalbcl`, that last being the 14-month shape where `dwcl`'s latent instance sits. Codes 129 and, under NVEG=2, 212 and 229 are excluded and REPORTED BY NAME rather than dropped; `NEWSURF=2` is refused outright, being CLIM-67's substitution asked for by namelist. ONE DEFECT FOUND ON REVIEW AND FIXED: the CLI re-anchored `latest_restart`'s already-anchored path, so every run directory failed on `run_dir/run_dir/MOST_REST.*` and only the self-test path worked. Registered as a one_off in `config/pipeline.yaml`; it generates nothing and is imported as a module.

title: Cold-start the next commissioning rather than seeding
description:
Cold-start the next commissioning rather than seeding it, and gate its first resume on `restart_surface.py`. NO RUN ON DISK HAS EVER INTEGRATED THE PEDOLOGY FIELD: all 18 descend from a donor whose payload is gone and which never staged code 229, so every restart carries `dwmax` as one value, 0.5, `WSMAX_EARTH`, while `config/planet.yaml` sets `soil_water_source: pedology` and the staged `.sra` holds 3781 distinct values over 0.01 to 0.8. The albedo and forest records are a superseded generation on the same chain. So `soil_water_source: pedology` has never been a property of a run, only of a directory

Source: `exoplasim/scripts/restart_surface.py`, CLIM-67, CLIM-70
