From TASKS.md status column:
open, and it is the ONLY route to two things at once: it is what makes the pedology field reach the model for the first time, and it is the only way CLIM-67's fix becomes verifiable, since no artifact on disk can exercise a path that no run has taken. `restart_surface.py --self-test` is the interim substitute and is not the same claim. BLOCKED ON CPU, which is what makes it a commissioning decision rather than a task to schedule now: it is a bootstrap and baseline pair on the current build [step: bootstrap_run, baseline_run]

title: Verify that a restart's topography still derives from the staged code 129
description:
Verify that a restart's topography still derives from the staged code 129, which `restart_surface.py` names as its one residual gap and excludes as NOT_COMPARABLE. The restart's `doro` is `oroscale`-scaled and spectrally fitted, and under `nglacier=1` it also carries ice-sheet orography, so no right answer exists from the `.sra` alone and a comparison would have to reproduce the fit

Source: `exoplasim/scripts/restart_surface.py` NOT_COMPARABLE, CLIM-70
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
open, and it is REAL WORK rather than an omission: closing it needs the spectral fit plus the glacier orography reproduced offline, which is why CLIM-70 declared the gap instead of asserting a comparison it could not make. Everything else this project stages is now checked, so this is the last surface code that can drift unseen. It needs no climate run: the restarts and the staged field are both on disk [step: baseline_run]

title: Settle why the SHTns ANALYSIS arms miss the equivalence bar above T42 while synthesis
description:
Settle why the SHTns ANALYSIS arms miss the equivalence bar above T42 while synthesis is at rounding scale everywhere. `verify_shtns_equivalence.sh` declares 1e-11; scalar synthesis runs 1.0e-15 to 5.6e-14 across T21 to T170, scalar analysis 2.2e-14 to 2.3e-12, and the vector analysis arms 1.1e-13 at T21 rising to 5.9e-11 at T127 and back down to 9.9e-12 at T170. Three explanations are already excluded: it is not l(l+1) amplification from returning divergence as l(l+1) times the spheroidal potential, because that predicts NTRU^2 growth and T170 is six times better than T127; it is not the reference field being built by SHTns's own synthesis, because building it with legmod's changes no digit; and it is not concurrency, because the probe runs on one thread. The untested hypothesis is the NORMALISATION -- `spcheck` divides by the largest spectral coefficient where the synthesis arms divide by the largest grid value, and those differ by orders

Source: `exoplasim/notes/shtns-viability.md`
notes:
From archive/tasks.md closing note:
done 2026-08-22. It was the Gaussian quadrature WEIGHTS, which enter the forward transform and nothing else -- `fc2sp` carries gwd, `uv2dv` and `mktend` carry gwd/cos^2, and the synthesis direction never touches them, which is why every check that compared synthesis was clean. `inigau` evaluated the Legendre polynomial as a TRIGONOMETRIC SERIES and took the weight as z4(1-z^2)/z5^2, squaring that series' error into the weight. Adjudicated against an extended-precision reference, SHTns was exact to 2.7e-16 and bit identical over most of the hemisphere while inigau was wrong by 9.9e-11 at the pole-most latitude; numpy's `leggauss` is also wrong there by 4.2e-11, which is why a three-way double-precision comparison had read as a wash. Rewritten as Newton on the three-term recurrence: nodes to 1.1e-16 absolute, weights to 6.9e-13 at NLAT 256, weights summing to 2 within 8.9e-16. THE BAR WAS NEVER MOVED -- the 1e-11 declared before any of this now passes at every resolution, the analysis arms having fallen one to two orders, and the T127 MODEL went from 23 records beyond tolerance at 20 steps to none, worst 1.6e-07 to 7.9e-12. The other two candidates were excluded by measurement: band-limiting the field moved the error a quarter and the scalar arms carried it equally, so not vector under-integration; and nphi=384 mixed radix beat nphi=512 pure radix-2, 1.07e-14 to 1.20e-14. `verify_gauss_weights.sh` stands behind it with the replaced implementation as its control. NOTE FOR THE RECORD: this changes every number the model produces, because the nodes moved -- it is an accuracy improvement to PlaSim independent of SHTns, and every forward transform this model has ever done carried the old error [step: rebuild_binaries]

title: Measure what SHT_QUICK_INIT costs, and find a deterministic route to the alternative if
description:
Measure what `SHT_QUICK_INIT` costs, and find a deterministic route to the alternative if it costs anything. `shtns_setup` asks for it because the default `SHT_GAUSS` BENCHMARKS SHTns's algorithm variants at startup and keeps the winner, which makes the model irreproducible -- eight runs of one binary gave four distinct restart hashes, and the check that should have caught it was asking twice. `SHT_QUICK_INIT` picks by a fixed heuristic instead, and `nm` on the resulting binary shows only `_fly` kernels: SHTns is recomputing the Legendre functions with SIMD rather than streaming stored tables. That was chosen for reproducibility and has never been measured for speed. THE PREDICTION, stated before the measurement, is that it is resolution dependent and that on-the-fly wins where it matters: stored tables are nlm*nlat/2*8 bytes, which is 0.23 MB at T42 and 0.7% of a die, but 6.05 MB at T127 and 14.36 MB at T170 -- 44.9% of the 32 MB target, before the model's own 260 MB of state is counted. So expect stored tables to win at T42, wash near T85, and lose at T170, which is the only rung where the transform is a large enough share to care

Source: `exoplasim/notes/shtns-viability.md`, `docs/src/reference/environment.md`
notes:
REFRAMED 2026-08-22 by reading the pinned SHTns and probing it; exoplasim/notes/shtns-algorithm-selection.md carries the evidence.

THE PREMISE IS GONE. This row was to measure SHT_QUICK_INIT against STORED LEGENDRE TABLES. At SHTns 3.7.5 rev 4e69ceb the matrix-based algorithms are ABSENT, not unselected: init_sht_array_func never writes an SHT_MEM entry, choose_best_sht carries on_the_fly_only = 1 and overrides i0 = SHT_MEM with i0 = SHT_SV, and shtns_set_grid_auto declares on_the_fly = 1. The table-size prediction (0.23 MB at T42 to 14.36 MB at T170, tables win at T42 and lose at T170) is arithmetic about a configuration the library cannot produce and cannot be tested.

WHAT THE CHOICE ACTUALLY IS: on-the-fly unroll depth. quick_init pins FLY2 with no timing; sht_gauss times the candidates and keeps the winner. It is decided SEVEN TIMES, once per transform type (syn ana vsy van gsp v3s v3a), so a configuration is a vector of seven picks. Candidates are s+v and fly1..fly4, capped per rung by alg_lim = nlat_2/VSIZE2, with no OpenMP variants because the model calls shtns_use_threads(1).

SHT_GAUSS IS DISQUALIFIED ON DETERMINISM, MEASURED: five timed inits at T42 and five at T170 gave TEN DISTINCT pick vectors. Most of the seven races are decided on sub-1% differences from single unrepeated samples -- at T21 syn it is 7.11e3 against 7.12e3. That is archive CLIM-44's mechanism located rather than inferred.

THE ONE CANDIDATE EFFECT: at T170 syn the tuner reports fly4 at 1.60e6 against fly2 at 1.85e6, about 13% on the most-performed transform type, and it recurs across runs. To be settled by measuring the MODEL, not by trusting the tuner -- failure class 34.

THE DETERMINISTIC ROUTE IS A FILE. SHT_LOAD_SAVE_CFG loads shtns_cfg before any timing and suppresses the tuning pass. The file is plain text and AUTHORABLE: grid parameters, req_flags, SIMD id, then algorithm NAMES resolved through sht_func. So a per-rung pick can be DECLARED with a sha for provenance rather than raced for, and QUICK_INIT+LOAD_SAVE falls back to deterministic fly2 when the file is absent -- a fallback that must announce itself.

DECISION RULE, set by the user 2026-08-22: pick the best setting AT EACH GAUSSIAN ON THE LADDER and always use that rung's pick for that rung. This is not a search for one best-overall setting, and a per-rung difference is an expected outcome rather than an inconsistency.
close_reason:
Closed: the alternative does not exist, and the one deterministic mode is already what the model runs.

THE PREMISE WAS FALSE. The row was to measure SHT_QUICK_INIT against stored Legendre tables. At SHTns 3.7.5 rev 4e69ceb the matrix-based algorithms are ABSENT rather than unselected -- init_sht_array_func never writes an SHT_MEM entry, choose_best_sht carries on_the_fly_only = 1, shtns_set_grid_auto declares on_the_fly = 1. The table-size prediction (0.23 MB at T42 to 14.36 MB at T170, tables win at T42 and lose at T170) describes a configuration the library cannot produce.

WHAT THE CHOICE REALLY IS: on-the-fly unroll depth, picked once per transform type. quick_init pins fly2 with no timing; sht_gauss times the candidates and keeps the winner.

THE ALTERNATIVES ARE NONDETERMINISTIC, MEASURED. Five timed inits at T42 and five at T170 gave TEN DISTINCT pick vectors. SHT_GAUSS_FLY, which this row called deterministic by construction and the honest floor to measure against, IS NOT: shtns_set_grid_auto sets quick_init only for quick_init, reg_fast and reg_poles, so gauss_fly falls through to choose_best_sht exactly as gauss does -- five runs, five vectors. SHT_QUICK_INIT runs zero races in five runs. The deterministic set has exactly one member and the model is already on it.

THE PRIZE IS 0.1% AND UNRESOLVABLE. shtns-viability.md measures SHTns kernels at 0.00% of T170 model runtime, wrappers 0.74% together. Best per-type gains are a few percent of that, against a 5% bench floor, so no model-level A/B can resolve the pick. The tuner's one large claim -- T170 syn to fly4 at 13% -- was 3.2% over 2001 repetitions; the direction was real and the size inflated tenfold by measuring once. No uniform variant wins either: fly4 takes syn by 3.2% and loses vsy by 12.0%, on the costlier call.

WHAT LANDED INSTEAD OF THE MEASUREMENT. smoke_test.py now fails if shtnsmod.f90 asks SHTns for any mode that runs a startup race, so the decision cannot be undone by a plausible optimising edit. A different transform function is a different rounding order and sets the restart hash; archive CLIM-44 is that, paid for once.

REOPENING PREDICATE, and it is checkable rather than a mood: reopen when the transform is a materially larger share of model runtime than the 0.74% measured at T170 -- a rung above T170, a retaken profile after the radiation scheme is replaced (CLIM-61/CLIM-84), or an SHTns revision that restores matrix-based algorithms. Not on the strength of the library tuner's own numbers, which overstated their one large effect by an order of magnitude.

NOT MEASURED, and deliberately: the per-rung, per-type variant table at T21/T42/T85/T127/T170. exoplasim/scripts/shtns_variant_sweep.py is the instrument, registered and documented, if the predicate ever fires. The pilot covers T170, which is the rung where the transform share is largest.

title: Convert mkdheat to SHTns, the last hot legmod caller. It calls dv2uv three times and runs
description:
Convert `mkdheat` to SHTns, the last hot legmod caller. It calls `dv2uv` three times and runs EVERY timestep -- `ndheat` defaults to 1 and `spectrald` calls it unguarded -- and at T170 with NSHTNS=1 `dv2uv_` is still 7.05% of self samples, the fifth heaviest symbol in the profile and the largest remaining piece of legmod. It was missed because CLIM-57 converted its shared-state TRAFFIC and its transforms were never in the audit, which only swept the gridpoint and spectral paths

Source: `exoplasim/notes/shtns-viability.md`
notes:
From archive/tasks.md closing note:
done 2026-08-22. mkdheat's three dv2uv calls, its three analyses and its zhe synthesis all run through SHTns, and its seven grid scratch arrays became full-globe bands -- which also takes 18.7 MB a thread off the stack that CLIM-57 left behind when it moved only the SPECTRAL arrays. Three more mpsumscp reductions go with it, since the analyses return the finished field. The sweep that followed found a second per-step caller nobody had looked for, mkdqtgp in rainmod, guarded by nprc which defaults to 1; that is converted too. Verified at T21: all arms at rounding scale, bit identical across four runs. The gain is not separately measured -- it was folded into the same rebuild as the LPAIRLAT deletion, and the profile that would confirm dv2uv has left the T170 top symbols is the next thing to run

title: Decide the thread count by resolution instead of using sixteen everywhere. The row was opened
description:
Decide the thread count by resolution instead of using sixteen everywhere. The row was opened on an inference: at T42 libgomp is a QUARTER of runtime, 25.49% with SHTns and 21.04% with legmod against 10.9% at T170, and sixty-four latitudes across sixteen threads is four each, so the barriers looked to cost more than the work between them. MEASURED, THE INFERENCE IS WRONG, at exactly the resolution where it was most likely to be right: at T42 sixteen threads beats eight by 35.95%, four by 123.71% and two by 308.68%, 0/4 rounds to the smaller team in every arm. Fewer threads is monotonically worse, and both confounds -- idle cores boosting higher, and eight threads landing alone on the 96 MB V-Cache die -- favoured the low counts. Above sixteen was already refused twice over in `exoplasim/notes/smt-rank-layout.md`, on the SMT penalty and on a restart written at sixteen threads being unreadable at thirty-two. A high barrier share is the price of a team that is still paying, not evidence of over-threading

Source: `exoplasim/notes/thread-count-by-resolution.md`
notes:
From archive/tasks.md closing note:
done: sixteen at every resolution, which is a uniform answer to a per-resolution question rather than an unanswered one. The residual is attributed rather than left as one number -- 9.0% of cycles is the least-waiting thread's floor and the spread to 18.2% is imbalance -- so at most six points are recoverable, and by the level decomposition in CLIM-79 rather than by any thread count [step: rebuild_binaries]
No closing date was recorded for this task in TASKS.md or archive/tasks.md, so the closed_at timestamp on this issue is the date it was migrated into beads, not the date the work finished.
close_reason: done: sixteen at every resolution, which is a uniform answer to a per-resolution question rather than an unanswered one.

title: Move zqout to SHTns, the last per-timestep legmod caller. nlowio defaults to 1 and outaccu
description:
Move `zqout` to SHTns, the last per-timestep legmod caller. `nlowio` defaults to 1 and `outaccu` sums `sqout` on every step, so the humidity it carries has to be current every step -- the comment at `plasim.f90:3485` records why -- which means its NLEV scalar analyses run as often as anything in the dynamical core. IT IS NOT A SUBSTITUTION, which is why it was left rather than done with the rest: `sqout` is THREADPRIVATE and each thread's `fc2sp` fills a partial that `mpsum(sqout,NLEV)` reduces afterwards. A wrapper returns the COMPLETE field, so that reduction would multiply it by the thread count, and `sh_gp2sp` is parallel over LEVELS, so writing into a threadprivate array leaves each copy holding only the levels its own thread owned. The shape of the fix is gridpointa's -- the finished field into shared scratch, a barrier, then the reduction dropped -- but `sqout` is read whole by `writesp` and accumulated into `aasqout`, so every thread needs the whole of it afterwards, not a slice

Source: `exoplasim/notes/shtns-viability.md`
notes:
From archive/tasks.md closing note:
done 2026-08-22. `zqout` is a full-globe band through `sh_gp2sp`, `sqout` lands in shared storage, the `mpsum` is dropped, and every thread takes the whole field afterwards, which is what `writesp` and `aasqout` need. THE GATE COULD NOT HAVE CAUGHT EITHER MISTAKE, which is why the row asked for a check before the change: the beds set NLOWIO=0, so the guard never fired, `sqout` was never computed, and `aasqsp` -- the only record that reaches the restart -- was all zeros. The comparison was zero against zero, and it would have passed a reduction that multiplied the answer by the thread count. `verify_shtns_model.sh` now sets NLOWIO=1, which is also the configuration production spin-up runs; `aasqsp` then has 4840 of 5080 values non-zero, both arms agree at rounding scale at 1 and 20 steps, and the filter control sharpens as a side effect, its worst going from 12 to 36. `docs/src/practice/failure-modes.md` class 29, for the third time. Found on the way: `fc2sp` has an implicit interface, so gfortran infers its dummy from the call sites and refuses a mix of pointer-array element and whole-column section, which moved mkdheat's six legmod-path calls to sections

title: Give the threads a WORK QUEUE instead of a fixed share
description:
Give the threads a WORK QUEUE instead of a fixed share, because the fixed share is measurably unequal and no permutation of it helps. The OpenMP barrier is **17.89%** of T170 on sixteen threads, the largest single item outside the model's own code, and per-thread attribution puts the least-waiting thread at 13.7% of its cycles against 23.8% for the most-waiting -- a 10.08-point spread, of which the die explains 17%. TWO CAUSES, SEPARATED BY MEASUREMENT rather than assumed. Swapping the hemispheres between dies with `bench_ab.py --b-launch omp@<order>`, decomposition untouched and restart bit identical, moves `swr_`'s gradient WITH THE THREADS -- half-sums flip 4.32/5.91 to 5.60/4.74 -- so the largest model routine at 10.31% is imbalanced by LATITUDE, insolation cost varying about 2.6x across bands. `vdiff_` at 7.63% and `calcgp_` at 5.08% do not move: their heavy half stays on cores 8-15 across the swap, 2.90/4.78 to 2.60/4.53 and 1.97/3.15 to 2.14/3.11, so those are the DIE, CCD1's 32 MB running them about 1.6x slower whatever data it holds. `kuo_` is flat at 0.21-0.25% and contributes nothing

Source: `exoplasim/notes/where-the-time-goes.md`, `exoplasim/notes/thread-count-by-resolution.md`
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
open. A WORK QUEUE FIXES BOTH CAUSES WITH ONE MECHANISM, which is why it is the shape and not a weighted decomposition: slower threads take fewer chunks whether they are slow from cache or loaded from latitude, and no part of the model has to know the topology. A static permutation cannot, and that is measured -- the hemisphere swap is +0.006% [-1.03, +3.66], 2 of 4 rounds. It reads as a null because the two causes STACK natively, the geography-heavy hemisphere sitting on the die-slow half, so moving one of them re-splits the same critical path instead of shortening it. TWO SHAPES, AND THEY ARE NOT THE SAME SIZE. The contained one is the transform's iteration space: every wrapper is `!$omp do schedule(static)` over `jlev = 1, klev` with klev = NLEV = 10 against sixteen threads, so six threads get no iterations at all and four calls a step pass klev = 1 where fifteen get none; batching the (field, level) pairs into one loop -- gridpointa's four `sh_sp2gp` calls are 40 units, not 4 x 10 -- fills the team and touches only `shtnsmod.f90` and two call sites. The large one is the physics, where a queue means NHOR becomes a runtime chunk extent across roughly 700 `(NHOR,...)` declarations and 169 `where` statements -- THE SAME RESTRUCTURING CLIM-80 WAS REFUSED FOR, and the tension is deliberate rather than hidden: that refusal was on the CACHE argument, which the profile killed, and the work-queue argument is a different justification that this row's measurements make live. Reopening it needs that stated, not assumed. THE CONTAINED SHAPE WAS BUILT AND IT IS WORTH NOTHING, which is the first thing to know before taking the large one. Batching the (field, level) pairs was implemented, verified BIT IDENTICAL at T170 over 60 steps, and measured **-0.28%** [-1.02, +0.43] at T170, 2 of 4 rounds; at T42 it is UNRESOLVED rather than null across three attempts, the point estimate wandering -2.17%, +1.77%, +0.74% with an interval that never clears zero and two arms refused for scatter. The code is reverted and the finding is in the note, because the next reader of `sh_sp2gp`'s comment will have the same idea. So the prize here is bounded twice over and by two independent experiments: the swapped arm CUT the measured imbalance, 13.84/9.19 to 12.38/10.34, and bought +0.006%; the batch removed a REAL starvation -- threads 10 to 15 genuinely get no iterations -- and bought -0.28%. THE THIRD MEASUREMENT WAS TAKEN AND THE GATE PASSES. Both nulls above move work AROUND; neither says whether the slack exists. Spending it does: a control patch adds a calibrated busy-wait to every thread except the two on the critical path, and the added work is ABSORBED up to a saturation point -- 1.5 s vanishes entirely, 3.0 s costs 0.95 s, 6.0 s costs 4.1 s. **The slack is about 2.0 s of a 47.9 s run, 4.2%**, sitting just under the six points the attribution implies, which is where a real quantity should sit relative to its bound. So the earlier reading that max-minus-mean OVER-PREDICTS is withdrawn: the slack is real at close to the predicted size, and what the two nulls establish is that it is not reachable by redistribution. THE TRADE IS THEREFORE A CLEAN ONE AND IT IS LARGE ON BOTH SIDES: about 4% of T170, against converting **447 threadprivate variables** and 540 `(NHOR` declarations across plasimmod, radmod, rainmod, landmod, fluxmod and surfmod into shared globe-addressed state -- a re-architecture of how the model is parallelised rather than the loop-bound refactor this row and CLIM-80 both described, and one that puts determinism at risk in a model that has already paid for losing it once, archive CLIM-44. Whoever takes it should stage it: one physics routine converted and measured before the rest, with `swr_` the obvious first because it carries the largest single imbalance [step: rebuild_binaries]

title: Take -finit-real=zero out of the production flag line and put -finit-real=snan in the checked
description:
Take `-finit-real=zero` out of the production flag line and put `-finit-real=snan` in the `checked` profile, turning a permanent tax into a check that can fail. The flag initialises every local real on entry to every routine, arrays included, and it is the cause of the memset that three sessions read as the physics clearing its own work arrays: 1193 memset call sites in the T170 threaded binary with it against 623 without, spread across `swr`, `lwr`, `vdiff`, `kuo` and `gridpointd` exactly as widely as the flag is. It is worth **+26.03%** [+22.76, +27.29] at T170, paired and interleaved over 300 steps, faster in 4 of 4 rounds, 70.55 s against 51.97 s

Source: `exoplasim/notes/the-zeroing-is-an-init-flag.md`
notes:
From archive/tasks.md closing note:
done 2026-08-22. `-finit-real=zero` is out of `model.compile_flags.f90_opts` and `-finit-real=snan` is in the `checked` profile, where a read of an uninitialised local traps instead of quietly returning a zero. THE DECLARATION DELIVERS THE THING THAT WAS MEASURED, which is checked rather than assumed: the threaded build now compiles byte for byte to `c8b9c41046fd93ca`, the arm benchmarked at **+26.03%** [+22.76, +27.29], 4 of 4 rounds, 70.55 s against 51.97 s on the 300-step T170 bed. Determinism survives, which is the one thing this could have cost given archive CLIM-44 -- `verify_shtns_model.sh` passes whole on the new build: both arms at rounding scale, the control rejected, and the four-run bit-identity arm giving one hash, `fcf46ebbb1302d3a`. The registry is rebuilt, twelve executables. Two things it did not do. `most_compiler_omp` had to be edited by hand because nothing derives it from the declaration, which is CONS-16 and is why the flag now lives in two files. And the serial `most_compiler` keeps it deliberately: that file is a different build already, carrying `-fcheck=all` and no `-march`, so the init flag belongs with the rest of its debug posture [step: rebuild_binaries]

title: Establish what SHTns reads that it has not written
description:
Establish what SHTns reads that it has not written, and whether the model should be running it under an unmasked FE_INVALID at all. Under `-finit-real=snan` the model traps at the first timestep inside `_an12_l`, from `spat_to_SH_fly2_l`, from `sh_gp2sp` at `shtnsmod.f90:367`, from `gridpointd` at `plasim.f90:3717`; the faulting instruction is the tail of a horizontal reduction, `vaddpd -0x20(%rsi),%ymm0,%ymm0`, and the address it reads sits 21 KB BELOW both of the wrapper's locals, inside `_an12_l`'s own frame. Three candidates are already excluded by measurement: the model does not hand SHTns an undersized buffer, `probe_shtns_nspat.c` giving nspat exactly NUGP at T21, T42, T127 and T170; it is not an unwritten m=0 imaginary part, `sh_sp2gp` assigning every element to NCSP with the m=0 imaginary set to an explicit zero; and it is in no model array

Source: `exoplasim/notes/the-zeroing-is-an-init-flag.md`
notes:
From archive/tasks.md closing note:
done 2026-08-22, and the answer is that the trap STAYS UNMASKED. Two measurements already taken settle it, so no new arm was needed. THE LANE NEVER REACHES A RESULT: the `snan_noinv` build initialised every local to a signalling NaN -- which is exactly what fills the stack region SHTns over-reads -- and ran with FE_INVALID MASKED, so a bad read propagates a quiet NaN into the restart instead of aborting; the restart came out bit identical to production's. AND IN PRODUCTION THAT MEMORY CANNOT HOLD A NaN: `-ffpe-trap=invalid` means a NaN cannot be made by arithmetic without trapping at the line that made it, and `overflow` does the same for an infinity, so what SHTns over-reads is ordinary numbers left by previous Fortran frames. The exposure is confined to the `checked` profile on the threaded build, where `-finit-real=snan` deliberately writes the one bit pattern that trips it -- a documented limitation of that profile. Masking INVALID around the transform was considered and REFUSED: it would mask real NaNs arising inside the transform, which is where a bad gridpoint first shows up, trading the whole value of the flag for an exposure measured to be inert. `notes/audits/model-build-flags.md` [step: rebuild_binaries]
close_reason: done 2026-08-22, and the answer is that the trap STAYS UNMASKED.

title: Stop gridpointd carrying three full-globe scratch arrays per thread. zgq
description:
Stop `gridpointd` carrying three full-globe scratch arrays per thread. `zgq`, `zmmr` and `znrho` are `(NLON,NLAT,NLEV)` locals, 10.486 MB each at T170, so 31.5 MB a thread and 503 MB across sixteen, and they are used only inside `if (nsela > 0 ...)` and the aerosol branch. `zgq` is not read at all in this configuration, its branch needing `nqspec == 0` where both the default and the bed are 1

Source: `exoplasim/notes/the-zeroing-is-an-init-flag.md`
notes:
From archive/tasks.md closing note:
done 2026-08-22, and it is NUMERICALLY INERT -- the T170 60-step restart is `017a35afbdf1f5f6c621c734`, the same value the build produced before the change, which is the bar a change that reassociates nothing should earn. `zgq`, `zmmr` and `znrho` are one shared module array each instead of one per thread, and that is what the code already meant: `mpgagp` and `mpscgp` both route every thread's band through the shared `zbufgp` and then let only NROOT touch the destination, so on sixteen threads fifteen copies were never written to at all. Declared outside the OMPSHARED guard deliberately, so the MPI build -- where a module array is one per process, exactly what a local was -- is unchanged. Measured: `.bss` grows by 31,457,280 bytes, which is precisely the three arrays, and 503 MB of per-team stack goes away. The wall-clock effect is within noise, WHICH IS WHAT WAS PREDICTED BEFORE THE MEASUREMENT: these arrays are cold, touched only inside the aerosol branch, so the win is footprint and stack headroom rather than time. `zgq` is still never read in this configuration, its branch needing nqspec == 0 [step: rebuild_binaries]
close_reason: done 2026-08-22, and it is NUMERICALLY INERT -- the T170 60-step restart is `017a35afbdf1f5f6c621c734`, the same value the build produced before the change, which is the bar a change that reassociates nothing should earn.

title: Price the RADIATION SCHEME before optimising the one that is there. Radiation is 9.74% of T170
description:
Price the RADIATION SCHEME before optimising the one that is there. Radiation is 9.74% of T170 in libm alone -- `pow` at 6.69% and `log` at 1.70%, and the call graph attributes all of it to `radstep` through `lwr` and `swr` -- which is the first time this project has measured the transcendental cost the compute roadmap listed as a route and never priced. Two routines and one libm function is a small enough surface to attack directly. THE REASON THIS ROW IS NOT SIMPLY THAT: a swap to a correlated-k scheme, SOCRATES or the LMD Generic PCM's, would replace `lwr` and `swr` outright, and this project already holds the tables and a harness that cross-checks the current band model against them -- `docs/src/reference/external-data.md` records the `corrk_data` sets for an N2 atmosphere with variable H2O and CO2 to 0.95, and `exoplasim/notes/corrk-cross-check.md` is the comparison. Optimising a scheme that is about to be replaced is wasted work, so the two are one decision

Source: `exoplasim/notes/where-the-time-goes.md`, `exoplasim/notes/corrk-cross-check.md`, `docs/src/reference/external-data.md`
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
open. WHAT TO SETTLE FIRST, and it is a scoping question rather than a measurement: what a correlated-k radiation costs per timestep against the present band model, and what it buys in accuracy for a host star this project has already had to re-derive shortwave weights for. Both halves have existing evidence to start from -- `corrk_cross_check.py` for the accuracy side, this profile for the cost side -- and neither has been put next to the other. If the swap is refused, the fallback is narrow and cheap: the `pow` calls in `lwr` and `swr` are candidates for fixed exponents, `exp`/`log` identities, or precomputed tables, and 6.69% is the ceiling on what that can return. If the swap is taken, none of that work should be done. Note the swap is a PHYSICS change and answers to `docs/src/practice/failure-modes.md` class 16: a scheme belongs in the model because it represents the world better, not because it is faster, and a correlated-k scheme that is SLOWER may still be the right answer [step: baseline_run]

title: check_consistency.py's biosphere check compares a sha256 of the raw config/planet.yaml
description:
`check_consistency.py`'s biosphere check compares a sha256 of the raw `config/planet.yaml`, so an edited COMMENT is indistinguishable from an edited parameter

Source: `scripts/check_consistency.py`
notes:
From archive/tasks.md closing note:
done 2026-08-17, as ONE mechanism rather than a second one. `config_drift` moved out of `continue_exoplasim.py` into `lib/provenance.py` and takes the allowlist as an argument, so the resume guard and the biosphere check share the comparison but not the list -- reachability is a property of the consumer, and `baseline_climatology` is inert for a resume and live for the biosphere, so a shared list would have to be their intersection. The three biosphere generators now write `source_config` into their provenance, as an ExoPlaSim run manifest already did; a record without it falls back to the file hash and SAYS that it cannot separate a comment from a parameter. Allowlist is four keys, each traced by grep to no reader: `schema_version`, `star.activity`, `star.surface_uv_relative_to_earth`, and the two `stellar_cycle.components.*.note` strings. What was deliberately left OFF is the more useful half and is recorded in the code: `star.spectral_type` looks like a label but `build_stellar_spectrum.py` writes the `.dat` from it, and `model.*` reaches the climatology the solstice offset is fitted against. Both reach an artifact through one more file. It caught a live one on the way: the resume guard's allowlist carried `star.surface_uv`, and the key is `star.surface_uv_relative_to_earth`, so that entry had excused nothing for as long as the guard had existed. `--self-test` is the class 17 half, 8 cases, each negative paired with the positive proving the edit landed, and it was demonstrated failing two ways before being trusted. Left standing knowingly: three binary checks hash source files the same way, but a compiled binary has no value-level view and a rebuild restores certainty rather than silencing a hash. Spun out as CONS-3: the spectrum is staged by name
close_reason: done 2026-08-17, as ONE mechanism rather than a second one.

title: binary_manifest.json records the sha of every source file and the ExoPlaSim version
description:
`binary_manifest.json` records the sha of every source file and the ExoPlaSim version, and records nothing about the compiler or the flags, so a toolchain change produces a different executable under an identical set of recorded sources. `--verify` sees the executable's sha move and can only call it unknown provenance

Source: `notes/audits/aocl-and-model-build-flags.md`
notes:
From archive/tasks.md closing note:
done 2026-08-20. `toolchain()` records the four generated compiler and precision option files VERBATIM, the versions of the compilers those files actually name rather than a hardcoded `gfortran`, `precision_bytes` from the config, the declared `model.optimization_flag`, and THE FLAG LINE THE MAKEFILE ACTUALLY USED. That last one is not redundant and the first cut of this task lacked it: `compile.sh` copies `most_compiler_mpi` to `plasim/bld/compilerargs` and appends its `-O` flag THERE, so the file the manifest was reading never carried it. Adopting `-march=znver4` exposed it immediately -- the executable held 20,371 AVX-512 references while the recorded flag line showed none. It is read after the build loop, so it describes the binaries just written rather than the previous set; `--verify` reports `TOOLCHAIN HAS MOVED SINCE THE BUILD` and exits non-zero. What makes the comparison worth making is measured rather than assumed: the build is BIT-REPRODUCIBLE on this host, so same sources plus same flags plus same compiler give a byte-identical executable and a sha that moved has somewhere to be attributed. Verified on five cases with right answers known in advance -- identical toolchain silent, a compiler version named with both versions, a flag change named, an absent record named, and PRECISION named, which is `notes/audits/compiled-precision.md`'s defect: a manifest built at 4 against a config declaring 8 is now a reported drift rather than a silent one [step: rebuild_binaries]

title: A clean build of the model fails. glaciermod.o's rule in make_plasim omits landmod.o
description:
A clean build of the model fails. `glaciermod.o`'s rule in `make_plasim` omits `landmod.o`, and `outmod.o`, which needs `glaciermod.o`, precedes `landmod.o` in `OBJ`. `compile.sh` empties `plasim/bld` only when switching between the MPI and serial builds, so a `landmod.mod` from a previous build always masks it, and `make -j` is unsafe at any level

Source: `notes/audits/aocl-and-model-build-flags.md`
notes:
From archive/tasks.md closing note:
done 2026-08-20, and it was THREE missing edges rather than the one the row names. Derived rather than guessed: every `use` in `plasim/src` was resolved to the file defining that module and compared against the declared prerequisites, which found `glaciermod.o` short of `${LANDMOD}.o`, `plasim.o` short of `radmod.o` and `carbonmod.o` short of `${RAINMOD}.o`. The first two link EARLIER in `OBJ` than the module they need, so each fails a build from an empty tree; the third is ordered safe by accident and unsafe under `make -j`. Fixing only the row's edge would have moved the failure to `plasim.o`, and the earlier hand build had passed only because forcing `landmod.o` first happens to drag `radmod.o` in with it. Proved on a test that could fail: a build from an EMPTY directory at `-j16`, which the defect made impossible, now succeeds and produces an executable byte-identical to the shipped one, and the five-binary rebuild that followed reproduced all five byte for byte, so the change touches ordering and not output. Recorded in `exoplasim/patches/README.md` as an upstream build defect of the #59 class, found here and not yet offered [step: rebuild_binaries]
close_reason: done 2026-08-20, and it was THREE missing edges rather than the one the row names.

title: carbonmod rewrites both namelist files with truncated groups
description:
`carbonmod` rewrites both namelist files with truncated groups, deleting every fork key. `carbonmod.f90:353-372` declares its OWN `radmod_nl` carrying 27 keys where `radini`'s real group at `radmod.f90:862-871` carries 60, then writes it over `radmod_namelist` at run end. Under `nco2evolve=1` that DELETES the stellar spectrum file and its switch, the two-band albedo switch, the ozone and water-vapour and CO2 shortwave weights, the trace-gas band keys, every dust and cloud setting, and the stellar-cycle keys -- and the next year runs on defaults. `psurfupdate` does the same to `plasim_namelist`, dropping the day count, the timestep, the diffusion keys and the reference temperature; its group also names two keys that are not in it. SEPARATELY, `carbonmod.f90:116` captures `psurf` in `carbonini` BEFORE `plasim.f90:566-569` applies the mean-orography correction, and `:339` writes the uncorrected value back, so under the same switch surface pressure ratchets up by that correction every year on top of the intended drift

Source: `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 58e
notes:
From archive/tasks.md closing note:
done 2026-08-22. Rule 4's gate is discharged: all 12 binaries rebuilt from `vendor/exoplasim` at b7854949, `--verify` reports all 12 current against the sha of the source they were built from, and `check_consistency.py` passes `binaries carry current patches` at 29 checks 0 failed. A COMPILE PROVES THE CODE BUILDS AND NOT THAT THE NUMBERS ARE RIGHT; the guard is key containment rather than the size test this row specified, which was refuted against all 19 `radmod_namelist` artifacts on disk and would never have fired. It hardens against destruction and does not make `nco2evolve=1` usable; CONS-15 is that.

title: Replace the vendored build driver with one that REFUSES an input it does not understand
description:
Replace the vendored build driver with one that REFUSES an input it does not understand, and delete `configure.sh`. Every defect in the source document is the same shape -- an unrecognised argument silently changes what gets built rather than failing -- and it has already cost a session once as CLIM-22, sixteen-rank binaries built single precision. `compile.sh -r 170` builds T21 and exits 0, because the `case` arms are the seven names and the seven latitude counts and the last arm is `\?)`, which in bash matches a literal `?` rather than anything else, so the "INVALID RESOLUTION" message it guards is unreachable; `-p` has the same shape over a `prec=4` default, which is the CLIM-22 mechanism still in place. The executable is then named for the resolution the parse ARRIVED at, and `compile.sh` deletes only the name it is about to write, so a caller copying the name it asked for gets an untouched binary from an earlier session with nothing anywhere reporting an error. Separately, `config/planet.yaml`'s declared flag line reaches `most_compiler_mpi` only: the threaded build reads `most_compiler_omp`, which nothing derives from the declaration, and all twelve registered binaries are MPI while every binary this optimisation workstream measures is threaded and unregistered

Source: `notes/audits/model-build-driver.md`
notes:
From archive/tasks.md closing note:
done 2026-08-22. `compile.sh`, `configure.sh`, `make_plasim`, the three `most_compiler*` files, both `most_precision_options*` and the four `most_{ice,snow}_build*` scripts are deleted; `plasim/CMakeLists.txt` and `exoplasim/scripts/build_model.py` replace them. THE ACCEPTANCE TEST WAS THAT A WRONG ARGUMENT FAILS, and it does: `--res 170`, `--parmode threads` and `--ranks 7` each exit non-zero having written nothing, and `--drop-flag` naming a flag the declaration does not carry is an error rather than a no-op. Equivalence was declared before the first build as byte-identity or else an identical restart with an identified reason. Byte-identity FAILED, for a reason that is now written down: CMake compiles out of tree, so gfortran embeds absolute paths in its runtime-diagnostic strings and `.rodata` grows 35,776 bytes, shifting every address after it. What is identical is `.text` SIZE, all 2187 symbols by name and size, and the T170 60-step restart. Both open questions the row named are answered: the threaded build takes its flags from `config/planet.yaml` like every other, and the manifest records the flag line `build_model.py` actually passes rather than the contents of files that no longer exist. Threaded binaries are still not in the registry MATRIX, which stays MPI-only and is a separate decision. `verify_paired_decomposition.sh` went with it: it patches LPAIRLAT, which the source no longer has [step: rebuild_binaries]

title: Decide whether the producing binary joins run_id's identity
description:
Decide whether the producing binary joins `run_id`'s identity: `binary_manifest.json` guards the build, but a run's identity does not record which binary made it

Source: `docs/src/practice/failure-modes.md` class 11
notes:
From archive/tasks.md closing note:
done 2026-08-20, and the DECISION is that it does not: CLAUDE.md rule 6 says an id encodes nothing, so the binary joins the MANIFEST. Half of that was already true and the half that was missing is the half that bites. `run_exoplasim.py` stamps `executable.sha256` at prepare time, and `continue_exoplasim.py` recorded `input_restart_sha256` per segment and never the binary, so a run SPANNING A REBUILD had segments no single executable produced and nothing said so. Rule 4 makes that the normal case rather than an edge: it requires rebuilding every binary after any change under `vendor/exoplasim`, and runs here are long. Fixed by stamping `executable_sha256` into each segment record, for the same reason the stellar spectrum digest beside it is per segment -- those two came apart once already -- and it matters more here, because the low-I/O change alters the restart layout, so a resume across a binary change is not merely unattributed but wrong, and the script now says so when the segment's binary differs from the prepared one. NOT BACKFILLED, deliberately: writing a per-segment record from a top-level one would assert something that was never measured. The 40 orbits on disk lose nothing in fact, because the rebuild the same day left all five binaries BYTE-IDENTICAL [step: baseline_run, bootstrap_run]
close_reason: done 2026-08-20, and the DECISION is that it does not: CLAUDE.md rule 6 says an id encodes nothing, so the binary joins the MANIFEST.

title: Make the NetCDF products this project writes declare their own geometry
description:
Make the NetCDF products this project writes declare their own geometry, so a generic reader cannot substitute Earth's without saying so. Three parts. `lat` and `lon` carry `units = "deg"` where CF names the axes `degrees_north` and `degrees_east`, so a reader that does not recognise an axis falls back to guessing it from position. No coordinate system is declared on any of them, so a reader that derives cell areas from one takes an Earth radius: iris `area_weights` uses the radius from the cube's coordinate system when it is present and spherical and falls back to its Earth default only otherwise, which makes a declared spheroid the difference between a right answer and a plausible wrong one. The radius is `planet.radius_earth` in `config/planet.yaml` and is read rather than copied, per rule 2. And the files carry no Gaussian quadrature weight variable, so `ncwa -w` has nothing to find and gives the unweighted mean that is the first of environment.md's three traps. Writing the weight also makes the file the one place the grid's quadrature is RECORDED rather than recomputed, which seventeen modules currently do through `leggauss`; whether those then read it is a separate row and not this one. SCOPE: the writers this project owns, swept together rather than one at a time, since `exoplasim/`, `hydrography/`, `pedology/`, `minerals/` and `aeolian/` all write NetCDF and a partial sweep leaves a reader unable to tell which convention a file follows. NOT `source/`: its conventions are `vendor/orogen/tools/` and `source/README.md`, and a metadata edit there is an overwrite rather than a new build, which rule 7 forbids. NOT the time axis, deliberately -- it stays `units = timesteps` with no calendar, because no CF calendar expresses this orbital period and imposing one would make an Earth-calendar operator succeed silently where it now refuses. The second trap documents a correct artifact rather than a defect in it

Source: `docs/src/reference/environment.md` "Three traps, because these tools assume Earth", `source/README.md`
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
open; independent of any run and cheap. Products written after the sweep carry the attributes and products written before it do not, which is the tree's resting state rather than a work list [step: bootstrap_climatology, baseline_climatology, analyze_climatology, hydrography, surface_water, groundwater, surface_classes, dust, sea_salt, volcanic_sulfate, prospectivity]

title: Spike AiiDA as the record of what the pipeline has done
description:
Spike AiiDA as the record of what the pipeline has done, and decide from the answers rather than from the comparison. Install `aiida-core`, `aiida-shell` and `aiida-workgraph` into `.venv`, wrap `hydrography` and `bootstrap_climatology` with `launch_shell_job`, and dry-run one step in the `hours` band. Five questions, all left open by `notes/orchestration-frameworks.md`, and every one about effort or fit rather than about whether AiiDA can do the thing. (1) What does keeping a multi-GB climatology out of the content-addressed store actually cost: does the `remote_folder` route behave as documented, and does a checksum emitted beside the artifact and retrieved on its own give back what the store would have given? `use_symlinks` does not answer this -- it applies to input staging, not output retrieval. (2) Does `aiida-shell` wrap the step scripts as they stand, or must their inputs be exposed as nodes first? (3) Can an Orogen generation sit inside the graph? The exit predicate itself -- carve the intersection of the verdicts taken at the two bounding climates -- is what the `while_`-and-pause pattern is for, so the open part is the generation, which runs a vendored fork and writes the read-only `source/` tree. (4) What does `verdi node delete --dry-run` report against `pipeline.py --purge` on one seed? That is a differential test with a right answer: the two must agree within a pass, and the instance graph should be correct where the `orogen` cut is an approximation. (5) Is a WorkGraph program an acceptable replacement for reading `config/pipeline.yaml`? That one is a preference, settled by looking at both rather than by measuring, and it is the only question here whose answer is a matter of taste. SCOPE: what AiiDA would replace is the record half -- `exoplasim/runs/INDEX.json` as the run registry, `downstream()` and `--purge`, and part of the stamping -- while `config/pipeline.yaml` stays as the declaration, because cost bands and gates are annotations for a person deciding whether to start an expensive step, and the two answer different questions on the same division that keeps `--purge` and `check_consistency.py` apart. This row is NOT a decision to adopt; adoption if taken belongs at a generation boundary, where rule 7 leaves nothing to ingest and the migration cost is therefore about zero

Source: `notes/orchestration-frameworks.md`

From TASKS.md status column:

title: Remove the nutrient-activation call to disturbance(patch
description:
Remove the nutrient-activation call to `disturbance(patch, 1.0)` from the accepted ecological trajectory, or isolate it as an explicit initialization-only operation; preserve C-N-P exactly, manifest the intervention and prove against a no-reset control that vegetation, litter, soil pools and patch-age distributions are equivalent over the declared equilibrium window before accepting an accelerated state

notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
open; source isolation and no-simulation mass-routing checks can proceed independently, but the equivalence measurement is blocked on BIO-12, BIO-14 and explicit permission for LPJ-GUESS runs [step: lpj_run]. A SECOND DEMOGRAPHIC MODEL, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS STRUCTURAL, 2026-08-22. IN FATES A PATCH IS A PLACE -- area-tracked, summing to the site, created by disturbance and fused on a biomass profile. IN LPJ-GUESS A PATCH IS A SAMPLE, with no area member at all, aggregated by an unweighted mean, never created or destroyed. THE SHIPPED CNP CONFIG SETS `npatch 1`, so the ensemble has one member; check what `biosphere/scripts/build_lpj_driver.py` actually writes. What follows is the distinction this fork cannot express and that sits upstream of standing biomass: FATES separates RATE from AREA and DENSITY LOSS from GAP CREATION, and with its default disturbance fraction a canopy tree's death produces no density loss at all, only new disturbed area, while an understory death is pure density loss. Canopy layer is cohort STATE that changes the physics, which is what makes that expressible. FATES CANNOT BE RUN HERE -- it needs a host land model for per-layer soil hydraulics, canopy-air vapour pressures and someone else's transpiration flux -- so the value is comparative, and the rows that should change shape are the ones about disturbance representation and canopy-layer-dependent mortality, not the ones about processes. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 54a

From archive/tasks.md closing note:

The correction is the FOURTH root of the gravity ratio, 1.0691, not the square root's 1.1429: Shao and Lu (2000) eq 22 splits the threshold into gravity and cohesion terms, the minimum is where they are equal -- Kok et al. (2012) section 2.1 says so of the observed 75-100 um minimum -- and at that minimum `u*t ~ (rho_p g gamma)^(1/4)`, so the cohesion parameter cancels out of the ratio. That is worth having: gamma is known only to a factor of three, 1.65e-4 to 5.0e-4 N/m, and the ratio is 1.0691 to four figures across the whole range. 6.9% on the threshold cut emission 30% and the land-mean optical depth from 0.740 to 0.512. title: There is NO wet deposition in ExoPlaSim's aerosol. aerocore takes no precipitation argument
description:

It gathers `dprl + dprc`, flips them in latitude like every other field `aero_main` gathers, and applies Sportisse (2007) below-cloud scavenging `Lambda = scava * p**scavb` behind `lwetdep`, default 0 so ONE BINARY RUNS BOTH ARMS per the rewritten A3. Same form and coefficients as the offline chain, so the two can be compared rather than contrasted; column-uniform rather than below a diagnosed cloud base, which is the offline chain's own approximation and is declared. `scava` and `scavb` get no Fortran default -- `aero_ini` aborts -- because they live in `aeolian/config/dust.yaml` and a default here would be a fourth place to go stale. PREDICTION with falsifiers: burden falls about 10x at fixed emission, bracket 4 to 15; below 1.5x means the precipitation is not arriving through the gather or the flip, above 50x means m/s was read as mm/h, which inflates Lambda by 9985 and collapses the burden to zero rather than to a smaller steady state. The LMD Generic PCM has no wet deposition for aerosols either, so this is a common omission in exoplanet GCMs rather than an ExoPlaSim defect [step: rebuild_binaries]

notes:
From archive/tasks.md closing note:
done 2026-08-18, SINGLE MODE, and the check this task proposed turned out to be VACUOUS. Only `Qext/apart` enters the optical depth, so the mass extinction efficiency round-trips for ANY radius, and for either DUST-12 dataset -- they differ 0.32% in MEE, because MEE is set by the real part while the datasets differ in absorption. So the result does not depend on DUST-12 either way. What `apart` actually controls is SETTLING, and there the optical 0.98 um is 4.8x too long-lived for the burden and 16x too slow for the emitted mass. Generic PCM carries dust as one aerosol kind with one effective radius, which supports the single mode, but DECOUPLES the optical radius from the sedimentation radius; ExoPlaSim can too, through that same identity. Recommended: `apart` = 2.21 um, burden-matched, with the aerofile's four Q values per band scaled by 2.251, which leaves optical depth, SSA, backscatter and the band ratio unchanged because each is a ratio. NOT APPLIED, deliberately: it only bites once `apart` reaches `radmod`, which is upstream defect 1, and applying now would churn a tracked aerofile for no effect. DECLARED COST of the single mode: total deposition still equals emission in steady state, so the cost is WHERE it lands -- one lifetime is one travel distance, and the coarse 73% of emitted mass goes 3.4x too far while the sub-micron fraction goes 30x too short, so both ends of the phosphorus argument come out wrong in opposite directions. The offline chain therefore keeps producing the size-resolved deposition field that pedology and phosphorus read [step: rebuild_binaries]
close_reason: done 2026-08-18, SINGLE MODE, and the check this task proposed turned out to be VACUOUS.

title: Write the aerofile, and pin down the undocumented bottom-level sink

Write the `aerofile`, and pin down the undocumented bottom-level sink

Source: `exoplasim/scripts/dust_aerofile.py`, `aeolian/notes/in-model-dust.md`
notes:
From archive/tasks.md closing note:
done 2026-08-17. The aerofile is generated from `analysis/dust_optics.json` and validated three ways: `radmod` reconstructs the single-scattering albedo and backscatter ratio to four decimals, the optical depth round-trips against the offline chain's 0.5122 exactly, and Qext comes out 2.65, a plausible Mie efficiency for a micron particle. The conversion is the trap -- Qext is an efficiency against one sphere's geometric cross section, so `Qext = 4 apart rhop MEE / 3`, and only the ratio Qext/apart affects optical depth while apart alone sets settling. The sink is NOT undocumented, there is a comment one line above calling it an anti-build-up term, and it is a stability hack rather than a parameterisation: 99% of the bottom layer per timestep, an implied deposition velocity of 52.7 cm/s against a real 0.1 to 2, and it does not scale with dt so the rate is inversely proportional to the timestep. It must be replaced with a deposition velocity before any emission is calibrated

SPITFIRE reads lightning from an input file whose default is literally named `lightning_fixed`, in `hectare-1 d-1`, and uses it in ONE LINE multiplying by two Earth-tuned constants whose product is 0.008, one being Earth's cloud-to-ground flash fraction. title: Glacial erosion carries no gravity term, and Glen's law makes ice velocity go as g^3 (2.23x
description:
Glacial erosion carries no gravity term, and Glen's law makes ice velocity go as `g^3` (2.23x here)

Source: `notes/audits/orogen-gravity.md`
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
blocked on the downscaling pass, deliberately. AMENDED: two further facts make a g^3 term precision on the wrong quantity. `iceFlow` accumulates a CELL TALLY, seeded from the glaciation index and summed downstream, where the hydraulic path was deliberately given `flowSeed = cellArea / refCellKm2` so its accumulation is a real drainage area; the two accumulators disagree about what is resolution-independent, and the same valley collects about four times the ice flow at four times the region count, carving as `iceFlow^0.6`. And per PHYS-13 the index feeding it is an Earth-calibrated latitude threshold blind to this planet's obliquity, spectrum and rotation. Fix the ice mask first. The sub-grid judgement also survives measurement: at four times the region count the mean edge is 7.59 km against a 1-5 km valley, and reaching 1.5 km edges needs about 256 million regions, 26x the run measured. See `notes/audits/orogen-resolution.md`. The audit's recommendation was Option B, carry it as a declared gap: `iceFlow` is a heuristic accumulation rather than a Glen's-law velocity, so a rigorous g^3 on it is precision theatre. Decisive on top of that, a glacial valley is 1-5 km against a 15.19 km mesh cell, so the process is SUB-GRID and cannot be resolved here at any gravity. It belongs with the downscaling machinery, which has to persist sub-grid hypsometry anyway [step: orogen]. AMENDED 2026-08-22, and this does NOT reopen the row: the objection that a `g^3` velocity on an Earth-calibrated ice mask is precision on the wrong quantity is unchanged. What is new is that the `(rho_i g)^n` term has a published reference implementation to take whole rather than a term to bolt on, in BIG-MITgcm's MITgcmIS -- shallow ice, Glen's law at n = 3, Positive Degree Day mass balance, no basal sliding or calving -- and that it costs about 1 CPU-hour per 40,000 years, so ice sheet flow is a SMALL component rather than a large one. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 4. TAKING THE SOLVER IS NOT TAKING THE MODEL, and the split is where the work is. The flow half is a few lines of algebra and the two routes to it, native on the region mesh or a port off the cubed sphere, are costed by CLIM-62 rather than assumed here. The mass balance half is not usable here at all: its ablation is driven by 2 m air temperature alone, with no shortwave, albedo or spectrum, which is structurally blind to the term this world differs on most over ice, and its accumulation assumes densification into glacial ice is instantaneous, which is GRAV-8's missing physics assumed away. So the deliverable from that paper is Eq. 2 to 4, and `A_dot` is the other ninety percent. GRAVITY ENTERS AT FOUR POWERS, NOT ONE, 2026-08-22, from SICOPOLIS's own algebra in `references/climber-x/src/ice_sico/`. The g^3 velocity scaling this row states is CONFIRMED independently: driving stress is g^1, Glen `creep = sigma^2` makes it g^3, so 2.23x. TWO THINGS THIS ROW DOES NOT CARRY. (1) STRAIN HEATING IS g^4, `creep(sigma)*sigma^2`, giving 2.91x -- the thermal feedback is a HIGHER power than the flow, so a simulated ice sheet here goes temperate more readily than the velocity scaling implies, and temperate ice re-enters the flow through the rate factor and the sliding switch. (2) BASAL SLIDING IS ONLY g^(p-q), which is g^1 under the default Weertman exponents p=3 q=2, against g^3 for deformation -- SO THE DEFORMATION-TO-SLIDING RATIO SHIFTS BY g^2 = 1.71x AND THE MODE OF FLOW CHANGES, not just its speed. `c_slide` is dimensional, `m/(a*Pa^(p-q))`, so its Earth-tuned value is wrong here by exactly that factor. AND TWO EARTH GRAVITIES HIDE IN PER-METRE COEFFICIENTS WITH NO `G` ON THE LINE, failure-mode class 32 in its unit form: `BETA = 8.7d-04 K/m`, the Clausius-Clapeyron gradient per metre OF ICE, is `dTm/dp` times `rho_i*g` and must become 1.136e-3 here, propagating into the pressure-melting point, the cold-temperate transition position and temperate-layer drainage; and the sub-shelf freezing point's 7.64e-4 per metre is the same shape, becoming 9.98e-4. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 45a-b. AND A CHEAP ISOSTASY IMPLEMENTATION WITH A NON-OBVIOUS SIGN, 2026-08-22 -- adjacent to this row rather than answering it, since Landlab carries no glacial erosion law. Its `flexure` component is not a plate PDE but a superposition of analytic point-load Green's functions, with Airy as a one-line short-circuit. Gravity enters at exactly ONE place, the mantle specific weight, at power 1. What propagates is worth stating because the sign surprises: flexural parameter goes as `g^-1/4` (0.935x here), deflection per unit LOAD IN NEWTONS as `g^-1/2` (0.875x), but **deflection per unit ice or sediment THICKNESS as `g^+1/2`, 1.143x** -- because a load is a weight, so heavier gravity makes a given thickness depress the bed MORE even though response per newton falls. Airy cancels gravity exactly. Two defects before copying: the 1-D class omits the cell-area factor the 2-D path applies, so its result is off by the grid spacing, and the gFlex wrapper's step method calls a name that does not exist. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 53c. AND THE MISSING TERM HAS A SOURCE, 2026-08-22. iSOSIA's `source/glacial.c:1375-1470` carries BOTH erosion terms in about 90 lines of C with no solver coupling -- quarrying after Iverson (2012) as `q = Kq*pe^3*u_b*(slope+0.55)^2`, and abrasion as `a = Ka*u_b^ap*sqrt(1+bslope^2)*cos(bslope)` with an optional `pe^3` variant and a sediment-cover factor. IT IS COMPLETELY SEPARABLE: it reads per-cell scalars and writes erosion rates. AND THE GRAVITY ENTRY POINT IS EXPLICIT AND LOAD-BEARING: line 1416 sets `pe = 0.01*te` with the comment recording that `te` is normalised by `rho_ice*g`, so that 0.01 IS EARTH'S GRAVITY BAKED INTO A CONSTANT and becomes 0.01306 here. With `pe^3` in the quarrying law, **gravity enters quarrying as g^3 INDEPENDENTLY of the g^3 already priced through Glen's law** -- which is precisely the term this row says is absent. The real cost is not the law but its second input: effective pressure needs a subglacial hydrology assumption, where sliding speed comes from the ice dynamics already held. The coefficients are Earth-calibrated so absolute erosion rates are not transferable, BUT THE GRAVITY SCALING IS CALIBRATION-FREE, which is what this row asks for. `notes/external-source-inventory.md`

THE TWO CEILINGS SCALE DIFFERENTLY, WHICH IS WHY COUPLING THEM MATTERS HERE, 2026-08-22. This row already requires the mechanical and hydraulic ceilings be coupled rather than treated independently; the exponents say how. HYDRAULIC: `h_max = abs(psi_crit)/(rho_w*g)` goes as `g^-1`, giving 0.766x Earth at 12.81 m/s2. MECHANICAL: Greenhill self-loaded buckling, `(E/(rho*g))^(1/3) * d^(2/3)`, goes as `g^-1/3`, giving 0.915x. Both hold material properties fixed, which is this row's own no-retuning stance. SO THE HYDRAULIC CEILING TIGHTENS ABOUT TWO AND A HALF TIMES FASTER WITH GRAVITY THAN THE MECHANICAL ONE, and a world at 1.306 Earth gravity moves the binding constraint toward hydraulics -- on Earth the two are close enough that either can bind, here the ordering is more likely fixed. The hydraulic figure bounds the GRAVITATIONAL component of xylem tension only; frictional path resistance lowers both columns without changing either exponent. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 41c

title: Snow density is a constant and there is no compaction
description:
Snow density is a constant and there is no compaction, so the one snow term that carries gravity is absent. 330 kg/m3 is declared twice, `rhosnow` at `landmod.f90:73` and `CRHOSN` as a hardcoded `parameter` at `icemod.f90:24`, and both are used the same way, as `dsnowz * 1000 / rhosnow`, to convert water equivalent to physical thickness. That thickness sets the snow thermal layer thicknesses `zsntop` and `zsnowz` in `landmod` and the combined ice-plus-snow threshold at `icemod.f90:591`, so the constant reaches surface albedo through cover depth, the ground heat flux through layer thickness, and the sea ice diagnostic. PALADYN's self-loading term after Kojima (1967) is LINEAR IN `g`, so at 12.81 against 9.81 m/s2 compaction runs 1.306x Earth's for the same load and viscosity and this planet's simulated snowpack should sit thinner for the same water equivalent

Source: `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 3b, `notes/audits/inherited-earth-constants.md`
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
open. The DIRECTION is known and one-signed; the MAGNITUDE is not, because the viscosity depends on temperature and load and this world's snow temperatures are not Earth's -- so a prognostic density is the only route to a number, and a re-chosen constant would be a second guess wearing the first one's clothes. EXPLORATION: the deliverable is what the term is worth on cover depth and albedo, priced offline against an existing climatology before any source change. Deduplicating the two declarations is correctness-neutral and available immediately, and it is not cosmetic: the `icemod` copy is a hardcoded `parameter`, beyond namelist reach, so it cannot be bracketed where it stands [step: rebuild_binaries, bootstrap_run]. MODERATED 2026-08-22 by a third implementation. ClimaLand declares `AbstractDensityModel` and ships exactly one, `MinimumDensityModel`, computing `rho = rho_min*(1-q_l) + rho_l*q_l` -- a minimum dry-snow density blended toward liquid by liquid fraction, with NO self-loading compaction and no gravity term. So two of three land models omit compaction entirely, and this model's constant is CONVENTIONAL at this complexity level rather than anomalous. That is a real difference from PHYS-14's flat band arrays, where the structure existed and the value denied it; here the structure is absent nearly everywhere. IT DOES NOT MAKE THE TERM UNIMPORTANT, and the reason is the one that raised the question: a term that can be omitted on Earth is one whose EARTH magnitude somebody judged small, and that judgement does not transfer at 1.306 g without being re-made. So this row's question is not why the term is missing -- it is missing almost everywhere -- but whether the Earth-calibrated judgement of negligibility survives this planet, which is the price this row already asks for. FOR THE PRICING: no model does all of it. ClimaLand captures wet-snow density through liquid content, which PALADYN explicitly neglects; PALADYN captures fresh-snow temperature dependence and self-loading, which ClimaLand omits. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 23d. A THIRD RUNG EXISTS, AND A SECOND PATH TO ALBEDO, 2026-08-22. ClimaLand's `MinimumDensityModel` sits between the constant and PALADYN's prognostic compaction: `rho_snow = rho_min*(1-q_l) + rho_liq*q_l`, interpolating toward liquid water by LIQUID MASS FRACTION with depth diagnosed from it. It has no load term and therefore NO GRAVITY TERM, so it does not answer this row's argument, which stands -- but it shows a density responsive to melt state is available without solving compaction, and the constant here misses that effect as well as the gravity one. SEPARATELY AND MORE IMPORTANT FOR THIS ROW'S SCOPE: ClimaLand's snow albedo multiplies by `min(1 - beta*(rho_snow/rho_liq - x0), 1)`, so in peer practice snow density reaches albedo DIRECTLY as a grain-size proxy and not only through cover depth as this row has it. At the 330 kg/m3 constant that factor is 0.874. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 37a

title: Glacier orography is built from Earth's mass and radius rather than the model's gravity.
description:
Glacier orography is built from Earth's mass and radius rather than the model's gravity. `glaciermod.f90:352-356` computes `radius = 6.371e6` and `grav = gconst*p_mass/(radius+dz)**2` with `p_mass` Earth's mass, evaluating to 9.8200 m/s2 against the model's `ga = 12.81`. Glacier thickness is converted to geopotential with that value and every reader divides by `ga` to recover metres, INCLUDING PRINTOUTS IN THE SAME FILE, so **a glacier enters the orography at 0.767 of its physical thickness, understated by 23.3 percent**. The `dz` recovered from ground geopotential on the line above is wrong by the reciprocal for the same reason, and `radius = 6.371e6` overrides a latitude-dependent ellipsoid form sitting commented out two lines up, leaving the WGS84 constants dead

Source: `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 56b

title: Declare this world's ROTATION DIRECTION and its PRIME MERIDIAN
description:
Declare this world's ROTATION DIRECTION and its PRIME MERIDIAN, both of which are currently defaulted rather than chosen. `config/planet.yaml` carries a signless `rotation_hours: 30.0` and nothing anywhere says prograde or retrograde; the model runs it prograde by omission, because a positive rotation period becomes a positive rotation speed. `maps/README.md` says the prime meridian is drawn heavier and nothing says which meridian it is or what fixes it. THESE ARE COUPLED, and the IAU convention is what couples them: `archinal2018-iau-cartographic-coordinates-and-rotational-elements.pdf` defines prograde as `W` increasing with time and retrograde as `W` decreasing, where `W` is the angle from the ascending node to the prime meridian -- so rotation direction and meridian phase are one declaration, not two. The report also provides for exactly this world's case: "for planets or satellites with no accurately observable fixed surface features, the expression for W defines the prime meridian", so what is available here is a PHASE, not a landmark. Longitude is positive east by construction -- `maps/projections.py` fixes the handedness -- which is IAU-correct for planetocentric and is nowhere written as a decision

Source: `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 49c, `references/archinal2018-iau-cartographic-coordinates-and-rotational-elements.pdf`
notes:
From archive/tasks.md closing note:
done 2026-08-22 as DETERMINED rather than chosen: all three were already fixed by the code, so the deliverable was a declaration of an existing state and nothing downstream moved. `config/planet.yaml` now carries `rotation_direction: prograde`, `longitude_positive: east` and `prime_meridian: orogen_export_zero`, with the evidence in `docs/src/reference/config-rationale.md` and the graticule line in `maps/README.md`. PROGRADE IS NOT EXPRESSIBLE OTHERWISE: `radmod.f90:solang` builds the hour angle so the subsolar column index falls with time, `plasimmod.f90:253` sets a positive `plavor`, and `exoplasim/__init__.py:2635` derives `ROTSPD` from a signless positive period, so retrograde has no representation on this path at all. title: The water table's dependence structure is wrong
description:
The water table's dependence structure is wrong, and it is not resolution and not the arithmetic. Measured on Earth at three cell sizes: the model is a monotone function of recharge, Spearman -0.90 to -0.93 where the truth is -0.27, and carries no elevation signal at all, -0.047 to -0.003, while the observations' strengthens as cells shrink, +0.125 to +0.199. The suspect is the sink rather than the transmissivity: with `E(h) = et_max exp(-(z-h)/lambda)` the supply-and-sink balance has the closed form `d = lambda ln(et_max A / supply)`, which `et_balance_depth` computes directly and which mentions no neighbour, so at `lambda` = 1 m it is a local clamp that can express a few metres of range from recharge alone and leaves nothing for the lateral term to organise

Source: `hydrography/notes/earth-calibration-criterion.md`, `hydrography/notes/water-table-convergence.md`
notes:
From archive/tasks.md closing note:
done 2026-08-20, and the answer is neither of the two things this row first blamed. CORRECTION, and it is this row's own: an earlier draft proposed re-running with Fan's depth-decaying transmissivity and said GW-9's argument against it "was never measured". Both halves were wrong. The argument IS quantitative and sits in `groundwater.py:transmissivity`: `exp(h/f)` is convex, so a cell mean over a water table varying within the cell by `sigma` carries `exp(sigma^2/2f^2)`, and 100 m of sub-grid relief against the 0.95 m `f` Fan reaches on steep bedrock makes that `exp(5000)` -- not a correction to apply but a statement that the parameterisation has no value at this cell size, and refining to 7.60 km does not rescue it. And the proposed experiment is the one that already failed: `water-table-convergence.md` records that Picard on the transmissivity LIMIT-CYCLES, because `T` moves by a factor of e per e-folding length so the map is not a contraction, and the damping that stopped the oscillation held the water balance residual flat instead of converging. Two solvers died there. Do not re-run it. MEASURED INSTEAD. The sink does set depth locally: median depth is linear in `lambda`, 5.12/10.23/25.51/50.86/126.35 m at 1/2/5/10/25 m, and rho(model, recharge) is pinned at -0.90 throughout. But raising `D` from 100 m to 20 km moves rho(model, elevation) -0.047 to +0.466 and rho(model, recharge) -0.902 to -0.245, bracketing the observed +0.125 and -0.272, so the dependence structure IS reachable with the formulation in hand, and agreement still does not follow: Pearson stays between +0.058 and +0.101 across `D` over 200-fold, `lambda` over 25-fold, and the sink on or off. SECOND CORRECTION: this row and GW-6 quoted Pearson and said no skill. On RANK the model has Spearman +0.276, +0.291 at best, which is not nothing and the claim is withdrawn. What it is, though, is exactly the recharge field's own rank agreement, -0.272, so the flow solve recovers what its forcing already carried and adds under 0.02. R^2 stays negative and worsens with `D`, -0.365 to -7.025, because the spread overshoots to 45 and 75 m against the observed 28.5. So the limit is the INPUTS, not the formulation and not the mesh: recharge, GLHYMPS at 15 km and a cell-mean elevation do not determine this water table, and no rewriting of a flow equation adds information its forcing lacks. What would reopen it is a better forcing, not a better solver: a recharge product that is not itself a climatology-derived proxy, or a permeability field with real aquifer structure rather than surface lithology. The saturated-thickness form `T = K (h - z_bottom)` remains the one untried formulation worth a look, being linear in head and so free of both the Jensen term and the factor of e that killed the exponential, but on this evidence it would be tidying rather than a fix [step: hydrography]

On 73,451 bores the USGS labels unconfined -- a water table, which is what the solver computes, rather than the potentiometric head a confined bore reads -- the cell-mean correlation is +0.2599 against Australia's +0.0703, and the model's spread is 20.72 m against an observed 28.94 where in Australia it was 1.91 against 18.36. THE FINDING IS A REGIME. Where the sink takes the recharge locally the steady state collapses to `lambda ln(et_max A / supply)` and the flow solve contributes no variance; where lateral flow carries it the solve does real work, which is why the same model behaves differently on two continents. That is measurable per cell, so `water_table.nc` now ships `sink_fraction` beside the depth and a consumer can ask which of three cases a cell is in: a recharge map near 1, a pinned and seeping cell when `at_surface` is also set, or a flow solution.
