title: Groundwater leaves an unconfined aquifer through unmapped first and second order gullies
description:
Groundwater leaves an unconfined aquifer through unmapped first and second order gullies at hundreds of metres, not by crossing a 15.19 km cell to a mapped river, and the solver knows only the mapped network. So recharge has no local outlet and piles up until a REGIONAL gradient can carry it, which is the shape GW-21 measured: without the evapotranspiration sink 91.4% of cells pin at the surface, and with it the depth is a local recharge balance. The discarded input is real and is the right size. Binning the 1.855 km ETOPO into the 15.19 km Australian mesh, at a median 95 pixels a cell, the within-cell relief the mean throws away is 14.8 m of standard deviation and 25.9 m from mean to minimum at the median, against an observed water table depth whose median is 7.6 to 9.8 m. The relief being averaged out is about three times the signal being predicted

Source: `hydrography/notes/earth-calibration-criterion.md`, `docs/src/reference/external-data.md`
notes:
From archive/tasks.md closing note:
done, tested at its bounding limit 2026-08-20, and it does not hold, but the investigation found a real defect and that is the part to keep. `C -> infinity` is a fixed head at the cell's own valley floor, which `fixed_head_m` supplies for free, so the family is bounded without a solver term: 22,284 of 26,372 Australian land cells have 10 m or more of relief to vent into, at a median of 30 m, and draining them INVERTS the correlation below the cell mean, +0.0703 to -0.0575, and costs below the bore, +0.1341 to +0.0492, over-draining to a median 25.5 m against an observed 12.9. Both ends of the family are without skill, so a finite `C` would have to beat both, which nothing measured suggests. THE DEFECT, which is the useful half: the model's depth hung from the DEM CELL MEAN and the bore's from the ground at the bore, two different surfaces, and bores sit a mean 8.4 m below their cell mean because wells are in valleys. Hanging both from the DEM takes Pearson +0.0703 to +0.1341 with NO change to the model, the largest single improvement anywhere in this work, and it means every earlier score including GW-3's and GW-21's was measured against the wrong surface. It is still not skill: R2 -3.05, spread 36.18 m against 28.19 observed, because a flat cell head plus each bore's own ground gives the depth all of the relief. Do NOT mix the observation's own surveyed elevation in: it disagrees with the DEM at sd 51.97 m and that lands whole on the residual, R2 -18.0. What remains open is the middle of the bracket rather than the drain: the true within-cell behaviour sits between a model spread of 3.96 m and 36.18 m with the observations at 28.19, which is a three-number target for any sub-grid parameterisation. Superseded approach kept for the record: a head-dependent sub-grid drain per cell rather than a finer mesh, `Q = C max(0, h - z_valley)`, with `z_valley` from the within-cell DEM minimum or `mean - 2 sigma` and `C` scaled by a drainage-density proxy. That is a Robin condition and the solver has no term for it; the existing `fixed_head_m` gives its `C -> infinity` limit for free and BOUNDS the effect, so run that first. TWO THINGS TO WATCH, both from measurements already taken. A direct correlation of within-cell relief against observed depth is only -0.10 Spearman against recharge's -0.27, but that test is confounded by the bias `external-data.md` records from Fan, that wells sit in valleys, so the bores already report valley-floor depths and relief cannot predict them; the real mismatch is that a CELL-MEAN head is being scored against VALLEY-SITED bores, which is what this term would fix. And a sub-grid drain is another LOCAL sink, so it risks reproducing the evapotranspiration sink's pathology; the difference that matters is that its balance is set by terrain, `h = z_valley + Q/C`, where the sink's is set by recharge, `d = lambda ln(et_max/supply)`, which is the dependence GW-21 found missing. Falsifier: Pearson rising off 0.07 and rho(model, elevation) moving toward the observations' +0.20. NOTE THE ASYMMETRY: this is measurable on Earth, where a 1.855 km DEM sits under a 15.19 km cell, and NOT on Vesper, where `notes/audits/orogen-resolution.md` finds the generator designs nothing below about 20 km, so `z_valley` there would have to be parameterised rather than measured. That is GW-6 with a job to do [step: hydrography]
close_reason: done, tested at its bounding limit 2026-08-20, and it does not hold, but the investigation found a real defect and that is the part to keep.

title: Depth-dependent transmissivity is the governor the model lacks
description:
Depth-dependent transmissivity is the governor the model lacks, and it is not the same lever as transmissivity MAGNITUDE. GW-21 raised constant `D` from 100 m to 20 km and did move the dependence structure onto the observed values, rho(model, elevation) -0.047 to +0.466 and rho(model, recharge) -0.902 to -0.245, but that raises `T` everywhere at once. A depth-dependent `T` raises it only where the table is SHALLOW, which is a self-limiting local governor rather than a global flattening, and the uniform sweep cannot stand in for it

Source: `hydrography/notes/water-table-convergence.md`, `hydrography/notes/earth-calibration-criterion.md`
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
open, and NOT via Fan's exponential, which is excluded twice over and measured both times: `exp(h/f)` is convex so a cell mean carries `exp(sigma^2/2f^2)`, which at 100 m of sub-grid relief against the 0.95 m `f` Fan reaches on steep bedrock is `exp(5000)`, and Picard on it LIMIT-CYCLES because `T` moves by a factor of e per e-folding length so the map is not a contraction. Two solvers died there; do not re-run it. The form to try is saturated thickness, `T = K (h - z_bottom)`, the textbook unconfined case the constant `D` currently approximates as confined. It is depth-selective, so it carries the governor; it is LINEAR in head, so cell-averaging is exact and there is no Jensen term; and it is Boussinesq, which under the Kirchhoff substitution `u = (h - z_bottom)^2 / 2` is exactly linear for uniform `K` and `z_bottom`, so the fixed point that killed the exponential does not arise. The `h <= z` box constraint survives the substitution monotonically, as `u <= (z - z_bottom)^2 / 2`, so the complementarity structure is kept [step: hydrography]

title: Every Earth score this project has recorded hangs the model's depth from the DEM CELL MEAN
description:
Every Earth score this project has recorded hangs the model's depth from the DEM CELL MEAN and the observation's from the ground at the bore. Those are different surfaces: measured on 48,552 Australian bores, the DEM at a bore sits a mean 8.4 m below its cell mean, because wells are in valleys, which is the bias Fan states and `external-data.md` records. Hanging both from the DEM takes Pearson +0.0703 to +0.1341 with no change to the model at all, which is the largest single improvement found in this work and makes it a measurement defect rather than a modelling one

A joint least squares on model and `delta` reaches R2 +0.0208 against a statistical fit's 0.2098. `--surface dem-at-bore` stays available and labelled, and this sharpens GW-21: the model does not merely fail to add to its recharge forcing, it is out-predicted by pure geometry carrying no groundwater physics at all. The corrected scoring is not simply better: Pearson nearly doubles while R2 goes -0.365 to -3.05 because the spread goes to 36.18 m against 28.19 observed, since a flat cell head plus each bore's own ground gives the depth ALL of the within-cell relief. Neither surface is right and GW-23 brackets the truth between them, so the honest default may be to report both rather than pick. And restating the archived numbers matters: GW-3's R2 = 0.017 against a bar of 0.07, and GW-21's conclusion that the inputs limit the score, were both measured against the wrong surface. Neither verdict flips, since +0.1341 is still far under the 0.2098 a statistical fit reaches, but the numbers quoted should say which surface they used. Do NOT reach for the observation's own surveyed elevation as the third option: it disagrees with the DEM at sd 51.97 m, median -0.28 m, so it is scatter rather than offset and it lands whole on the residual, giving R2 -18.0 [step: hydrography]

title: Compute a compound topographic index on the native mesh and derive a saturated-AREA closure
description:
Compute a compound topographic index on the native mesh and derive a saturated-AREA closure from it, which is the quantity GW-6 declared unrecoverable as a DEPTH. `f_sat = f_sat_max * exp(-f_grad * z_grad)` under TOPMODEL is how PALADYN obtains wetland area without resolving the valley-to-ridge gradient, and the change of quantity is the point: a per-cell saturated FRACTION rather than the per-cell depth GW-3 and GW-22 measured as regime-dependent. PALADYN takes `f_sat_max` from ETOPO1 because CLIMBER-X has no sub-grid terrain; here the 15.19 km region mesh under a roughly 300 km T42 cell IS that population, and `hydrography` already holds the upslope contributing area the index needs beside a local slope. SHAPE: one artifact per (build, grid) on the coupling-matrix precedent, carrying the index and the closure, with `f_grad` DECLARED and bracketed rather than fitted. It is NOT GRID-2's hypsometry -- an elevation distribution is not a topographic index -- though both come off the same mesh

Source: `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 3a, `hydrography/notes/earth-calibration-criterion.md`
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
open, and it must be scored against something that can FAIL before any consumer takes it: the fraction is untested here, inheriting the depth's bias through `z_grad` is the obvious failure mode, and the bar is declared before the score. Use the same two-continent observation sets the depth was scored on, which are already cached. Consumers are WET-2's wetness classification, SURF-7's discharge mask and LSHY-6's mosaic, and none may take it before that score exists. A DECISION rides along and must be stated rather than defaulted: PALADYN estimates its grid-cell mean water table from column water content and not from a lateral solve, so whether that estimator and this project's Dupuit-Forchheimer solution are reconciled or kept as separate estimators is open [step: hydrography, groundwater]. A SECOND INDEPENDENT IMPLEMENTATION, WITH FOUR THINGS THIS ROW LACKS, 2026-08-22. ClimaLand's `src/standalone/Soil/Runoff/Runoff.jl` implements SIMTOP, Niu et al. (2005). (1) A FACTOR OF TWO AND ONE CONSTANT FOR BOTH FLUXES: `f_sat = min(f_max*exp(-f_over/2*z), 1)` while `R_ss = R_sb*exp(-f_over*z)`, so the surface decay is HALF the subsurface decay and a single calibrated constant sets both -- bracketing it moves surface and subsurface runoff together, which the form as stated here does not show. (2) The `min(...,1)` cap is explicit. (3) PARAMETER PROVENANCE SPLITS EXACTLY THE WAY THIS ROW WANTS: `f_over` and `R_sb` are labelled "calibrated" in their docstrings, while `f_max` is "computed from the topographic index CDF per grid cell" -- terrain-derived, and computable here from the region mesh -- which independently supports declaring and bracketing `f_grad` rather than fitting it. (4) ICE: the saturated column is computed TWICE, including ice for the surface saturated fraction and liquid-only for the subsurface flux, so frozen ground makes saturation-excess surface runoff but no subsurface flow. Neither this row nor PALADYN's form carries that, and it matters in a cold winter hemisphere. ON THE DECISION THIS ROW FLAGS: ClimaLand also estimates water table depth from column water content rather than a lateral solve, so the column estimator is the field's normal practice and the Dupuit-Forchheimer solution is the departure that needs the argument. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 36. A THIRD CONSUMER OF THIS INDEX, WITH A CALIBRATION REQUIREMENT, 2026-08-22. CLIMBER-X's three wetland-extent schemes at `src/lnd/surface_hydro.f90:565-613` -- SIMTOP, DYPTOP and a CTI-CDF lookup -- all key off a per-gridcell compound topographic index, after PALADYN and ClimaLand's SIMTOP. THE CONSTRAINT THAT RIDES ALONG: `cti_mean_crit = 5.5` is an absolute threshold below which no wetland forms, so this row's index needs an absolute calibration and not merely a consistent ranking, and the score this row demands has to test the index on that footing. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 42d

title: Valley-to-ridge water table texture is sub-grid and stays sub-grid
description:
Valley-to-ridge water table texture is sub-grid and stays sub-grid: Fan et al. (2013) put the well-articulated gradient at decameters to kilometres, against a 15.19 km region

Source: `hydrography/notes/groundwater-scoping.md` section 5, `hydrography/notes/groundwater-et-sink.md`
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
open as a DECLARED gap on GRAV-6's precedent, and now MEASURED TWICE. GW-3 scored the solver at 70,119 Australian bores with no skill at all. GW-15 then added the physics that was actually missing, removed the surface pinning entirely, and the skill did not appear: Pearson +0.031, 0.1% of variance, with the model spanning a factor of 1.9 in depth against the observations' 56.5. The model is a function of recharge at Spearman -0.977 and the real water table is not, at -0.156. So the variance is terrain at a scale this mesh cannot hold, and no sink, thickness or conductivity recovers it. NOW ANSWERED for the resolution route, `notes/audits/orogen-resolution.md`: a generation at four times the region count adds at most 12% to relief at any separation from 5 to 200 km, and the pre-erosion substrate is converged outright, so a finer Orogen does not hold the missing texture and cannot supply it. The generator's noise sits at fixed physical wavelengths and its erosion cuts at whatever the mesh scale is. Sub-grid hypsometry has to come from a parameterisation or external data. CONFIRMED INDEPENDENTLY ON EARTH 2026-08-20, which is the stronger test because Earth's topography has real content at every scale where Vesper's generator has none. The same case at 15.19, 10.74 and 7.60 km raises the CEILING from 0.6335 to 0.7408 and more than doubles the model's own spread, 1.91 to 4.33 m, while Pearson does not move at all: +0.0703, +0.0665, +0.0711. The dependence structure says why. The model is a monotone function of recharge at every cell size, Spearman -0.90 to -0.93, where the truth is -0.27; and against elevation the two diverge as the mesh refines, the observations' terrain signal strengthening +0.125 to +0.161 to +0.199 while the model's decays to -0.003. So GW-6 is NOT a resolution gap and was never going to be closed by a finer mesh on either planet. GW-21 then took the formulation apart and found the limit is neither: on RANK the model reaches Spearman +0.28, which is precisely its recharge field's own +0.27, so it recovers what its forcing carried and adds nothing, and the dependence structure can be tuned onto the observed values by transmissivity alone without agreement following. The binding constraint is the input fields IN THAT REGION, and GW-22 then showed the qualifier matters: scored on United States bores labelled unconfined the same model reaches Pearson +0.2599 against Australia's +0.0703, with a spread of 20.72 m against 28.94 where Australia gave 1.91 against 18.36. So this gap is regional rather than universal. Where the evapotranspiration sink takes the recharge locally the depth is a recharge map and the sub-grid texture this row is about is the least of its problems; where lateral flow carries it the solve does real work. `water_table.nc` ships `sink_fraction` to tell the two apart per cell. Which regime VESPER is in is not yet established, because the current forcing is a bootstrap climatology on pre-carve terrain. SHARPENED 2026-08-20: the 0.28 those rows measured against was never computed by anything, and is corrected to 0.2098, what a gradient boosting fit over every resolvable field reaches held out with the model EXCLUDED, from `earth_calibration.py --stage benchmark`. Both halves hold at once: the fields support only 0.2098 against a between-cell ceiling of 0.6335, and the model reaches +0.0193 alone and ADDS to that fit, 0.2098 to 0.2381. An earlier draft of this row called it information-negative from the -0.0467 and 0.1435 against 0.1411 measured on bores that fail the consistency filter; on the clean subset it is not, and that reading is withdrawn. See GW-21 [step: hydrography]

title: Fan's e-folding constants are read off a REGIONAL DIP rather than a hillslope gradient
description:

Source: `hydrography/notes/groundwater-scoping.md` section 7b
notes:
From archive/tasks.md closing note:
done 2026-08-20, and settling it found a SECOND and larger defect that subsumes the first. The slope mismatch is real: Fan fits `f = a/(1 + b*slope)` against a hillslope gradient at about 1 km, `local_slope_deg` is a 15.19 km plane fit that `minerals/README.md` documents as an upper bound on regional dip, and gradient falls with the scale it is measured over, so `f` comes back too large. BUT THE FLOOR IS INCOHERENT AT ANY SLOPE, and that is what broke GW-1. Cell-averaging `T = A exp(h/f)` over a water table varying within the cell by `sigma` gives a factor `exp(sigma^2 / 2 f^2)`; at 100 m of sub-grid relief against the bedrock floor of 0.95 m that is `exp(5000)`, which is not a correction but the statement that the parameterisation CANNOT BE EVALUATED AT A CELL MEAN. The solver's measured `|z|/f` of 4588, against an `exp` argument limit near 709 in double precision, is the same fact arriving as an overflow. The requirement is a scale rather than a tuned value: the effective e-folding length for a cell cannot be smaller than the relief that cell contains, which makes the factor `exp(0.5)`. Fan's numbers are not wrong, they are being asked a question three orders of magnitude from where they were fitted. Consequence for GW-1: the blocker is the FORMULATION, not the iteration, and Newton would converge a model that applies a metre-scale parameter at 15 km -- worse than not converging, because the answer would look like a result. The sub-grid relief this needs is the same quantity GRAV-6 parks glacial erosion behind

title: The endorheic basin catalogue is resolution-limited rather than physics-limited.
description:
The endorheic basin catalogue is resolution-limited rather than physics-limited. `selectionCriteria` declares floors of 0.05 km depth, 1000 km2 area and 12 mesh cells, and at the build's spacing the 12-cell floor is 3526 km2, so nothing below 2646 km2 survives and the carve list is drawn from a set the mesh floored rather than the criterion selected. Preserved goes 3,621, 6,345, 9,419 across one, two and four times the region count, and at four times the smallest preserved depression is 1000 km2 exactly, the declared floor having finally taken over from the mesh. The large end does NOT settle: the biggest basin is 3,059,665 km2 at the build and 5,499,601 at four times, one south polar basin remeasured 80% larger rather than two merging, and it is not erosional, since catalogues with `--glacial 0` are byte-identical

Source: `notes/audits/orogen-resolution.md`
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
open. Not a defect in the floor, which is a signal-to-noise criterion and correctly relaxes as the mesh becomes able to hold smaller depressions. It is a statement about what this build can see: the declared physical floor only starts binding near 8.8M regions. DECIDED 2026-08-20: the next generation raises the region count, and the reference export at 10,000,005 is registered as `precarve-craton-10m`. It is NOT the build to activate, because a generation meant to be commissioned should also carry the PHYS-13 ice-mask decision; the two changes belong in one generation, not two. The count is settled at 10,000,005 by the saturation measurement below, the reference export carries the full grid set and its hash is registered in `lib/orogen.py`, so remaining work is one generation at that count carrying PHYS-13's mask, and then pointing `source_build` at it. THE LADDER IS NOW T21/T42/T85/T127/T170, T63 is dropped, and `precarve-craton-10m` carries all five with every grid verified to the same terrain hash; `rebuild_binaries.py`'s MATRIX gains the two missing rungs so no truncation has an export without an executable. What is left of this row is the DECISION to activate, which rule 7 makes consequential and which should carry PHYS-13's ice-mask change in the same generation. CEILING ON THE COUNT, measured: Orogen's terrain noise sits at fixed physical wavelengths and the finest it DESIGNS is about 20 km, so `elevation_pre_erosion` gains only 8% of semivariance per lag doubling below 10 km against 26% at 50 km. The 7.60 km mesh at 10,000,005 regions already oversamples that floor by 2.6x. MEASURED AT 25,000,000 and the catalogue SATURATES there: preserved goes 3,621, 6,345, 9,419, 9,649 across 2.5M, 5M, 10M and 25M, so four times again the region count adds 2.4% against the 48% the previous step added, while detected depressions keep climbing 286,534 to 646,725 because every new one is below the declared 1000 km2 floor. That is the crossover working as predicted: once `minCells` stops binding the physical criterion governs and refining further buys nothing. So 10,000,005 is not adequate-with-margin, it is where this converges, and it is the recommendation; 25M costs 3,875 s and 21.1 GB against 10M's 1,093 s and 9.0 GB, superlinear in time, for 230 more basins; 50,000,000 is 3.40 km rather than the sub-km it looks like, since edge goes as the square root of the count, and a 1 km edge needs about 577 million regions, roughly 17 hours and 517 GB. Below the floor a finer mesh manufactures erosion texture at the mesh scale rather than resolving terrain. Sub-km relief is a synthesis problem, not a region-count one. Note what activating costs under rule 7: `precarve-craton` has been consumed by a commissioned run, so superseding it makes the climatology and everything derived from it worthless rather than stale [step: orogen]

title: The pedology parameter that closes the loop to the climate is uncited. pedogenesis.yaml's
description:
The pedology parameter that closes the loop to the climate is uncited. `pedogenesis.yaml`'s `water:` block gives volumetric plant-available water as "standard textbook mid-range values", and the `catena:` block's four constants carry reasoning but no source and no `declared` label

Source: `notes/audits/absent-and-inherited-physics.md` finding 4, `docs/src/pipeline/steps.md` section 3.6
notes:
From archive/tasks.md closing note:
done 2026-08-18. Two papers fetched and read, and BOTH turned out to license the mechanism and not the numbers, which is the answer rather than a shortfall. Saxton and Rawls (2006) is the standard texture-to-water basis, 1,722 A-horizon USDA/NRCS samples at 33 and 1500 kPa, and it fixes the SHAPE the block relies on -- plant-available water peaking at intermediate texture. It does not fix the three endmember values, because the regression is over a continuous mixture and the paper excluded samples above 60% clay, so a pure endmember is outside its data; reading values off it would be `docs/src/practice/failure-modes.md` class 9. Heimsath et al. (1997) gives the first empirical soil production function, `-(de/dt) = (77 +/- 9) exp(-(0.023 +/- 0.003) h)` um/yr, and names "mechanical processes as freeze-thaw" as its own reason for the exponential form, which sources the frost term; but its control variable is hillslope CURVATURE where `catena:` uses tan(beta), a stated simplification rather than an equivalence. So all seven constants are labelled DECLARED with brackets, on the `aeolian/config/dust.yaml` model, and `build_soil.py` reports the spread the way the row asked: water capacity comes out 96.1 to 167.7 mm around 127.3, a factor of 1.75 on the field that sets ExoPlaSim's `dwmax` and whose overflow IS its runoff. Re-running the soil to get that exposed a second staleness and rule 7 decided it, as with the albedo: the soil on disk was built from the BOOTSTRAP climatology while `config/planet.yaml` names the baseline, so it was rebuilt on the baseline and code 229 regenerated from it

title: Recheck the playa clastic fraction and what it is derived
description:
Recheck the playa clastic fraction and what it is derived FROM, because it is being quoted as a property of this world and it is neither stable nor reconstructible. FOUR THINGS AT ONCE. (1) IT IS DERIVED FROM ENDORHEISM, not independent of it: `vendor/orogen/js/lithology.js`'s `basin_fill` cover rule fires on `when: (c) => !!c.endorheic` and assigns `evaporite` where `saltCrust` and `playa_clastic` over the rest, so opening a basin removes the flag and the cover reverts to parent material. The fraction therefore moves with the carve list exactly as the endorheic figures do, and rule 9 applies to it: 0.23869 is a pre-carve LIMIT. (2) THE QUANTITY IT DEPENDS ON IS NOT REPORTED. `world_state.json` gives `endorheic_fraction_of_land = 0.7629` beside an `endorheic_note` that carefully distinguishes `drainage_share_of_land` from `basin_floor_share_of_land` -- and the key itself says which it is nowhere. The lithology depends on the second and the reported number appears to be the first. (3) EVAPORITE IS INVISIBLE: the `lithology_land_fractions` block is truncated to six classes and evaporite is below melange's 0.0617, so the basin-fill total, which is playa plus evaporite, cannot be reconstructed from the artifact at all. (4) A STATED FIGURE DOES NOT RECONCILE: `vendor/orogen/tools/README.md` says the split is about 10 percent salt to 90 percent clastic and that this is a planet with "a fifth of its land in closed basins", but playa alone is 0.23869, which under that split implies a basin floor near 0.265

Source: `vendor/orogen/js/lithology.js`, `vendor/orogen/tools/README.md`, `world_state.json`
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
open, and NARROWED to two vendored-prose edits: the measurement is done and all four questions are settled. MEASURED 2026-08-22 on `precarve-craton`, area-weighted over `surface_class` land: basin floor `is_endorheic` 0.267620 of land, playa clastic 0.238693, evaporite 0.028487, basin fill 0.267180, salt share of fill 0.106621, fill share of basin floor 0.99836. Basin fill IS the endorheic set: no fill cell lies outside it, and the 0.000439-of-land residual inside it is basement stripped of its veneer. THE REPORTING HALF IS CLOSED: `scripts/world_state.py` now emits `endorheic_catchment_share_of_land` and `endorheic_basin_floor_share_of_land` as two named keys, and `lithology_land_fractions` is no longer truncated to six, which is what hid `evaporite` at tenth and made basin fill unreconstructible. WHAT IS LEFT is prose in the vendored subtree, so it wants the fork-note convention in `docs/src/reference/vendored-upstreams.md` applied in the same pass: `vendor/orogen/tools/README.md:303-306` says "a fifth", which understates the measured share by about a quarter and carries ~2.8 W/m2 per 0.10 where the measured share gives ~3.9; `vendor/orogen/js/lithology.js:148` says 12.65 percent and ~1.7 W/m2 and needs the same treatment. Both derived figures reproduce from their own share, so each moved with it and the ARGUMENT IS STRONGER, not weaker. A SECOND FIGURE IN THAT PARAGRAPH IS STALE AND DEMONSTRABLY SO: "effective 0.32 rather than 0.50" reproduces exactly from a playa clastic albedo of 0.30, which `lithology.js`'s own header records as corrected to 0.19 on Post et al. (2000); on current albedos and the measured 10.66/89.34 split the effective basin-fill albedo is 0.2231. THE CONSUMER WARNED: LSHY-1's retention closure rests on "a quarter of this land is playa clastic". The magnitude its argument wants is basin FILL at 0.26718 rather than playa alone at 0.23869, and both are pre-carve LIMITS rather than states, so the claim stands at roughly the size it assumed but permanently as an upper bound. `pedology/README.md`'s thermostat table shows the direction, 25.6 percent pre-carve to 15.8 configured to 11.7 projected [step: orogen]

title: Build one versioned, vertically explicit vadose/land-column hydraulic and thermal property
description:
Build one versioned, vertically explicit vadose/land-column hydraulic and thermal property artifact: physical and rootable layer geometry; mineral, organic, andic and weathered-bedrock fractions; porosity, retention curve, wilting/field-capacity/saturation states, conductivity/permeability and heat properties; pressure/head conventions with Vesper gravity; units, provenance and correlated uncertainty cases. Compare pedology AWC, ExoPlaSim `dwmax` and LPJ's Cosby/Lawrence derivation before removing duplicate consumer-side pedotransfer and organic-mixing paths; keep aquifer transmissivity a separately scaled groundwater property joined at the declared contact

Source: `biosphere/notes/soil-land-surface-hydraulic-consistency-audit.md` finding 1
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
open; schema, converter and checked-in-map comparison require no model execution; do not collapse the contract back to one AWC scalar or substitute vadose conductivity for aquifer transmissivity [step: soil, surface_soil_water, lpj_driver]. THE RETENTION CLOSURE IS A FAMILY CHOICE THIS CONTRACT LEAVES IMPLICIT, 2026-08-22. `references/climaland/src/standalone/Soil/retention_models.jl` declares `AbstractSoilHydrologyClosure` with `vanGenuchten` and `BrooksCorey` as its two implementations, and parameterises `RichardsParameters` over the closure type so the choice is made at construction. This project sits entirely in ONE family without having recorded that a family was chosen: LPJ-GUESS's Cosby (1984) derivation is a Clapp-Hornberger form and PALADYN uses Clapp-Hornberger too. The two differ most in their tails -- Brooks-Corey has a discontinuous air-entry point and a power-law tail, van Genuchten is smooth through saturation -- which matters here specifically, because a quarter of this land is playa clastic, so wetting and drying through near-saturation is a common state rather than an edge case. That rests on the PLAYA FRACTION -- which LITH-27 establishes is itself derived from endorheism, since Orogen assigns basin fill on `!!c.endorheic`, so it carries the same pre-carve limit and moves with the carve list. The argument is therefore about a class of surface this terrain produces, not about a settled area, and it survives only in that weaker form until LITH-27 reports what the derived fraction is. NOT an argument for switching: an argument that this contract should carry the closure as a NAMED property with its family stated, so a consumer knows which it is reading and a later comparison has something to vary. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 23b

title: Replace the active ExoPlaSim scalar bucket behind a selectable reduction with a restart-exact
description:
Replace the active ExoPlaSim scalar bucket behind a selectable reduction with a restart-exact climate-side land column that consumes LSHY-1 and produces LSHY-2's infiltration, storage, surface-runoff and drainage terms; register the current bucket, a parsimonious multilayer scheme and gradient-driven flow as explicit hypotheses, include Vesper gravity in potential flow, expose free-drainage/bedrock/aquifer lower boundaries, and serialize every layer, phase and partial accumulator. Treat the current steady groundwater product only as a fixed-head or orbit-mean exchange bracket unless PLHY-4 establishes a transient saturated-storage state; do not synthesize seasonal head

Source: `biosphere/notes/soil-land-surface-hydraulic-consistency-audit.md` findings 2, 3 and 6
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
open; source and analytical reduction/restart fixtures require no simulation, but timing, climate response and solver selection require explicit permission; coordinate the LPJ-only controls under PLHY-2 [step: groundwater, surface_soil_water, baseline_run]. AMENDED 2026-08-22: the parsimonious multilayer hypothesis now has a named candidate at this project's THROUGHPUT rather than a CMIP one. PALADYN is five soil layers to 3.9 m on Clapp-Hornberger properties with a free-drainage lower boundary, `references/climber-x/src/lnd/soil_hydro.f90` and `surface_hydro.f90`, and the licence question is already answered: ExoPlaSim is GPL version 2 or later, so a GPL-3 combination is permitted with the combined work under GPL-3. Take the formulation and not the tree, and its uniform default `ksat`, `psisat` and `b` are Earth configuration that LSHY-1 already owns. `notes/external-model-survey.md` sections 3 and 6. TWO OF THIS ROW'S THREE HYPOTHESES SHIP AS INTERCHANGEABLE COMPONENTS, 2026-08-22. `references/climaland/src/standalone/` carries `Bucket` and `Soil` as peer standalone models against a shared interface, with `Soil/rre.jl` the Richards equation -- so the current bucket and gradient-driven flow, two of the three hypotheses this row wants registered, exist as swappable implementations rather than as a plan. That is the SUMMA pattern of Clark et al. (2015) built, and Clark is already in `references/INDEX.md` as the argument FOR registering them this way. Read it for STRUCTURE only: ClimaLand is CMIP-class and GPU-oriented, so it is not a candidate for adoption, and PALADYN stays the EMIC-class implementation reference because it runs at a comparable cost. `notes/external-model-survey.md` sections 23a and 23c. A PEER IMPLEMENTATION OF THE SAME ABSTRACTION DISAGREES BY AN ORDER OF MAGNITUDE, 2026-08-22, and this project's side is the permissive extreme. Both ExoPlaSim and cGENIE's ENTS scale land evaporation by a soil-moisture factor and differ in that factor: `landmod.f90:418` is LINEAR, `min(1, W/(drhsfull*Wmax))` with `drhsfull = 0.4` at `:53`, so it evaporates at the POTENTIAL RATE for any bucket above 40 percent full; `surflux.F:1334` is QUARTIC, `min(1, (W/bcap)**4)`, reaching potential only at a full bucket. At equal fractional fill the ratio runs 39x at 0.4, 16x at 0.5, 8x at 0.6 and 2x at 0.8, agreeing only when full. Compare the SHAPE only: capacity differs too, ExoPlaSim's `wsmax` being a uniform scalar against ENTS's carbon-dependent `bcap`, and ENTS's `k8`/`k9`/`k10` arrive by namelist and are NOT shipped in the vendored tree, so the capacity half cannot be closed from here. Neither limiter is right and this is a bracket, not an adoption -- but the replacement column this row specifies should carry the limiter as a DECLARED choice with the bracket beside it rather than inheriting the linear form silently. The direction reaches the carve: at a given bucket state the permissive form sends more precipitation to evaporation and less to runoff, and `scripts/error_budget.py` already records E/R as amplified into the carve. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 32a. AND THE LIMITER HAS A SHAPE VOCABULARY PLUS A SCOPE WARNING, 2026-08-22. ClimaLand's `src/standalone/Vegetation/soil_moisture_stress.jl` carries `beta = min(1, max((theta-theta_low)/(theta_high-theta_low),0)**c)`, cited to Egea et al. (2011), `references/egea2011-water-stress-in-coupled-photosynthesis-conductance-models.pdf`. THE THREE PARAMETERS ARE THE RIGHT AXES for the replacement column's limiter and both behaviours above sit on them -- ExoPlaSim at `c = 1` with the knee at 0.4 of capacity, ENTS at `c = 4` at full capacity -- so implementing the general form makes the bracket a runtime selection rather than a code fork. DO NOT CITE EGEA FOR IT: that paper is about water stress in coupled photosynthesis-stomatal conductance models and its beta multiplies PHOTOSYNTHESIS, applied to `An` in `photosynthesis_farquhar.jl:335` and deliberately not re-applied in stomatal conductance, evaluated on ROOT-ZONE AVERAGED moisture weighted by root distribution. ExoPlaSim's `drhs` and ENTS's `beta` multiply the SURFACE EVAPORATION FLUX over vegetated and bare ground alike from a store with no depth. Same algebra, different flux. THE THIRD AXIS SURVIVES THAT CORRECTION AND IS THE USEFUL ONE: `theta_low` is the wilting point or residual water fraction, and both models here pin it at zero, so each approaches zero flux only as its store approaches empty and water held below the wilting point is still available to be removed. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 33

description:
Close the fast vegetation--climate water loop around LSHY-3: choose either a shared/online operator or an explicit fixed-point outer iteration with convergence criteria; have LPJ provide chronology-bound LAI, canopy capacity, stomatal conductance and root demand by source/layer; let the climate-side owner compute interception, soil evaporation, transpiration and latent heat from its actual state; return fulfilled uptake to LPJ and debit it once. notes:

AN EMIC-CLASS CLOSURE OF THIS LOOP IS SMALLER THAN THIS ROW ASSUMES, 2026-08-22. cGENIE's ENTS closes it with THREE ALGEBRAIC FUNCTIONS of two prognostic carbon pools, not a land-surface model: bucket capacity `min(k8, k9 + k10*Csoil)` at `setup_ents.F:474`, roughness `max(0.001, kz0*Cveg)` at `:476`, and a soil albedo interpolating sand to peat in `Csoil` at `initialise_ents.F:239`. ExoPlaSim prescribes all three as `wsmax`, `dz0clim` and `dalbclim`. BE PRECISE ABOUT WHAT THIS DOES NOT SHOW: ENTS has no stomatal term in its evaporation either -- `fv` and `fws` feed photosynthesis, and the comment at `surflux.F:1386` distinguishing bare-soil evaporation from evapotranspiration sits above a formula identical in both cases -- so the entire vegetation-to-water coupling there runs through the capacity. That is the cheap closure worth pricing against this row's fuller one. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 32b

title: Make snow, frozen-soil and thermal state consistent across climate and ecology

title: What is left DECLARED in the downstream prospectivity rules after the 2026-08-17 literature
description:
What is left DECLARED in the downstream prospectivity rules after the 2026-08-17 literature pass: the wet end of the supergene copper window, and any relief or slope term for bauxite or nickel laterite

Source: `docs/src/reference/economic-minerals.md`, `references/INDEX.md`
notes:
From archive/tasks.md closing note:
done 2026-08-18, and the three gaps turned out to be ONE gap. The user obtained the Economic Geology 100th Anniversary Volume after both chapters were surfaced as unfetchable; Sillitoe (2005) `10.5382/AV100.22` and Freyssinet et al. (2005) `10.5382/AV100.21` were cut out of it by page range and read off the page images, the volume's OCR being unreliable enough to print `m/m/y` for `m/m.y.`. **THE WET END DOES NOT EXIST**: Sillitoe p. 736 admits every climate but hyperarid desert and glacial or permafrost ground, and calls tropical the most favourable, so the declared 500 mm/yr cap was contradicted rather than merely unsourced and was removed, not re-derived. What replaced it is the exclusion the source DOES name, on seasonal melting rather than an annual mean. The wet-side control is erosion against water-table descent, and since "erosional efficiency depends chiefly on rainfall and slope steepness" it is the same criterion as the laterites' relief term -- which is why one paper closed all three. **THE RELIEF OMISSION WAS TWO-SIDED**, not one-signed as both rules recorded: too steep strips the profile, too flat impedes leaching. Applied is a 5 degree upper bound on regional dip from Freyssinet p. 685, with the 1 degree lower end deliberately NOT applied as a floor. It removes 0.86% of land but 5.13% of melange, the Ni laterite host. Needed a new field, `lib/orogen.py:local_slope_deg`, a plane fit rather than a steepest drop, with a smoke_test check whose tolerance sits between those two implementations
close_reason: done 2026-08-18, and the three gaps turned out to be ONE gap.

title: Lithium and borate prospectivity rest on a geological association, not on a modelled mechanism
description:
Lithium and borate prospectivity rest on a geological association, not on a modelled mechanism

Source: `docs/src/reference/economic-minerals.md`
notes:
From archive/tasks.md closing note:
done 2026-08-18, and NOT by attrition, which this row warned against. The objection in it is contradicted by a test that could have failed: Risacher and Fritz (2009) sect. 3.5 plot Li and B against water temperature across Bolivian and Chilean groundwaters that are 60% and 78% thermally influenced, and NEITHER RISES -- both "originate from the alteration of volcanic rocks, especially ignimbrites" -- with Risacher et al. (2003) sect. 7.7 reaching it independently. So the hydrothermal flux this pipeline cannot place is not required for the Andean type, the principal Li brine and Quaternary borate province; the Anatolian type does need it and is recorded as unplaceable. THE BORATE RULE WAS WRONG rather than weak: it weighted `arc_basalt` at 1.0, and Helvaci (2019) with Floyd et al. (1998) put the fertile rock at high-silica rhyolitic ignimbrite carrying B and Li TOGETHER. Correcting it left the two rules identical in every key but `name`, which is the tin-and-gem-placer error, so they are now ONE field `brine_lithium_borate` on silcrete's three-settings-one-value precedent. Nature separates them and this pipeline cannot: Bradley et al. (2013) have borate leaving solution as a mineral while Li stays in residual brine, so the borate set CONTAINS the lithium set and only the boundary is open, and placing it needs the release coefficient this task established does not exist -- the same missing number twice, which is the finding. What would split the field again is recorded, and it is a missing NUMBER not missing machinery: hydrography already computes a graded `aridity_index` per basin and `require_no_overflow` discards it for the boolean [step: downstream_prospectivity]
close_reason: done 2026-08-18, and NOT by attrition, which this row warned against.

title: Replace the rainfall proxy for water table depth in the supergene rules with a modelled depth
description:
Replace the rainfall proxy for water table depth in the supergene rules with a modelled depth field. `minerals/config/downstream_prospectivity.yaml` says in its own comments that it substitutes rainfall because nothing better exists, while the mechanism it cites is depth: Reich and Vasconcelos (2015) put oxidation in the vadose zone and secondary sulfides below the water table

Source: `hydrography/notes/groundwater-scoping.md` section 6, `docs/src/reference/economic-minerals.md`
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
open and UNBLOCKED: GW-1 closed 2026-08-20, so the mean depth field exists as the `groundwater` step's output. What is left is a judgement rather than a wait, and GW-3 HAS now supplied the external test, so the judgement can be made on evidence. The verdict is regime-dependent: on Australian bores the model has no per-cell skill, Pearson +0.0703 with a spread of 1.91 m against an observed 18.36, while on United States bores labelled unconfined it reaches +0.2599 with a matched spread. `config/pipeline.yaml`'s gate says plainly that MIN-6 cannot use this field, and that stands for a per-cell depth. What GW-22 adds is the per-cell test rather than a blanket one: `water_table.nc` ships `sink_fraction`, and a prospectivity rule could in principle key on cells where the sink did NOT set the depth. Whether enough of this planet qualifies is not yet knowable, because the current forcing is a bootstrap climatology on pre-carve terrain. It supplies the DEPTH and not the descent RATE, so Sillitoe (2005)'s wet-end control -- erosion in balance with the rate of water table descent -- stays unreachable and stays declared [step: downstream_prospectivity]

title: Fix the prospectivity normalisation, which is unstable across builds. Weights-of-evidence
description:
Fix the prospectivity normalisation, which is unstable across builds. Weights-of-evidence requires a point set of known deposits and REFUSES TO RUN without one, and every validation tool in ArcSDM takes deposit points as a required parameter; there is no unsupervised prospectivity path in the toolbox at all. So the supervised-method tension does not apply here: an exhaustive search of `minerals/` for prior, posterior, contrast, training or AUC returns nothing, and the word it uses is FAVOURABILITY, which is correct for an unsupervised index. THE DEFECT IS ELSEWHERE AND IS REAL: `normalise()` divides by `field[land].max()`, a single cell's value, so A NEW BUILD PRODUCING ONE UNUSUALLY FAVOURABLE CELL RESCALES THE ENTIRE FIELD DOWNWARD. `minerals/README.md` states that comparing one deposit type against another says nothing, which covers the cross-type case and not the temporal one; its argument against quantiles is about the top of the distribution and does not address the stability of the divisor. AND ONE HONEST STRUCTURAL POINT: these fields are untestable within this world by construction, which meets this project's own standard that a check with no possible wrong answer is not a test. The `grounding` attribute grades the provenance of the RULE rather than the correctness of the FIELD -- a good move that no document draws out loud. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 49d

Source: `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 49d
notes:
From archive/tasks.md closing note:
done 2026-08-22, and there were FOUR duplications rather than the three this row named. `minerals/scripts/prospectivity_scale.py` is now the one copy of `normalise`, `host_ceiling` and `host_weight` -- the fourth was `host_weight`, inlined at `build_prospectivity.py:119-124` and defined again at `build_downstream_prospectivity.py:153`. THE DIVISOR IS NOW A PROPERTY OF THE RULE: `input_ranges` in both configs give each modifier's declared range, `ceiling()` mirrors the score expression term for term, and `normalise` RAISES if any land score exceeds the ceiling -- a closed form that disagrees with the expression it bounds has a right answer, so it is a test and not a diagnostic. THE OLD DIVISOR WAS A SEAFLOOR CELL ON A LAND-ONLY FIELD: `r_stress` maxes at 5.5358 over all cells against 4.7084 over land, compressing the stress term by about 3.8x. It is replaced by `stress_reference = 1.449732`, which is Orogen's own `maxStress`, the `STRESS_PERCENTILE = 0.97` quantile of `r_stress` above `STRESS_PROPAGATE_MIN`. VERIFIED AGAINST AN IDENTITY RATHER THAN ASSUMED, and re-verified independently: `min(1, min(1, r_stress/1.449732) * 3.0)` reproduces the exported `r_t_foldBelt` to 1e-6 on 99.39 percent of 1,079,396 land cells, and every one of the 6,600 misses has `r_t_foldBelt == 0`, the cells Orogen skips as internally-ocean. Rounding to 1.45 holds on only 31.58 percent, so the full figure is declared rather than tidied. CONSEQUENCE WORTH KNOWING: orogenic_au's attainable maximum is 6.4 against a raw maximum of 5.4399 on this build, so the field now tops out at 0.850 where the old divisor reported 1.0 by construction. ONE SUBSTANTIVE RULE CHANGE, argued in the config: `ca_excess` was `Ca/HCO3 - 1`, unbounded above, so a single basin at Ca/HCO3 = 40 would set the divisor for every gypsum basin. It is now `1 - HCO3/Ca`, the exact mirror of the alkaline side's `1 - Ca/HCO3`, same ordering and bounded 0-1 by the ratio rather than by a build. NOTED IN PASSING: `elevation.js:543` comments the quantile as 95th where the constant is 0.97.
close_reason: done 2026-08-22, and there were FOUR duplications rather than the three this row named.

title: Establish what a multi-layer column ocean costs and what it is worth. NLEV_OCE = 1
description:
Establish what a multi-layer column ocean costs and what it is worth. `NLEV_OCE = 1` in `oceanmod.f90` is a source constant and the module is already written for `NLEV_OCE > 1`: `vdiffkl` is in `oceanmod_nl`, line 255 branches on it, and line 229 collapses the general case to the slab. What is missing is a layer count, a `dlayer` profile, and a measurement of what the change does to the seasonal amplitude that `mixed_layer_depth_m: 50.0` currently sets on an orbit half Earth's length. EXPLORATION: the deliverable is a viability verdict, a cost and an effect, not the change

Source: `notes/audits/ocean-and-marine-biosphere.md` finding 1
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
open. It is a source constant, so CLAUDE.md rule 4 costs a full `rebuild_binaries.py` pass rather than one executable, and that is most of the price. The prediction A3 requires can be made offline and before anything is compiled: a column of N layers coupled by `vdiffkl` has a computable impulse response, and the seasonal damping follows from it. This is the cheapest change in the note that acts on a term `config/planet.yaml` already declares as ExoPlaSim's default arriving unnamed [step: rebuild_binaries, bootstrap_run]. A SPECTRAL TERM THE SLAB HIDES, 2026-08-22: water's e-folding depth never exceeds 0.51 m anywhere above 0.75 um, and 61.8 percent of this star's flux sits there against 46.3 percent of the Sun's, so a larger share of the shortwave is deposited in the topmost water as heat. A one-layer slab cannot see this. A multi-layer column can, and its penetrative solar heating would be MORE surface-concentrated than Earth tuning assumes, stratifying the top of the column more strongly -- so this belongs in the case for the column rather than being discovered after it. OCN-10 already names net and penetrative solar in its forcing contract. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 40e

title: Define and version one chronological atmosphere/land/ice-to-ocean forcing contract
description:
Define and version one chronological atmosphere/land/ice-to-ocean forcing contract: interval bounds and absolute time; source/destination support; wind stress; net and penetrative shortwave, longwave, sensible and latent heat; precipitation, evaporation, routed river and groundwater discharge; sea-ice freeze/melt and brine/freshwater exchange; salt and required solutes; units, signs, masks and state-versus-flux semantics. Assign every heat, water and salt term one owner, preserve correlated forcing, and retain temperature or salinity restoring only as named numerical controls rather than physical sources

Source: `notes/audits/ocean-and-marine-biosphere.md` section 8a
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
open; schema, synthetic conservation and restart/interval fixtures require no model run and extend EFOR-1's conventions without reusing its land-ecology artifact. Production fields depend on accepted climate, LSHY-2, ANUT-6 and OCN-11; any ocean integration requires explicit permission [step: baseline_run, hydrography]. A REFERENCE INTERFACE EXISTS and it is closer than expected: `vendor/cgenie/genie-plasim` is a complete Planet Simulator sharing TWENTY-FOUR OF ITS TWENTY-FIVE MODULES with `vendor/exoplasim`, the sole exception being `geniemod.f90`, the coupling itself. So a PlaSim-to-GOLDSTEIN exchange already exists against the same `pumamod` state this model carries. It moves net solar, evaporation, precipitation, runoff and two staggered wind-stress pairs to the ocean, and returns sea surface temperature, ice temperature, height, fraction and albedo, alongside area, mask, an atmospheric pressure term and CO2. Read it before specifying from first principles -- and note the term it will not give you: every exchange array is dimensioned 360, an Earth year of daily fields compiled in rather than configured, against this world's 180.7 days. What replaces that is this contract's to state. `notes/external-model-survey.md` sections 10b and 10c. AN ARCHITECTURAL FORK THIS ROW DECIDES BY IMPLICATION AND SHOULD DECIDE EXPLICITLY, 2026-08-22. The published ExoPlaSim-to-cGENIE path does NOT do what this contract specifies. It keeps EMBM running and supplies ExoPlaSim's DYNAMICS to it -- `ea_` parameters appear 13,688 times across shipped configs against 7,314 `go_`, the regrid README sets `ea_11`, and EMBM's namelist reads `xu_wstress`, `yu_wstress`, `xv_wstress`, `yv_wstress`, `u_wspeed` and `v_wspeed` from files, which is exactly what that path converts. EMBM then computes the surface heat fluxes itself, with its transport tunable through `diffamp`, `diffwid`, `difflin`, `betaz` and `betam`. THIS ROW SPECIFIES THE OTHER ARCHITECTURE: a contract carrying net and penetrative shortwave, longwave, sensible and latent heat, i.e. ExoPlaSim computing the fluxes and no EMBM. Both are viable and they cost different things. Keeping EMBM avoids OCN-5's loop but means running a second atmosphere whose transport coefficients are calibrated for Earth, on a planet with 30-hour rotation and 32 degree obliquity -- and re-tuning them so a coupled answer comes out is what failure-modes class 16 forbids. Dropping EMBM keeps ExoPlaSim as the only atmosphere and requires the loop. The second is more consistent with everything else here, but this row should CHOOSE rather than imply. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 28c. A PUBLISHED INSTANCE OF THIS CONTRACT EXISTS AND CAN BE READ OFF, 2026-08-22. cGENIE ships a PlaSim, and `vendor/cgenie/genie-plasim/src/fortran/` is a strict SUBSET of ExoPlaSim's module set plus exactly one file: `geniemod.f90`, 71 lines, pure declaration. THE WHOLE COUPLING SURFACE IS ONE ARRAY-DECLARATION MODULE, which is far smaller than this row assumes. Ocean to atmosphere, 6 used: sst, ice temperature, sea-ice height, sea-ice fraction, SEA-ICE ALBEDO, and CO2. Atmosphere to ocean, 17, each a full seasonal cycle: latent and sensible transfer COEFFICIENTS rather than fluxes, netsolar, solfor, insolar, inlong, sat, spec_hum, pressure, evap, precip, runoff, wind stress as two level pairs, and windspeed. Take this as the starting draft of the contract rather than deriving one. The unit and resolution traps a port hits are in the survey section. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 30

title: Build the ocean spatial-support and bathymetry contract from the accepted 10M Orogen export
description:
Build the ocean spatial-support and bathymetry contract from the accepted 10M Orogen export: conservative wet area and volume; partial coasts; depth/hypsometry; shelves, sills, straits and closed marginal seas; routed river mouths; explicit bathymetric smoothing and connectivity changes; ocean-grid identity; and conservative maps to every T21/T42/T85/T127/T170 atmosphere. Require area/volume/constant closure and resolution/connectivity diagnostics against the native mesh rather than treating a convenient coarse ocean grid as truth

Source: `notes/audits/ocean-and-marine-biosphere.md` section 8b, `biosphere/notes/spatial-support-ecological-aggregation-audit.md`
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
open; extends SPAT-1 through SPAT-5 and SPAT-8/10, and its geometry/remap fixtures require no climate or ocean run. Host-specific grid generation follows OCN-3; any circulation adequacy or timing measurement requires explicit permission [step: orogen, hydrography, boundary_conditions]. AMENDED 2026-08-22: the requirement to declare bathymetric smoothing and connectivity changes explicitly now has an OBSERVED case and not only an argument. BIG-MITgcm removes isolated oceanic points and lakes irrespective of size, and sets every point shallower than 20 m to 20 m, as a numerical-stability step in grid preparation. On a world whose generator produces closed basins in quantity that is not a detail -- and note the pre-carve build's 76 percent endorheic drainage is a LIMIT under rule 9 rather than a state, since the carve loop exists to open basins, so what matters is that the class of feature exists and the step deletes it irrespective of size. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 4. A GENERATOR ROUTE EXISTS AND NEEDS NO GCM. muffingen is at `references/muffingen/`, GPL-3.0, and `EXAMPLE_BLANK.m` sets `par_gcm=''` with every netCDF input name empty, so it will build `.k1`, `.paths` and `.psiles` from a supplied mask and topography alone rather than from another model's output -- which is this row's route from the Orogen bathymetry. `EXAMPLE_K2_supercontinent.m` is the idealised-world precedent beside it. Note the constraint OCN-18 turned up: island count drives a compile-time bound defaulting to 5, so the contract has to REPORT the island count a candidate configuration resolves, not merely produce one. `notes/external-model-survey.md` sections 10d and 10f. MUFFINGEN GENERATES SEVEN THINGS AND THIS PROJECT ALREADY HAS BETTER VERSIONS OF SEVERAL, so this contract must state which are taken and which are overridden -- the defaults are all ON. `EXAMPLE_BLANK.m` enables `opt_makemask`, `opt_maketopo`, `opt_makeocean`, `opt_makerunoff`, `opt_makewind`, `opt_makealbedo` and a sediment option. Runoff routing is `hydrography`'s, with drainage networks, catchments and a lake solver; albedo is `build_surface_albedo.py`'s and PHYS-14's; mask and bathymetry come from Orogen rather than being regridded from another model's output. WHAT ONLY MUFFINGEN KNOWS HOW TO BUILD is the grid topology, `.k1`, `.paths` and `.psiles`, and that is what to take. `opt_makezonalwind` must be OFF: the wind it would generate is a synthetic zonal profile fitted to Earth's circulation, and this world's stress is what ExoPlaSim computes at 30-hour rotation and 32 degree obliquity. `notes/external-model-survey.md` sections 18a and 18b. THE MECHANISM FOR THE FAR SIDE OF DISCHARGE EXISTS AND IS SMALL, 2026-08-22. `references/climber-x/src/geo/coast_cells.f90:115-186` delivers runoff, calving and weathering flux to N ocean cells per coastal cell, about 190 lines, with an ORDERED neighbour list: the cell itself, then 3x3 neighbours SORTED BY FEWEST OCEAN NEIGHBOURS FIRST, then a fixed 28-entry distant stencil reaching four cells in longitude. The embayment-first ordering is the non-obvious part -- freshwater goes preferentially into enclosed water rather than straight to open ocean. `river_discharge()` here stops at the land margin, so this is the liftable shape for the far side. NOTE ALSO `fix_runoff.f90`, which exists purely because the hi-res routing destination and the coarse ocean fraction disagree; that is the mesh-versus-grid disagreement this project has not hit only because discharge stops early. AND A CHOICE THIS PROJECT MADE SILENTLY: the peer's land/ocean fraction threshold is LATITUDE-DEPENDENT, `f_crit + max(0, f_crit_eq-f_crit)*cos(lat)**30`, doubled at the poles, against this project's scalar `geography_land_threshold: 0.5`. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 47e-f

title: Apply the implicit-Earth audit to the selected circulation and ecosystem sources before
description:
Apply the implicit-Earth audit to the selected circulation and ecosystem sources before adoption: inventory every calendar/day/year constant, rate time base, radius/gravity/rotation/reference-pressure value, equation-of-state and salinity range, geothermal/tidal/closure assumption, initial hydrography, latitude/hemisphere branch, Earth nutrient inventory, Redfield or fixed stoichiometry, PAR/photon conversion, sinking speed and supplied trait. Allow latitude only for geometry/Coriolis/diagnostics; replace environmental classifiers with forcing/state/traits; add source lints and fail-closed activation guards where possible

Source: `notes/audits/ocean-and-marine-biosphere.md` section 8c, `biosphere/notes/implicit-earth-assumptions.md`
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
open; source and configuration audit requires no model execution and begins during OCN-3/OCN-4 scoping. It extends BIO-22/BIO-29's contract without making terrestrial tasks own external ocean code. AMENDED 2026-08-22: `ClimaParams.jl` carries a block headed *Planetary and Orbital Parameters (Earth Defaults)* -- radius, gravitational acceleration, rotation rate, orbital semi-major axis, total solar irradiance, obliquity, eccentricity and longitude of perihelion -- which is an externally maintained enumeration of the quantities this audit inventories. Read it before auditing a source by hand. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 5. INVENTORY STARTED 2026-08-22 on the circulation side, and GOLDSTEIN's NON-DIMENSIONALISATION is the first hit. `initialise_goldstein.F:376-391` hardcodes `rsc = 6.37e6` and `gsc = 9.81`, Earth's radius and gravity, exposing neither, while `sodaylen`, `sidaylen`, `yearlen`, `nyear` and `par_dsc` are all in `ini_gold_nml`. Four derived scales carry the hardcoded pair into everything: `tsc = rsc/usc` sets every non-dimensional time, `rhosc = rh0sc*fsc*usc*rsc/gsc/dsc` carries both, `opsisc` scales the overturning streamfunction and `rfluxsc` the heat flux. At 1.20 Earth radii and 1.306 Earth gravity, three of those are wrong by 1.20 and `rhosc` by about eight percent, IN A MODEL THAT IS ENTIRELY NON-DIMENSIONAL -- so a reported overturning would be twenty percent low and would look plausible. AND ROTATION FAILS OPEN: `fsc` is `4*pi/sidaylen` only when solar and sidereal day lengths differ by more than 0.001, otherwise it reverts to Earth's `2*7.2921e-5` for backwards compatibility, so a configuration that sets them equal gets Earth's Coriolis scaling silently. That is the pattern this project's conventions forbid, in the one planetary constant the source does parameterise. Line 642 also records a scale having been wrong before and corrected offline. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 10e. INVENTORY EXTENDED TO THE GEOCHEMISTRY SIDE 2026-08-22, and it splits differently from the circulation side. THE CALENDAR IS COMPILE-TIME AND STATED MORE THAN ONCE: `genie-main/src/fortran/cmngem/gem_cmn.f90:585-587` declares `conv_yr_d = 365.25` as a `PARAMETER` with TWO COMMENTED ALTERNATIVES ON THE SAME LINE, 360.00 and 365.0, then `conv_yr_hr = 24.0 * conv_yr_d` with the 24-HOUR DAY AS A LITERAL, then `conv_yr_s`. Every per-year to per-second conversion in BIOGEM and SEDGEM runs through it and none of it is namelist-reachable, so the year length is a recompile. The 360.00 comment is live: the PlaSim coupling's seasonal arrays are dimensioned 360, so the codebase holds a 365.25-day geochemistry calendar beside a 360-day atmosphere coupling. `conv_yr_s` is 31,557,600 s against this world's 15,794,006, so every rate carried through it is 2.00x out. A SECOND AND INCONSISTENT STATEMENT: `sedgem_box_archer1991_sedflx.f90` hardcodes `3.15e7` TWELVE TIMES as its own seconds-per-year, converting the organic matter decay constant to a per-year rate. That is 0.183 PERCENT SHORTER than the model's own `conv_yr_s`, so a port that fixes `conv_yr_d` leaves sediment diagenesis on an Earth year and nothing fails. `gem_cmn.f90:802` likewise carries `const_rEarth = 6.37E+06` as a `PARAMETER`, a second independent statement of the radius GOLDSTEIN's `rsc` also hardcodes. THE GOOD NEWS, AND IT REDIRECTS THIS AUDIT'S EFFORT: BIOGEM's stoichiometry is NOT hardcoded -- `biogem_lib.f90:179-184` puts all four Redfield ratios in `ini_biogem_nml` and `par_bio_red_PC_flex` switches C:P to flexible entirely, so this row's "Redfield or fixed stoichiometry" item is already exposed and the fixed ratios are a default rather than an assumption. THE PORTING DIFFICULTY IS NOT UNIFORM: biogeochemical parameters are namelist-exposed, physical scaling constants are compile-time `PARAMETER`s, so an audit sampling evenly spends its effort in the wrong place. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 40. RATE TIME BASE SPLITS THREE WAYS and only one is a unit conversion, 2026-08-22 -- and note that a day inside a UNIT is invisible to a search for constants. (1) PHYSICAL/KINETIC, decided: `par_bio_remin_sinkingrate` and three siblings in `m d-1`, plus `par_bio_remin_CH4rate`, `par_scav_Fe_Ks` and `par_bio_remin_opal_K` in `d-1`, are settling speeds and reaction rates where the day is 86400 s and nothing else, so a port to a 30-hour rotation must NOT rescale them. (2) BIOLOGICAL, AMBIGUOUS: `par_bio_tau`, "biological production time-scale (days) (OCMIP-2)", was calibrated where the light cycle is 24 hours while the model resolves no diurnal cycle, so whether it moves with rotation is a modelling decision and should be recorded as an open choice rather than silently converted. (3) NOT TEMPORAL AT ALL: `par_bio_c0_I`, half saturation for light in W m-2 after Doney et al. (2006), is the marine twin of BIO-25's `CQ`; and `par_bio_I_eL` is a SINGLE SCALAR light e-folding depth in metres, which is the sharper case because its error is one-signed -- water is transparent in the blue-green and strongly absorbing in the red and near-infrared, a K dwarf puts more flux where water absorbs more, so THE PHOTIC ZONE IS SHALLOWER than a solar-calibrated e-folding depth implies. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 40d. A THIRD TIME CONVENTION, 2026-08-22, and this one carries a misleading comment. `references/climber-x/src/main/timer.f90:44-55` fixes `nday_year = 360` and `sec_year = 31556926`, the Julian year, then defines `sec_day = sec_year/day_year` with the inline comment "8.765813d4, actual seconds per day". IT IS 87658 s AND IT IS NOT A DAY -- it is a Julian year cut into 360 parts, 1.5 percent long. So every per-day rate in that model is per 1/360 Julian year. Three trees, three conventions, none configurable: cGENIE's compile-time 365.25, its separate hardcoded 3.15e7, and this. The audit should expect the convention to differ BETWEEN modules of one model, not only between models. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 42e. INVENTORY EXTENDED AGAIN 2026-08-22, and the count of independent year statements in cGENIE is SIX, not two. Beyond `conv_yr_d` and the sediment module's `3.15e7`: `genie_control.f90:190` declares `global_daysperyear = 365.25` SEPARATELY, in another module with no cross-reference, and it is what reaches the insolation routine -- so the orbital year and the biogeochemical year travel by different constants and nothing checks they agree; `initialise_genie.F:110` sets a one-hour master timestep beside an Earth solar constant; config files carry `ma_genie_timestep` as a literal second-count with a 360-day alternative commented adjacent; a dead 360-day calendar sits in `genie-lib`; AND `genie-main/runmuffin.sh:229` computes `3600.0*24.0*365.25/...` AS BASH LITERALS and appends the result to the generated config, WHICH MAKES A SHELL SCRIPT THE AUTHORITATIVE STATEMENT OF THE YEAR LENGTH for every standard run. The atmosphere's mole inventory is likewise Earth's by construction and stated three times -- `par_atm_th = 7777.0` m tuned so 1 ppm CO2 equals OCMIP's 2.123 PgC, `conv_atm_mol`, and that same literal repeated inline where the named constant was already in scope. FROM CLIMBER-X, three more of the same class: `ocn/eos.f90:85` computes ocean pressure as `p = 0.1*(-z)` bar, which is Earth gravity times seawater density WITH NO 9.81 AND NO DENSITY ON THE LINE; `constants.f90:79` welds `frac_vu = 0.45` as the sole shortwave band weight with no namelist path and no stated split wavelength, against this project's derived 0.382 at 0.75 um; and `atm_params.f90:240` welds `atm_mass = 5.12e18` kg with reference surface pressure DERIVED from it. Also THREE DIFFERENT CORIOLIS FLOORS in three components of one model -- `5e-5` as a literal in sea ice, `1e-5` in the atmosphere namelist, `5e-6` in the ocean's -- the first binding equatorward of about 20 degrees, so it replaces the Coriolis parameter over a fifth of the globe rather than guarding a small number. `notes/external-model-survey.md` sections 43c and 46b

Preserve carve-dependent source histories, route gases to WET-10/BVOC-6 rather than setting atmospheric abundance, and prohibit bulk terrestrial export or dust mass from becoming instant bioavailable ocean nutrient

Source: `notes/audits/ocean-and-marine-biosphere.md` sections 4 and 8d, `biosphere/notes/abiotic-nutrient-delivery-audit.md` findings 3, 4, 6, 8 and 9

From TASKS.md status column:
open; ledger/speciation and synthetic closure fixtures require no model run. Central boundary fluxes depend on ANUT-3 through ANUT-6, OCN-10/11 and VOLC-8 brackets; internal transformations inform OCN-4/14, trace-gas products feed the shared atmospheric owner, and any executed ocean biogeochemistry requires explicit permission [step: dust, hydrography, groundwater, soil].
