title: The calendar port left climate.mtemp on a hardcoded 31-day window
description:
The calendar port left `climate.mtemp` on a hardcoded 31-day window, and the ported form is two lines below it. `framework/guess.h:956` declares `Historic<double,31> dtemp_31` and `modules/driver.cpp:660` sets `climate.mtemp = climate.dtemp_31.mean()` -- a 31-day mean -- while `:718` reads THE SAME BUFFER the ported way, `dtemp_31.periodicmean(date.ndaymonth[date.month])`. So "month" exists twice in one function, 31 compile-time and 15 runtime. `mtemp` feeds `mtemp_min`/`mtemp_max`, then `mtemp_min20`/`mtemp_max20`, which are the PFT ESTABLISHMENT AND SURVIVAL criteria, and it gates the GDD5 and chilldays reset. THE SIGN IS OPPOSITE TO WHAT THE PORTING AUDIT PREDICTS: that note expects the coldest-month mean to read more extreme because the month is shorter, but the code never uses the month, so a 31-day window over a 183-day orbit DAMPS the seasonal cycle by about 3.55 percent of half-amplitude more than a ported month would -- roughly 1.4 C off the `mtemp_max20 - mtemp_min20` range on a cell with a 40 C annual swing

Source: `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 57
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
open, and a ONE-LINE FIX using a function already called two lines below. Correct `biosphere/notes/lpj-guess-porting-audit.md`'s stated expectation in the same commit [step: lpj_driver] SOURCE CHANGE LANDED 2026-08-22 AND NOT COMPILED, so this row is blocked on a build rather than on effort. `driver.cpp:673` takes the ported form; the row's arithmetic reproduces exactly, trailing-boxcar attenuation 31/183 giving 0.9535 against 15/183 giving 0.9890, a difference of 3.552 percent of half-amplitude and 1.42 C on a 40 C swing. ONE THING THIS ROW DID NOT CARRY: once ported there is NO residual against the Earth-calibrated limits, because a month is one twelfth of the orbit in both calendars, 30.4/365.2569 giving 0.9886 against 15/183 giving 0.9890; only the twelfth month differs, at 0.9842 and about 0.2 C. A fail-closed guard was added at `:566-579` because `Historic::periodicmean` silently returns the whole-buffer mean when `nsteps` exceeds `size()`, so a future orbit whose months outgrow `CAPACITY` would reintroduce this defect invisibly. The audit's stated expectation was wrong in BOTH halves and is rewritten: the code never used the month, and the sign is the other way. CORRECTION 2026-08-22: this is NOT clearable by a recompile. LPJ-GUESS does not build on this tree at all -- `framework/vesper.h` is a GENERATED header, and `pipeline.py --plan vesper_header` runs the chain to it through `baseline_run` and `baseline_climatology`, neither of which exists. So this row sits behind the same baseline run as CLIM-71, not behind a compile, and nothing here is verified by execution. Do not fit the header against the bootstrap climatology to make a build succeed; BIO-19 owns that ambiguity and choosing a climatology to serve a compile is not a way to settle it.

title: leaflong is read as Vesper orbits in one file and as Earth months in another
description:
`leaflong` is read as Vesper orbits in one file and as Earth months in another, in the same binary. `modules/growth.cpp:1424` uses `pft.leaflong * date.year_length()`, correctly treating it as simulation years. `framework/guess.h:2145` computes Reich et al. (1992) specific leaf area as `sla = 0.2*pow(10, 2.41 - 0.38*log10(12.0*leaflong))`, where the `12.0` converts EARTH YEARS TO EARTH MONTHS. The same `12.0*leaflong` appears at `:2161` for `cton_leaf_min`, and `ctop_leaf_min` derives from that `sla` at `:2175-2178`. WITH `ifcalcsla 1` AND `ifcalccton 1` IN THE LIVE INSTRUCTION FILE THESE OVERWRITE the declared per-PFT values, and `build_vesper_pfts.py` deliberately does not rescale `leaflong`. At `leaflong 0.5`, which is every summergreen and grass PFT, SLA comes out about 23 to 24 percent low and `cton_leaf_min` about 26 percent high. SLA sets leaf area per kgC, so it propagates into LAI, FPAR, APAR and GPP; the C:N and C:P minima set the whole nutrient limitation cascade

Source: `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 57
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:

DECIDE THE UNIT QUESTION FIRST, because it is the same per-orbit versus per-unit-time ambiguity FATES raises: `leaflong` in the parameter file is a leaf lifetime, and whether Reich's regression should be fed absolute months or orbit-months is a modelling decision, not a conversion. Partly overlaps `implicit-earth-assumptions.md` finding 2 and `plant-physiology-carbon-allocation-audit.md` finding 5, but the unit MISMATCH is recorded in neither [step: vesper_pfts, lpj_driver]

title: Repair the phosphorus cycle's copied parameters
description:
Repair the phosphorus cycle's copied parameters, three of which make P a duplicate of N rather than an independent element. `framework/guess.h:2278-2320` `init_pupscoeff()` is a VERBATIM copy of `init_nupscoeff()` including the comment, which still reads "nitrogen uptake" and "Soil nitrogen profile", so the rooting-depth uptake weighting is identical and P competition among PFTs cannot inform anything the N ranking does not. `:2230-2274` gives the P stoichiometry scalings N's values with N's citations, and line 2232 admits it in a comment ending "SAME FOR P, MAKES SENSE?". `modules/somdynam.cpp:71,75` sets `USORB` and `USSORB` to the same rate, which THIS ROW WRONGLY CALLED A COPY: Wang et al. (2010) Appendix D sets both constants to 0.0067 per year in the source itself. The real defect at those lines is that `UOCC` is declared and never used and `Soil::pmass_occluded` is never assigned, so there is no terminal sink for the strongly sorbed pool to drain into -- BIO-35 owns that. AND `:65-67` sets `PCONC_SAT = 0.02`, the NITROGEN value, with `//static const double PCONC_SAT = 0.004;` commented out directly above it

title: The CNP fork has no terminal phosphorus occlusion at all
description:
The CNP fork has no terminal phosphorus occlusion at all, so the P cycle has no ultimate sink. `UOCC` is declared and never used anywhere; `Soil::pmass_occluded` is initialised to zero, serialised, and never assigned; and `guess.cpp:616` has the occluded pool commented out of the P conservation sum, which is harmless only because the pool is always zero. Decide whether Vesper's phosphorus cycle closes with an occlusion loss or declares its absence, and note that Wang et al. (2010) deliberately omits the flux, saying it would add computation with little impact at decade to century scales

Source: BIO-33, `references/wang2010-cnp-terrestrial-biosphere.pdf` section 2.3, `vendor/lpj-guess/framework/guess.cpp:616`
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
open, and ASK WHETHER IT SHOULD EXIST BEFORE BUILDING IT: the omission is the cited source's own choice and is defensible at the timescales a run covers, so the deliverable may be a declared gap rather than a flux. What is NOT defensible is the current state, where a dead constant and a commented-out conservation term make an absent process look like a slow one. Either way `UOCC` goes or gets used [step: lpj_run]

title: Record in docs/src/pipeline/loops.md that the biosphere reaches the climate through albedo
description:
Record in `docs/src/pipeline/loops.md` that the biosphere reaches the climate through albedo, roughness and forest fraction only, and not through transpiration

Source: `notes/audits/missed-couplings.md`
notes:
From archive/tasks.md closing note:
done 2026-08-17, and VERIFIED in the vendored ExoPlaSim 3.4.2 source rather than asserted. Land evaporation is `mkevap`, and its whole dependence on the land surface is `zkdiff = drhs * zkonst1 * dtransh / dt` at `fluxmod.f90:658`: `dtransh` carries roughness, so that channel is real, and `drhs` at `NVEG = 0` is one bucket, `min(1, dwatc/(0.4*dwmax))`, with the five `dsoilz` layers holding temperature rather than water. No root, canopy, interception or stomatal term exists in `landmod.f90`, `fluxmod.f90` or `surfmod.f90`. Two refinements to the claim as written. Forest fraction is NARROWER than it sounded: at `NVEG = 0` it only mixes the snow albedo's forested and unforested endpoints, so it is radiative and reaches evaporation not at all. And there is a FOURTH channel one step removed, `dwmax` from pedology carrying LPJ-GUESS soil carbon, already bounded near-inert at 1.06x on runoff for a 3.75-fold bucket change, so the word "only" needed it. The finding worth more than the task: switching SIMBA on would NOT supply the missing physics. It does couple back at `nveg == 2`, but `dsc`, its "stomatal conductance", is prescribed -- allocated to `rinidsc` at `simba.f90:157`, optionally read as surface code 1606, and never assigned again -- and `dlai` is computed and used nowhere but output. So the absence is a property of the model, not of this project's configuration
close_reason: done 2026-08-17, and VERIFIED in the vendored ExoPlaSim 3.4.2 source rather than asserted.

Recomputed rather than carried, as a secant between run_bfa3f5269660 (0.91) and run_524fbed77a9a (0.945), the only converged pair sharing a surface digest, over the last ten orbits of each under the same land mean `land_water_balance` uses: +2.19 %/K land P and +2.42 %/K land E, agreeing with the carried figures to two significant figures but now with a stated window. The trap is defused IN THE ARITHMETIC rather than in a comment: applying the 6.51x amplification to a kelvin gives +14.3 %/K against a true +0.92, because a kelvin raises land evaporation slightly faster than precipitation and the two amplified terms nearly annihilate. The amplification is right for a water-cycle perturbation that leaves temperature alone and wrong for everything priced in kelvin, and the file prints both with the reason. The lake limb is BRACKETED rather than plugged, low end the land rate and high end PHYS-5's 6.7 %/K saturation-vapour-pressure convexity, since Penman's radiative term does not grow with the deficit; it reaches the basin column only, because runoff is P - E_land, so runoff is a number and basins are a range. title: Make the flux-to-kelvin conversion canonical
description:
Make the flux-to-kelvin conversion canonical

Source: `scripts/error_budget.py`, `notes/dust.md`, `docs/src/pipeline/state.md` section 5b
notes:
From archive/tasks.md closing note:
done 2026-08-17. `lib/sensitivity.py` owns it and `check_consistency.py` recomputes it from the run index every audit, so it cannot go stale silently again. THE SLOPE IS 202 K per unit flux ratio, 34% above the 150.2 it replaces, corroborated at 201.3 to 203.4 by four further estimates across two terrains. The 150.2 was T21 across 0.95-1.00, a bracket that stopped containing the baseline when the flux moved to 0.945, breaking the rule its own comment stated; and nothing ever fell back to it, `main()` assigned it unconditionally. THE DENOMINATOR WAS THE SECOND ERROR AND COMPOUNDED THE FIRST: a top-of-atmosphere forcing is an absorbed-flux change, so the divisor is `S/4 * (1 - alpha)` = 242.8 W/m2 rather than the incident 321.54, giving 0.832 K per W/m2 against 0.467 in use. Planetary albedo was stale at 0.266 and is now measured from the baseline's own `rst`/`rsut` at 0.28644 rather than declared. Two things worth keeping. The claimed 3.4x gap between the local slope and the stellar sweep's sensitivity was 1.9x once the local conversion was right, so most of it was arithmetic rather than the ice transition -- though the sweep is still the wrong sensitivity to use at the baseline. And the ORDERING moved: nothing reorders inside the albedo column, where a slope is a uniform multiplier, but the W/m2 items that previously sat under "no conversion invented" now have kelvin, and shortwave-only in-model dust lands SECOND in the whole budget at 3.3 to 3.6 K. The trap avoided: pairing the baseline climatology with the 0.910 run crosses a geography change and yields 224, a +0.80 K surface revision wearing a slope's units, so the bracket is taken within one geography and `verify()` enforces it

title: The error budget's basin reconstruction no longer reproduces the verdict
description:
The error budget's basin reconstruction no longer reproduces the verdict: `analysis/error_budget.json` reports "MISMATCH: 2026 against 2032"

Source: `analysis/error_budget.json`, `notes/audits/carve-criterion-terms.md`
notes:
From archive/tasks.md closing note:
done 2026-08-18, fixed on the GENERATOR side, which is the durable half. `export_carve_list.py` records precipitation, lake evaporation and land evaporation per basin in km/year, and the budget re-evaluates the criterion from them instead of inverting the recorded aridity index. An inversion is tied to whatever algebra the verdict used on the day it ran, which is exactly why it broke the first time the criterion moved. Three checks replace the one that broke, all identities of the artifact rather than comparisons between two formulations: recorded runoff == max(P - E_land, 0), the criterion re-evaluated at zero perturbation reproduces the recorded overflow, and a 0.1% error injected into any recorded term trips the discharge bound by six orders of magnitude. TWO THINGS THE INVERSION HAD BEEN HIDING, and both outrank the six-basin mismatch that prompted the task: it was still applying a Penman land-rate floor the verdict had already dropped, which was most of what the land-evaporation row measured (+1% land E read -110 basins and now reads -7), and the 1,077 basins with no catchment runoff could not be reconstructed at all because the clamp at zero destroys P - E, so they were silently absent and are now all evaluated [step: error_budget]

Regenerating the report to get the key exposed a genuine staleness and rule 7 decided it: `surface_water.nc` was two hours newer than the albedo built from it, so the surface fields were worthless rather than stale and were rebuilt on the current lake solution -- 124743 lake regions to 125429, land-mean written 0.156436 to 0.156355. title: Define a reduced Vesper oxidant/trace-gas bracket before any central SOA yield
description:
Define a reduced Vesper oxidant/trace-gas bracket before any central SOA yield: drive OH/O3/NO3 chemistry from the K-star UV, water vapour, temperature and adopted soil/fire NOx, return precursor loss plus O3, OH/oxidizing-capacity, CO and methane-lifetime changes, and expose the inconsistency between biosphere-derived BVOC and the current fixed-Earth-flux ozone/CH4 state rather than silently combining them

Source: `biosphere/notes/bvoc-soa-atmospheric-coupling-audit.md` finding 6
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
open; start with a documented box/reduced-chemistry interface and fixed-yield screening bounds; a closed photochemical state may require machinery outside ExoPlaSim and any model experiment requires explicit permission [step: baseline_climatology, lpj_run]. A REUSABLE SHAPE FOR THE OXIDANT BRACKET, AND ITS LIMIT, 2026-08-22. CLIMBER-X has NO atmospheric chemistry, but `src/ch4/ch4_model.f90:179-183` carries a reduced form this row can take the STRUCTURE of: reciprocal lifetimes added over four sinks -- OH, tropospheric chlorine, soil and stratosphere -- with OH represented by a fitted log-linear surrogate in the methane burden plus NOx, CO and VOC emissions and a linear temperature term. IT IS A SURROGATE FOR OH, NOT OH, and its anchors are two independent Earth baselines, 1056 ppb and 286.83 K. Take the reciprocal-addition shape and the sink decomposition; re-fit or bracket every coefficient. NOTE WHAT IT DOES NOT SUPPLY: the VOC term is a prescribed anthropogenic emission series read from file, so this gives a consumption interface and no producer, and ozone there is a prescribed radiative boundary condition that is never an oxidant. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 42a. A SECOND REUSABLE FORM, BETTER CONDITIONED, AND ONE FAMILY TO REFUSE, 2026-08-22. cGENIE's `genie-atchem` has six CH4 sink schemes and NONE is photolysis -- one well-mixed box, no OH, the source saying "omitting [OH], [NOx] etc etc". TAKE THE POWER LAWS IN PARTIAL PRESSURE: `tau = tau0*(pCH4/C0)**N`, with `schmidt03` the better-conditioned variant, namelist-settable and calibrated over 1x to 200x C0 against the default's 8x. REFUSE THE POLYNOMIAL EMULATORS: `claire06` and `goldblatt06` fit photochemical output as polynomials in log10 of ABSOLUTE MOLE INVENTORIES in Tmol, not mixing ratios, which anchors them to Earth's atmospheric mass -- 1.088x here per section 42b -- and the source itself warns "neither O2 nor CH4 are truncated at edge of training values here, so USE CAUTION". A TRAP EVEN IF ADOPTING THE DEFAULT: `par_atm_CH4_photochem` defaults to a scheme that reads only compile-time constants, so the three namelist `par_pCH4_oxidation_*` values are SILENTLY IGNORED unless the scheme string is also changed, while the run log prints them as though in force. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 46a. AND A THIRD MODEL, THIS ONE WITH ACTUAL CHEMISTRY, 2026-08-22. Where cGENIE and CLIMBER-X offer parametric lifetimes to take the SHAPE of, CAABA/MECCA offers 2,323 gas-phase reactions of which 414 are photolysis, with OH, O1D and the quenching competition explicit. That makes it the instrument for deriving this row's oxidant bracket rather than another source to fit one from. Its photolysis door and the gravity correction it needs are in `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 48

title: Name the residuals the flux diagnostics carry
description:
Name the residuals the flux diagnostics carry: the top-of-atmosphere one against state storage, and the surface one that CLIM-7 left untested

Source: `exoplasim/notes/water-and-energy-closure.md`, `exoplasim/scripts/close_term_energy.py`
notes:
From archive/tasks.md closing note:
done 2026-08-18 on the TOA half, which is what the task asked to NAME; the surface half is narrowed and continues as CLIM-11. `rsut` and `rlut` WERE NEVER POSSIBLE, and that is a structural result rather than a measurement: `outmod.f90` accumulates the same `dswfl`/`dlwfl` arrays that `radmod` forms `dflux` from, which `landmod` drives the surface with and whose divergence is the atmospheric heating, so the reported TOA net IS the number that heats the model and there is no reported-against-actual split for either flux to hide in. A wrong but self-consistent radiation scheme gives a different climate IN BALANCE, not a persistent imbalance. THE SOURCE IS THE ADIABATIC SPECTRAL STEP, creating +0.345 +/- 0.013 W/m2 where enthalpy and kinetic energy must cancel, 15.6% of the conversion it performs, stable across four window choices. Three identities each with a right answer of zero, and the third is what makes the second mean anything: had the kinetic-energy budget not closed at -0.007, `denergy27` would not be the adiabatic generation. With the term counted the atmospheric budget closes to -0.104 +/- 0.107 against the model's own column enthalpy trend of -0.007, from -0.853 on the flux route alone; -0.20 W/m2 of the planetary residual remains unattributed. The four-run flux leverage is EXHAUSTED and was reported as such rather than read: every fixed-fraction hypothesis predicts a shift below the 0.035 W/m2 run-to-run scatter. No criterion was retrofitted, deliberately: the quantity is resolution- and timestep-dependent by nature, so it stays recorded raw and `close_term_energy.py` must be re-run on the first low-I/O-off block of any T85 run before a T42 number is carried into loop D [step: assess_convergence]
close_reason: done 2026-08-18 on the TOA half, which is what the task asked to NAME; the surface half is narrowed and continues as CLIM-11.

title: exoplasim/scripts/run_albedo_bracket.sh calls continue_exoplasim.py without --run
description:
`exoplasim/scripts/run_albedo_bracket.sh` calls `continue_exoplasim.py` without `--run`, required since run ids became UUIDs, so the script cannot run as written

Source: `exoplasim/scripts/run_albedo_bracket.sh`, `exoplasim/runs/INDEX.json`
notes:
From archive/tasks.md closing note:
done 2026-08-18. The id is THREADED, not discovered, and `run_exoplasim.py` needed no change: it already announces `RUN_ID=<id>` on its own line with `flush=True` before any prepare guard, for exactly this, and nothing used it. Each case captures its OWN output rather than the shared log, extracts that line, and hands it to `--run`. Searching `INDEX.json` for a matching configuration was rejected as rule 6 with extra steps: the four cases are separable there, since `geography_tag` digests the albedo `.sra` and not only mask and topography, but a SECOND bracket at the same flux on the same surface has an identical fingerprint, and breaking that tie on `executable_sha256` is the encoded set growing by whatever someone last thought of. title: The -0.29 W/m2 slab residual is NOT the model
description:
The -0.29 W/m2 slab residual is NOT the model

Source: `exoplasim/notes/water-and-energy-closure.md`, `exoplasim/scripts/close_ocean_energy.py`
notes:
From archive/tasks.md closing note:
done 2026-08-19, and the row's own title turns out to be right for a reason nobody had reached: the residual was MEASUREMENT, all of it, in four layers each hiding the next. Three were the instrument. `align` floored `nrec // nbin` when the year is not a whole number of write intervals, worth 13.102 to 0.353. It then used EQUAL-WIDTH bins where pyburn's hold different record counts, 0.353 to 0.191. And the identities took the atmosphere side with `.mean(0)` while the stream side was a record mean, which is CLIM-13 committed two hundred lines below the block that diagnoses it -- D1 0.2016 to 0.0534. The fourth was the DATA. The model writes one record per 24.00 h and this planet's day is 30.00 h, exactly 40 timesteps against 32, so the regular output samples the diurnal cycle at FIVE PHASES forever while the ocean and ice streams accumulate every step and are a true integral. Predicted before the run: raise the sampling and the bias collapses. At NWPD = 8, ten phases and 1462 raw records an orbit against 182, D1 goes +0.0534 to +0.0079 -- a factor of 6.8 against the 2.8 that random noise would give, which is aliasing rather than variance. So the atmosphere and the streams agree to 0.008 W/m2 and the model's surface energy budget closes. D2 through D5 were at machine zero throughout. Found on the way and guarded: the streams follow their own counters and ignore NWPD, so the two sides only share a clock at NWPD = 1 and the closure now refuses any other case rather than tiling bins it does not share a clock with [step: bootstrap_convergence, baseline_convergence]
close_reason: done 2026-08-19, and the row's own title turns out to be right for a reason nobody had reached: the residual was MEASUREMENT, all of it, in four layers each hiding the next.

title: ExoPlaSim DEADLOCKS at NLOWIO = 0 on more than one rank once
description:
ExoPlaSim DEADLOCKS at `NLOWIO = 0` on more than one rank once `exoplasim-3.4.2-lowio-first-record.patch` is resident. `nlowio` is read from `plasim_nl` on NROOT and never broadcast, so the other ranks keep the compiled default of 1; the patch puts `nlowio` into a PER-TIMESTEP condition in `gridpointd` that guards `call mpsum(sqout,NLEV)`, so the non-root ranks take it every step and NROOT every `nafter`, and the ranks desynchronise on step one

Source: `notes/audits/nlowio-collective-deadlock.md`
notes:
From archive/tasks.md closing note:
done 2026-08-18. Fixed by `exoplasim-3.4.2-nlowio-broadcast.patch`, which broadcasts `nlowio` and `nstpw` in `prolog` beside the `mpbci(nafter)` already there; the low-I/O patch is resident again on top of it and all binaries plus the cycle executable are rebuilt. A full T42 p16 orbit at `NLOWIO = 0` goes from never finishing to 89.7 s, which REPRODUCES the 90 s that `run_manifest.json` recorded for the 2026-08-17 segment -- the check that the fix restores behaviour rather than merely stopping a hang. NEITHER HALF BITES ALONE, which is why it hid: `NLOWIO = 0` was first set at 15:21 and the patch became resident at 22:50 on 2026-08-17, the 23:56 climatology ran `NLOWIO = 0` fine on a binary built before the patch, and the first run carrying both was on 08-18. The low-I/O patch's real cost is 84.0 s against 78.0 s at `NLOWIO = 1`, about 8%, from the per-timestep humidity transform it deliberately adds. The test that separates all of it is to run the OLD binary under the NEW conditions and takes 78 seconds [step: rebuild_binaries, baseline_run]

title: Ocean horizontal heat diffusion has a namelist switch, nhdiff with hdiffk
description:
Ocean horizontal heat diffusion has a namelist switch, `nhdiff` with `hdiffk`, and the error budget records no-q-flux as STRUCTURAL with "no cheap version exists"

Source: `notes/audits/absent-and-inherited-physics.md` finding 1, `analysis/error_budget.json` other_items
notes:
From archive/tasks.md closing note:
done 2026-08-20. The declared 300/1000/3000 bracket ran against a length-matched control, one restart, one binary, fifteen diagnostic orbits each. CONSERVATION HOLDS, which was the prediction's primary claim: every arm's global net TOA difference is consistent with zero and inside the declared 0.3 W/m2, so the term redistributes and cannot be argued for or against on a global-mean flux. The poleward redistribution is confirmed at all three points, 0-20 losing and 40-60 gaining, each 15 of 15 orbits one-signed. The ice-edge term is measured through AREA rather than flux, which is where the signal-to-noise is: at 3000 the arm loses 0.00124 of the planet in sea ice and CLIM-17's conversion puts that at +0.079 to +0.127 K, while at the default the ice change is nothing and the predicted +0.03 to +0.12 K is not resolved and not claimed. THE SPREAD, which is what this row asked for: 40-60 ocean warming +0.13 to +0.19 K at the default and +0.36 to +0.57 K at 3000, each end a separate REALISATION of the same key, and sea ice 0 to -0.00124 of the planet. The realisation-to-realisation span is 35 to 37%, so a single realisation's error bar understates the uncertainty on one of these means by about a third. The method note worth keeping is that the differences must be read PAIRED per orbit -- combining each run's spread in quadrature double-counts the variability both inherit from one restart and inflates the error bars sixfold, which left only the top point resolved. The declared linearity falsifier appeared to fire and DID NOT: CLIM-19's replicate from a different restart put the 300 point below 1000 instead of above it, so the excess was an ice-state draw and linearity holds, 3000 over 1000 coming out 2.99 and 2.89 against a diffusivity ratio of 3.00 [step: baseline_run]

title: Ocean salinity is declared nowhere and Earth's arrives silently through TFREEZE = 271.25
description:
Ocean salinity is declared nowhere and Earth's arrives silently through `TFREEZE = 271.25`

notes:
From archive/tasks.md closing note:
done 2026-08-18. `config/planet.yaml` has an `ocean:` block carrying `salinity_psu: 34.7`, marked DECLARED rather than DETERMINED because a real salinity is the steady state of riverine delivery against hydrothermal uptake, evaporite burial and reverse weathering over an ocean age this project does not have. The value has not moved and that is the point: it is now VISIBLE and settable where it was compiled in. `run_exoplasim.py:freezing_point_k` derives TFREEZE from it with the UNESCO polynomial and passes it as `TFREEZE@icemod_namelist`, which needed no source change -- TFREEZE is already an `icemod_nl` key, broadcast and passed down to oceanmod. The polynomial is CHECKED against the constant it replaces rather than trusted, and that guard earned itself immediately: written at a 0.005 K tolerance it failed, because the polynomial gives 271.2449 and 271.25 is that rounded, so the tolerance is now the two decimals the model states. Direction carried in the error budget with its bracket: most land here is endorheic, so the exorheic share per unit ocean area is under half Earth's, a fresher ocean freezes WARMER, and the 20-to-34.7 psu span is about 1.1 K on the freezing point. What it is worth in global mean is unmeasured and now needs only an A/B on a settable key. Adding the block moved the config hash, so the two biosphere generators were re-run; no physical value in `vesper.h` changed and no LPJ-GUESS rebuild is implied

title: The first output bin of every orbit has corrupted WIND and HUMIDITY only
description:
The first output bin of every orbit has corrupted WIND and HUMIDITY only, worsening downward from 1.02 at the model top

Source: `docs/src/practice/failure-modes.md` class 14
notes:
From archive/tasks.md closing note:
done 2026-08-17, mechanism PINNED to six figures and now class 18. Three defects in the `NLOWIO = 1` path, and the counter was NOT the cause. `plasim.f90:857` and `:1086` save six SPECTRAL accumulators through `mpputgp`/`mpgetgp`, whose dummy is declared `pp(NHOR,klev)`; Fortran reinterprets the `(NESP,NLEV)` array and moves 5,120 of 19,040 elements at T42/L10/p16, so levels 4-10 are restored as ZERO while `naccuout` survives intact at 90 and the first write of each call divides 159 samples by 249. `outmod.f90:394` then subtracts the whole `plavor` from an accumulator holding only 0.638554 of it, leaving `-(1-delta)*plavor` in the (n=1,m=0) vorticity mode -- solid-body rotation, a retrograde 160.8*cos(phi) m/s on levels 4-10. That is the entire wind signature, and it explains every part of it: `ua` only because plavor lives in vorticity, worsening downward because the spurious wind is level-independent while the real one falls, and temperature escaping because `aast` holds the deviation from `t0`. Humidity is separate: `sqout` is recomputed only at output steps but summed every step and is not in the restart, and since 5850 mod 160 = 90 its phase walks with a 16-orbit period, measured at 0.946 correlation over 90 orbits. PREDICTIONS STATED BEFORE MEASURING, which is what makes this a mechanism rather than a story: the surviving coefficients must show no anomaly and the truncated ones must all show the same one, giving delta = 159/249 to six figures with a relative residual of 3e-7; a 6018-step run must give a DIFFERENT constant, predicted -0.127108 and measured -0.127108; orbit 0 of every run must be clean, and it is; and the wind anomaly must be a level-independent `cos(phi)` solid body of -53.59 m/s with nothing fitted, measured -53.44 to -53.56 on levels 3-9. The trap named in the task, `naccuout` persisting while the accumulators do not, was ELIMINATED with evidence: it is restored correctly, and the gridpoint accumulators share the same counter and are clean

title: pyburn's reader was QUADRATIC in record count
description:
pyburn's reader was QUADRATIC in record count: `readallvariables` grew every variable with `variables[kcode] = np.append(variables[kcode],field)` once per record, and np.append reallocates and copies the whole accumulated array each call

Source: `notes/audits/pyburn-postprocessing-cost.md`
notes:
From archive/tasks.md closing note:
done 2026-08-18. Records are collected per code and joined once with np.concatenate; `readvariablecode` had the same pattern and is fixed with it. One T42 orbit at `NLOWIO = 0`, 2.4 GB raw, driven with the exact kwargs `Model.run()` forwards and unprofiled both ways: 304.0 s to 29.4 s, 10.3x, np.append calls 3,062,749 to 1, and all 123 output variables BITWISE IDENTICAL. It reproduces the pipeline's own history -- `continue_exoplasim.py` records 387 s an orbit and this bench gives 81 s model + 304 s pyburn = 385 s; the same orbit is now 110 s. The triple loops over (time, lat, lon) in the omega/wa/streamfunction branches were vectorised in the same patch and are the smaller half. THE DIAGNOSIS WAS WRONG TWICE AND THAT IS THE DURABLE PART: cProfile charged 246 s to 6.0e6 tiny np.append calls in the loops, which is what a profiler costs for six million call events rather than what numpy spends, and the same 246 s actually belonged to the ~81k LARGE appends in the reader -- one function, two callers, call counts three orders of magnitude apart and opposite per-call costs. The ratio was the tell, not the tottime column. Separately, a claim that `example.nl`'s 216 duplicated codes were being processed was an artefact of the measuring harness: pyburn ignores `variables` when a `namelist` is passed, and the pipeline passes none. Consequences: the `NLOWIO = 0` penalty in `continue_exoplasim.py` is much smaller, and the 1.09x for two concurrent 8-rank runs was a workaround for this defect -- run at 16 ranks [step: rebuild_binaries, climatology]

title: build_climatology.py computes land_p_minus_e_minus_mrro_mm_per_orbit
description:
`build_climatology.py` computes `land_p_minus_e_minus_mrro_mm_per_orbit` with `EARTH_CALENDAR_YEAR_DAYS`, whose own docstring in `lib/orbit.py` says to use it for annualising to per Earth year

notes:
From archive/tasks.md closing note:

Verified on the baseline window: the value halves by exactly 1.9980, the Earth-calendar over orbital-year ratio, so nothing else moved. title: Price the interior moisture source: the water a catchment delivers to a closed basin
description:
Price the interior moisture source: the water a catchment delivers to a closed basin evaporates over land in the world `hydrography/` describes and is exported to the ocean in the model, which has no lake, so the moisture source moves off the continent. It is 5.6 to 6.6% of land precipitation, sited in the arid interiors, on a planet whose land is 76.2% endorheic

Source: `notes/audits/unpriced-terms.md` finding 1, `exoplasim/notes/lake-representation.md`
notes:
From archive/tasks.md closing note:
done 2026-08-19, and the measurement DEFLATED it and flipped its sign. `carve_verdict.py` now computes the area-weighted integral every run into `runoff_source.endorheic_inflow`, with an identity that closes to 0.00% -- inflow equals lake net evaporation plus the runoff generated over the lake bed plus what spills to the ocean, those being the only doors out of the endorheic system. Endorheic catchments deliver 69% of land runoff off 76% of the land, credible where the 97% that prompted this was not, and the cause was multiplying an UNWEIGHTED per-basin mean by the total catchment area rather than the clamp, which is worth 4.2%. The substantive correction is that gross lake evaporation is the wrong quantity: what the atmosphere gains from a lake is its evaporation against what the model already evaporates on that ground, and this world's land is several times rougher than open water, so the model's own evaporation exceeds Penman on 2,484 of 4,105 land cells. The term is -2,374 km3/Earth-yr, -0.9% of land precipitation, and NEGATIVE, so the intuitive direction was wrong as well as the size. The estimator uses catchment means rather than lake-footprint values and is biased against the lake; it would have to be wrong by a factor of six to reach what was first claimed. Not a dust-scale item

title: Give each rank the number of latitudes its die's cache can hold
description:
Give each rank the number of latitudes its die's cache can hold, instead of the same number to all of them. A 16-rank run spans both CCDs and hands every rank an equal `NLPP`, while CCD0 has 96 MB of L3 and CCD1 has 32 MB

The imbalance is real and was confirmed per rank rather than inferred: ranks 0-7 on CCD0 wait 23.1% of samples at T127 and 30.6% at T170, ranks 8-15 on CCD1 wait 12.4% and 20.1%, a 10.5 point step at the die boundary against 3.5 points of variation inside a die, with CCD1 the critical path at both. The default binding was checked rather than assumed. **What refuses the task is the size of the prize once the pairing constraint is applied.** Perfect balance recovers `mean - min` = 5.74% of wall at T127 and 5.65% at T170, and that ceiling binds every balancing scheme equally. Making `NLPP` a per-rank variable turns every `(NHOR,...)` array into a maximum rather than an exact size and every loop bound over it into a runtime value, across the whole physics, and that cannot be worth 1.8% at one resolution and nothing at another. The same ceiling refuses OpenMP threading on its balance argument, which was the other reason to want it. **What replaces this is CLIM-48**, which removes the cause instead of balancing around it: the working set is eight Legendre weight matrices that are all P or Q times separable factors, and storing two fits CCD1's L3 at both resolutions

title: Settle on the record what the production build initialises reals to. The flag line carries
description:
Settle on the record what the production build initialises reals to. The flag line carries `-ffpe-trap=invalid,zero,overflow` and `-finit-real=zero` together, and the second makes the first unable to fire on the case it is least able to survive: zero is a valid operand, so an uninitialised read succeeds and is indistinguishable from a deliberate zero. `aocl-and-model-build-flags.md` keeps the trap on the argument that a NaN raises SIGFPE at the line that made it rather than reaching every spectral coefficient through the Legendre transform, and that argument does not reach an uninitialised read at all. The pairing is not a decision anyone recorded, and `-finit-real=zero` is meanwhile load-bearing for determinism in a way nothing states, so deleting it is not the move: dropping it leaves garbage rather than detection

Source: `notes/audits/uninitialised-reads-and-implicit-save.md` finding 1
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
blocked, and PARKED until the optimisation worktree merges rather than blocked on effort. THE PREMISE THIS ROW WAS DECIDED ON IS CONTRADICTED: it was closed 2026-08-22 on the argument that zero fill is free, since gfortran folds a signalling NaN to a quiet one at -O1 and above so the alternative arms no trap, making the swap a loss on both sides rather than a trade. That argument holds only if the fill itself costs nothing, and the optimisation worktree reports `-finit-real=zero` costing on the order of 30 percent of runtime. If that survives review it is a real trade and the decision has to be retaken on it, so the comment written into `most_compiler_omp` has been REMOVED rather than left standing on a premise now in doubt. THE FILE IS ALSO THE WRONG PLACE NOW: that worktree reworked the build process, so where the flag line lives is itself unsettled. Retake this against the merged build, with the cost measured rather than reported, and do not re-derive it before then [step: rebuild_binaries]
close_reason:
Answered, and by exactly the procedure this row asked for: retaken against the merged build with the cost measured rather than reported. exoplasim/notes/the-zeroing-is-an-init-flag.md carries it.

WHAT THE FLAG WAS WORTH: two T170 threaded binaries from the same source differing in that flag alone, paired and interleaved on the 300-step bed -- 70.55 s with -finit-real=zero against 51.97 s without, +26.03% [+22.76, +27.29], faster in 4 of 4 rounds, and the restart IDENTICAL. Visible statically too: 1193 memset call sites with the flag, 623 without. The cause of the 31% of T170 that shtns-viability.md had attributed to physics routines clearing their own work arrays was the compiler doing it, not the model.

WHETHER THE MODEL NEEDS IT: three gates, and it does not. The trapping gate (-finit-real=snan with -ffpe-trap=invalid) is clean on the legmod path at T21 and T170, at NLOWIO=0 and 1. The propagating gate, which answers what the trapping one cannot on the SHTns path, gives one restart hash across -finit-real=zero, -finit-real=snan with INVALID masked, and no init flag: bit identical, so nothing uninitialised reaches a stored value.

ADOPTED: config/planet.yaml no longer declares -finit-real=zero and the checked profile carries -finit-real=snan. The threaded build compiles byte for byte to c8b9c41046fd93ca, which IS the arm the 26.03% was measured on. Determinism, the one thing this could have cost, survives: verify_shtns_model.sh passes whole on the new build, both arms at rounding scale, the control rejected, four-run bit-identity giving one hash, fcf46ebbb1302d3a.

The row's premise text is also now false -- the flag line no longer carries -finit-real=zero at all.

title: PARKED, and the row exists so the arithmetic is not redone. Running the model's spectral

The blocker is that a consumer RTX 4090 throttles FP64 to a sixty-fourth of its FP32 rate, giving 1.29 TFLOP/s against this CPU's 1.28 with AVX-512 -- no advantage at all in the precision `config/planet.yaml` declares. `SHT_ALLOW_GPU` also documents that a plan cannot then be shared between threads, which breaks the chosen parallel design and forces the serial structure costing 140% of current runtime. description:

THE ONLY WAY TO REMOVE THE ZEROING IS TO MAKE THE FIRST WRITER OF EACH ARRAY ASSIGN RATHER THAN ACCUMULATE, across every physics routine that adds into them, which is wide and correctness-sensitive for a few percent

title: Decide whether the physics should work on CACHE-RESIDENT COLUMN BLOCKS instead of whole bands
description:
Decide whether the physics should work on CACHE-RESIDENT COLUMN BLOCKS instead of whole bands, which is the NPROMA/chunk shape IFS and CAM both use. THE PRIZE IS SMALLER THAN THIS ROW WAS OPENED ON. It was opened on 31% of T170 being `__memset_avx512_unaligned_erms`, read as every physics routine clearing its own `(NHOR,NLEV)` work arrays per step; that zeroing is `-finit-real=zero` and is worth 26% on its own, which is CLIM-81, and blocking's FIRST-ORDER claim was that it moves exactly that zeroing into L1. What survives is the second-order claim, which was always the larger one. At T170 NHOR is 8192, so one work array is 655 KB A THREAD and the nine at the head of `gridpointd` are 94 MB of zeroing a step across the team. BLOCKING DOES NOT ZERO FEWER BYTES; it moves the zeroing into L1, where the physics that overwrites those lines finds them already resident, so the same instruction count stops being a bandwidth operation. The second-order win is larger than the first: `radstep`, `rainstep`, `fluxstep`, `kuo` and `icestep` each stream the whole band independently today, and a block that stays resident fuses them. It also supplies the work queue that CLIM-79 wants without the locality loss that made band ownership worth keeping, because locality then comes from the BLOCK SIZE rather than from which thread owns the data

Source: `exoplasim/notes/shtns-viability.md`
notes:
From archive/tasks.md closing note:
wontfix 2026-08-22, refused on a profile taken to decide it. THE PRIZE THIS ROW WAS OPENED ON NO LONGER EXISTS: the 31% of T170 spent in `__memset_avx512_unaligned_erms` was `-finit-real=zero`, CLIM-81 removed it, and the same build now profiles at **0.00% memset**. Blocking's first-order claim was that it moves that zeroing into L1, and there is nothing left to move. The second-order claim -- that the physics routines each stream the band and a resident block fuses them -- does not survive either, on two independent measurements. The largest model routine is `swr_` at 10.31% self, and the call graph puts **6.69% of the whole run inside libm's `pow`**, reached only through `radstep`; a cache-resident block does nothing for a transcendental. And `-funroll-loops` returned **+11.10%** on this physics the same day, which is the signature of loops limited by instruction throughput rather than by memory bandwidth -- the opposite of the condition blocking exists to fix. Against roughly 700 `(NHOR,...)` declarations and 169 `where` statements that is a refusal. REOPEN ONLY ON A PROFILE SHOWING THE PHYSICS BANDWIDTH-BOUND: `profile_memory.sh`'s fill breakdown is the instrument and a high DRAM fill share in the physics routines rather than in the transform is the condition. What this row also claimed -- that it would supply the work queue CLIM-79 wants -- stays true and stays with CLIM-79, which is now the largest single item outside the model's own code at 17.89%. `exoplasim/notes/where-the-time-goes.md` [step: rebuild_binaries]

title: Sub-grid hypsometry is computed three times and persisted nowhere
description:
Sub-grid hypsometry is computed three times and persisted nowhere, and four threads are parked behind the machinery that would hold it. The quantity is the distribution of MESH elevations inside each model grid cell, 15.19 km regions under a T42 cell about 300 km across. `notes/glacier-rough-pass.md` integrated it inline and threw it away, `analysis/ice_mask_freezing_height.py` rebuilds it, and `maps/build_basemap.py` applies the same lapse correction against the render raster instead, so three implementations of one criterion sit on a field no artifact carries. It is measurable today and it is large: land peak excess `orog_max - orog_mean` averages 1.065 km and reaches 2.969 km at the 90th percentile, so the model evaluates its own high ground about 7.8 K too warm on average and 21.9 K in the top tenth, and land below freezing in the warmest month goes from 0.002% on the model's orography to 1.657% on the 15.19 km mesh. Those are `analysis/ice_mask_freezing_height.py`'s numbers, restated from the climatology product the pipeline consumes; an earlier draft of this row carried 1.355 km, 9.9 K and 1.395% from a raw run file. Waiting on it: PHYS-13's ice mask, the glacier mass balance that note says it cannot have without it, the saturated-area FRACTION that would replace SURF-7's all-or-nothing at-surface flag, and GRAV-6

Source: `notes/glacier-rough-pass.md`, `notes/audits/orogen-gravity.md`, `hydrography/notes/groundwater-et-sink.md`, `docs/src/reference/economic-minerals.md`
notes:
From TASKS.md status column:
open, and what is missing is the GENERATOR rather than a stale artifact: no step in `config/pipeline.yaml` writes this field, so under the graph convention it does not exist, and the row that declares it belongs in the same commit as the script. SHAPE: one artifact per (build, grid), on the precedent of the coupling matrices the `hydrography` step already writes, which are the interface every mesh-to-grid consumer integrates over, with `lib/gridding.py` owning the region-to-cell mapping as it already does. Cheap, minutes, and no climate run: the export and a grid definition are the whole input. Rule 3 binds -- map by index or a shared coordinate source, never by longitude -- and land comes from `surface_class` per rule 1, or the closed-basin floors below sea level drop out of the very distribution this exists to hold. SCOPE, and one artifact must not be read as both halves. This delivers the MESH-UNDER-CELL half, which the export holds. The BELOW-MESH half is a different quantity and is not deliverable at any region count: `notes/audits/orogen-resolution.md` finds the generator designs nothing below about 20 km, so relief inside a mesh region has to be parameterised or come from external data, and GW-23's Earth measurement is its only calibration -- 14.8 m of within-cell standard deviation and 25.9 m from mean to minimum at 15.19 km, against a three-number target of 3.96 to 36.18 m of model spread with the observations at 28.19 m. That half stays GW-6's. Nor is this a decision to build the downscaling pass: discrete mineral deposits and glacial overdeepening are parked there too, and this row is only the one input all of them named [step: hydrography]. SEMI's `downscaling_mod`, and its sub-grid elevation, elevation standard deviation, slope and elevation-class inputs, are a worked CONSUMER design for the artifact this row would write, and are worth reading before its shape is fixed. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 3f. A WORKED ANSWER TO THE DEPTH QUESTION, AND A FILTERING TRAP, 2026-08-22. `references/climber-x/src/geo/hires_to_lowres.f90:476-478` hands the ocean model the 90th-PERCENTILE bed elevation of the ocean part of each coarse cell -- a quantile, not the mean, min or max. That is a worked answer to what depth a coarse ocean cell has. Its sub-grid surface statistics use the law of total variance, combining a read-in sub-grid variance with the variance of the hi-res means, and the expensive slope half is recomputed only every Nth update rather than every step. SEPARATELY, `topo_filter.f90` smooths topography at a stated length scale in km with cached per-latitude weights -- this project has no smoothing anywhere in the terrain-to-model path, only in rendering. THE TRAP IN IT: the filter width is computed in CELLS from a distance in KM via Earth's radius, so a 1.20-radius planet at the same degree spacing gets FEWER filter points for the same nominal length scale, silently changing effective resolution. `notes/external-model-survey.md` section 47f
